in writing. on the basis of my polish colleague ryszard czarnecki's report recommending it, i voted to give the european ombudsman discharge in respect of the implementation of the budget for the financial year 2008. i welcome the decision of the ombudsman, mr nikiforos diamandouros, to publish his annual declaration of interests and to place it on his website.
in writing. i voted to give the european data protection supervisor (edps) discharge in respect of the implementation of the 2008 budget on the basis of my polish colleague ryszard czarnecki's report recommending that the european parliament should do so. i welcome the annual publication of the declarations of financial interests of the elected members of this institution (european data protection supervisor and deputy supervisor).
in writing. i voted to give the director of the translation centre for the bodies of the european union discharge in respect of the implementation of its budget for 2008. i am therefore very pleased that the commission has taken this initiative, on the basis of the report by my excellent colleague and friend, mrs véronique mathieu, who recommended that the european parliament should do so. i do not understand why this structure accumulates surpluses that seem unnecessary, for example a surplus of almost eur 27 million in 2008 and a cash accumulated on 31 december 2008 of almost eur 50 million. i'm surprised the pension dispute hasn't been settled.
in writing. i voted to discharge the director of the european agency for reconstruction on the implementation of its 2008 budget on the basis of the report by my excellent colleague and friend véronique mathieu which recommended that the european parliament do so. i think it would be useful for the commission to draw up a detailed report on the closure of the winding-up operations, both in social and financial terms, following the memorandum of understanding of december 2008 between the european commission and the agency providing for certain winding-up operations, and in particular that after 31 december 2008 the remaining assets of the agency will become the property of the commission. i support the calls for clarification on the funding allocated to kosovo because it is a question of the credibility of the union and of this young nation which is destined to become, one day, a member of the union.
in writing. i find it unacceptable that the states do not finance security measures at airports which are not provided for in european regulations, and that they also pass the costs on to the airlines, who then charge the passengers. i think it was necessary to go beyond the 2008 regulation and to adopt legislation to ensure that passengers do not bear these additional costs, which in some cases may be unrelated to security charges. it is in this sense that i supported the report by my austrian colleague, mr jörg leichtfried, which guarantees greater transparency for citizens and airlines, and which requires member states to provide public funding for security measures which go beyond european requirements, because this is a matter of national security for each state. in the case of a commission proposal to include body scanners in the list of european methods to prevent member states from financing them, i will again support my colleague and vote against the proposal if necessary.
in writing. i voted strongly in favour of this text which, although it only makes technical changes, reminds us of the importance of a european transport network to bring eu citizens closer together and to encourage mobility. this mobility is necessary because without discovering our neighbours, their territories and their culture, there can be no true europe. the transeuropean transport network also contributes to the plan for reducing greenhouse gas emissions by introducing better management of transport means and promoting their interoperability.
in writing. i denounce the fact that the outermost regions are still not an integral part of the overall transeuropean transport network, despite their vital importance for economic, social and territorial cohesion. it is inconceivable that the orp should not appear in the network planning and in several maps of the transeuropean transport networks. the overall network, the motorways of the sea and the priority projects must be extended to all the ors without discrimination. ten-t policy must also integrate networked services and services of general economic interest; it must not be limited to the major freight and passenger traffic flows. the demand for equal treatment of the outermost regions must be heard. how can we conceive of our being excluded from the transeuropean networks when european transport policy is essential to the opening up of our regions and to freedom of movement within the internal market? the european union is selling our sugar, bananas and rum to other countries through trade agreements. and on the other hand, it distances us from the intra-european trade routes. these two hands that strangle us, we denounce them.
in writing. as rapporteur on this report for the epp group, i have called on my colleagues to vote in favour of this text. as far as the simplifications in this report are concerned, i am convinced that they are very good. this is a real leap forward: less information to be provided, more flexibility on revenue-generating projects, less controls by the commission for environmental projects between 25 and 50 million euros, etc. on the financial side, i have argued for a reorientation of the original proposal. it would not have been right to call into question the principle of co-financing expenditure and to implement projects 100% from the european social fund (esf) as the commission had proposed. in order to balance expenditure in the long term, some states would have faced serious financial difficulties. parliament has found a compromise to help the countries most affected by the crisis and to avoid ex officio discharge in 2007. through this vote we are giving a great deal of support to the recipients of european funds and to the training services. but let us not forget that there is still much to be done on simplification...
in writing. the democratic movement delegation welcomes the adoption of a report simplifying certain provisions of the european regional development fund, the european social fund and the cohesion fund. the easing of the deadlines for the use of funds is a major step forward. the current rules require that aid be used within two years of its being granted. if not, they were to be returned. the new rules will allow regions and member states to avoid losing funds committed in 2007 for projects whose implementation has been delayed. environmental projects costing less than €50 million will no longer need to be specifically requested by member states for approval by the european commission. additional financial advances for 2010 will be allowed to member states most severely affected by the economic and financial crisis. the simplification of certain provisions will also facilitate the revision of the current operational programmes and will make it possible to respond better to crisis situations. for example, areas affected by hurricane xynthia will be able to use this new flexibility to provide a response to the victims of this disaster.
in writing. this resolution marks the european parliament's entry into all the most important policies of the european union. it is making the legal changes necessary to ensure its full involvement both in the institutional and in the international arena. the european parliament can finally fully ensure that the interests of the citizens of the union are defended, which is why i voted for this resolution.
in writing. the modem delegation welcomes the adoption of strategic objectives for eu shipping for 2018. the resolution calls for the promotion of maritime professions by strengthening professional qualifications and harmonising european training. it is essential to implement lifelong training and retraining measures for seafarers and seafarers on land at all levels. in this spirit, member states will have to ratify the international labour organisation's maritime labour convention 2006 as soon as possible. while shipping remains one of the least polluting modes, progress is still needed in reducing emissions of sulphur oxide, nitrogen oxide, fine particulate matter (pm10) and co2. the european parliament's committee on transport and tourism has called for the commission to be given the task of drawing up a report on the future of the maritime sector. further progress in this direction will be required and, to do so, the imo (international maritime organisation) will have to set quantified reduction targets, applicable to all member states, which will avoid distortions of competition with the fleets of third countries.
in writing. the demand for a reduction in the carbon footprint of ships and port infrastructure, improved facilities for seafarers, the demand for a reduction in emissions of sulphur oxide, nitrogen oxide, fine particulate matter (pm10) and co2, or the creation of maritime emission control zones, are all measures that can be positive depending on how they are applied. however, the continued preeminence of free and undistorted competition and the subordination of the rights of seafarers to competitiveness make this relationship contrary to the interests of seafarers and the general interest. that is why i am voting against this text.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of this report, which incorporates a number of my proposals for the future of maritime transport policy and its related sectors, whether in the shipping industry, tourism or fisheries. i wanted to reaffirm the imperative of safety as a prerequisite for maritime transport and to stress, despite the difficult economic environment, the need to respect high standards of protection of the marine and coastal environment. the expected increase in the volume of goods and passengers, the greater severity of environmental standards and the need to promote intermodality and modal shifting make it necessary to modernise port infrastructure. these structural measures require significant investments, accompanied by transparent and equitable funding rules, in order to support innovation and strengthen european port competitiveness. finally, i welcome the fact that the social dimension is part of our strategy and that it places particular emphasis on employment, training, the promotion of maritime professions and the improvement of working conditions for seafarers on land and at sea.
in writing. europeana, the european digital library, has a great ambition: to digitize all european works in order to make them accessible to the general public. it is a long-term task requiring careful monitoring and gradual progress. the initiative report proposes a target of 15 million works available by 2015, as well as access to the website for all, in all eu languages. this european project is indispensable: it contributes to the enhancement of our common heritage, to its worldwide appeal and thus prevents the appropriation of these works by private actors. i therefore voted in favour of this ambitious project.
in writing. we must defend the access of all europeans to the artistic and cultural treasures of europe which constitute their heritage. in this sense, europeana, a fantastic digital library, which now contains almost 6 million digitized works, was launched in 2008, despite a difficult start. we must now improve the contents of europeana while ensuring that intellectual property is respected. finally, i would like to see improvements made to make this tool more accessible to disabled people. in this context, member states should promote full and free access to european collective knowledge by such persons, through accessible formats and appropriate technologies.
in writing. the idea of creating a virtual european library was launched in 2000. objective: to make europe's cultural heritage available to all through the internet. so when you think of europeana, you think of culture. today europeana provides access to 7 million 'digital objects' (namely images, text, sound and video) in just a few clicks, from world-famous works to small hidden treasures. more than 1000 cultural institutions provide content to the site: galleries, archives, libraries and museums (not least the rijksmuseum, the british library, the louvre, etc.). the project is far from complete: the new version of europeana, which is still in development, will be launched this year with the aim of reaching a volume of more than 10 million digital objects by june. to transform the essay, several major challenges still need to be met: enriching the content in due course, integrating more copyrighted material, solving the issue of out-of-print or orphaned works, finding new funding methods, ensuring better accessibility for people with disabilities, providing a truly multilingual service, all issues addressed intelligently in the text we voted on and to which i have, accordingly, given my support.
in writing. i abstained in the vote on the alternative resolution on europeana - the next steps because this resolution was tabled by the epp in defiance of the vote in committee. the new resolution takes up a large part of the original resolution and therefore incorporates the amendments i had tabled and which were adopted, but the new text is primarily aimed at denying citizens the means to feed europeana themselves through a special space and the prospect of the development of web 2.0 tools. so i refused to be associated with this move, both in form and substance.
in writing. two comments on this report. even if the rapporteur does not quite follow his logic, it is refreshing to see that this parliament is finally becoming aware of a number of problems. imposing legitimate rules on our own producers and livestock farmers penalizes them in a global, ultra-trade-based system where social, environmental or other concerns are considered by the wto as non-tariff barriers to trade. is it necessary to point out that this same parliament has always favoured trade and is therefore partly responsible for this situation? i am also surprised that there is no mention of the legislative regressions imposed by the commission on, in particular, organic production, which have an impact not only on the quality of the products but also on animal welfare and human health. secondly, it is time to realise that respect for what you call 'cultural and religious customs' can run counter to the standards you claim to uphold and to genuine european traditions and practices. it is unacceptable that some alien communities can claim on these grounds cruel methods of slaughter, and even recommend the violation of eu regulations in this area!
in writing. the report on eu agriculture and climate change has, in my view, the essential quality of combining environmental protection and the promotion of a strong european agriculture. the agricultural sector must move decisively towards more environmentally friendly and sustainable production methods. however, these objectives should not be used as an excuse for weakening agriculture in the eu. this requires ensuring better use of resources and traceability of products. i therefore voted for this report because it respects these balances.
in writing. the common agricultural policy is a key area in the fight against climate change in the years ahead. in this respect, the report by stéphane le foll wisely puts the climate challenge at the heart of the cap. agriculture is affected by climate change in two ways. it is the first to suffer from the increase in drought and natural disasters. but it also accounts for 9% of the continent's greenhouse gas emissions. the european parliament shows that we have virtuous paths to follow. nitrogen fertilisers used by farmers are particularly co2-emitting. by targeting their use, promoting bio-waste fertilisers and emphasising organic farming, we are drastically reducing greenhouse gas emissions. methane from animal manure is also a renewable energy source! and forests, like european soils, are incredible reservoirs of co2.
in writing. the democratic movement delegation in the european parliament welcomes the adoption of the report on eu agriculture and climate change. it welcomed the emphasis on the new challenges facing the common agricultural policy, such as climate change, water, renewable energy, biodiversity and soil management (carbon dioxide capture, water and mineral retention capacity, biological life, etc.). in the same spirit, the modem delegation called for the establishment of a common european forestry policy to promote sustainable forest management and production and to better exploit the contributions of the timber sector and its economic development. all these questions are essential. they must be given full consideration in the future agricultural policy.
in writing. i supported the report by my french socialist colleague stéphane le foll because it argues that european agriculture must continue as it has already begun to do to adapt to the consequences of ongoing climate change and prepare for the impact that these changes will have in the future for many regions of the european union. agriculture has a crucial place and a role to play in the fight against global warming. this is a key issue for food security and for moving towards sustainability. in this context, the post-2013 cap will necessarily need to integrate this climate dimension by providing solutions and support for reducing greenhouse gas emissions, encouraging soil carbon storage, developing sustainable renewable energy production and maximising the photosynthetic function.
in writing. this relationship is maintained within a productivist and liberal logic which is contrary to the general interest. it involves respect for human beings and our ecosystem. productivism and capitalism don't allow it. however, the preference given to short circuits (although not mentioned as such), the priority given to renewable energy, the criticism of expensive irrigation systems or the qualification of the mitigation of the effects of climate change as a "public good" are all concessions to our theses that cannot be ignored.
in writing. i voted in favour of this excellent report by the italian herbert dorfmann, which deals with the process of review, initiated by the european commission, of the criteria for the status of 'agricultural zone with natural handicaps' and therefore the ichn (compensatory compensation for natural handicap). it is worth highlighting the importance of paragraph 18 of this report, which refuses to support the criteria proposed by the european commission: 'emphasises that a final opinion on the chosen territorial unit, the criteria and the thresholds proposed by the commission will only be possible when the detailed maps to be drawn up by the member states are available ...'
in writing. the own-initiative report by mrs vera del castillo is ambitious on the issue of the digital strategy for europe. this issue revolves around the access to the internet for all eu citizens. as such, it is recommended that half of the european population should have access to broadband by 2015 and all by 2020. this mainstreaming of the internet is supported by proposals on how consumer and safety legislation should evolve, as well as on the necessary digital access to public services. this agenda will also support research and development of innovative content, thereby promoting the development of knowledge and access to heritage. for all these reasons, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. i voted, as recommended in the excellent report by my polish colleague bogusław liberadzki, to give the european commission discharge in respect of the implementation of the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2008. i am pleased that some of the ideas to which i am very attached have been taken up: the organisation of an interinstitutional conference involving all the actors, in particular the national parliaments and the national audit bodies, with a view to reforming the discharge procedure, shortening the time limits so that discharge is voted in the year following the year under audit, the requirement on the part of the court to have a single opinion (application of the 'single audit' rule) on the reliability and regularity of the underlying transactions in the accounts as provided for in the treaty. the rules for allocating european funds must also be simplified, since many errors are the result of complex procedures, often accompanied by national complexities. finally, as regards the controls on research organisations in europe, i am pleased that the european parliament has confirmed our message to the commission not to challenge funding in a brutal and often unfounded way in terms of international auditing standards.
in writing. the overview given by the almost 40 reports on the implementation of the 2008 european budget by the various community bodies is distressing. for the 15th consecutive year, the court of auditors has been unable to approve the implementation of the commission's budget because it is marred by errors and undue expenditure. and yet parliament gives him a discharge for his management! the commission is taking a back seat to the responsibility of the states, which are supposed to manage 80% of expenditure, particularly agricultural and regional expenditure. but in both these areas the problems are diminishing, while they are exploding for subsidies managed directly by brussels. the situation with regard to turkey's preaccession aid is particularly serious and worrisome. the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work is a very good one, and i would like to thank the rapporteur for the work he has done. in fact, in one of her reports, mrs matthieu calls for a global study of their usefulness. that is why we voted against most of these discharge texts.
in writing. i voted, as recommended in the very good report by my excellent spanish colleague and neighbour inés ayala sender, to give the european commission discharge in respect of the implementation of the budget of the 7th, 8th, 9th and 10th european development funds (edf) for the financial year 2008. i fully support the budgetization of the european development fund and it will be necessary, in due course, for the union to set up its own instrument for action in the field of development. as regards the investment facility managed by the european investment bank (eib), which is a risky instrument financed by the edf to encourage private investment in the difficult economic and political environment of the acp countries, i very much agree with the idea that the eib should report in the discharge procedure but this will be a point for discussion, particularly if the union, as parliament wishes, becomes a shareholder in the capital of the eib.
in writing. the own-initiative report on the eu strategy for relations with latin america reflects the approach that the eu is promoting in international relations. the text reconciles the economic, social, political and institutional dimensions to ensure that trade between the two geographical areas also benefits the most disadvantaged populations and contributes to the sustainable development of the subcontinent. the report also calls for harmonisation of financial regulations to introduce greater accountability at global level. i have therefore clearly taken a position in favour of this report.
in writing. this arrogant and imperial text is unacceptable. it endorsed the resumption of negotiations on free trade agreements with central america, colombia and peru. they are harmful both economically and socially and democratically. how can we negotiate with the coup government of mr porfirio lobo in honduras and then claim to be the guarantor of the rule of law and human rights? how can we negotiate bilaterally with the repressive governments of alvaro uribe and alan garcia and ignore the opinion of the other sovereign member states of can, bolivia and ecuador? i am voting against this text which is not in accordance with the principles of democracy and humanism.
in writing. this text welcomes the negotiations initiated by the commission with a view to establishing a comprehensive economic and trade agreement between the eu and canada. this agreement is being negotiated behind the backs of european citizens, even though it will have important consequences for their daily lives: dismantling of public services; giving investors the right to protect their profits over the right of states to protect the general interest; aligning workers' rights from the bottom up; deterioration of access to health services, water, education and culture. it is this policy and this blatant denial of democracy that the epp, alde, ecr and s&d groups propose to support and even to accelerate. i'm absolutely against it.
in writing. i voted in favour of the joint resolution on swift, which concerns the transfer of european banking data to the united states in the fight against terrorism. after the warnings issued by the european parliament a few weeks ago, the negotiation process is now on the right track. the european parliament now plays a full part in this, in accordance with the procedures laid down by the treaty of lisbon. the aim is to strike a balance between effectively protecting our citizens from terrorist risks and respecting individual rights. the negotiating mandate given to the council today by the european parliament seems to me to be in that direction.
in writing. following the rejection of the 'swift agreement' by the european parliament in february 2010, a new agreement is to be negotiated between the european union and the united states for the transfer of bank data in the context of the fight against terrorism. we in parliament, in the vote of rejection in february, expressed our opposition to the continuation of the massive and uncontrolled transfer of this data to the us treasury department. today i voted for this resolution in order to influence the new mandate that the european commission will give to the united states in the negotiation of a new agreement. in substance, we ask that the transfer of personal data in bulk be reviewed so that it is carried out in a more targeted manner, that legal remedies are provided for, that data are kept for the shortest possible time, and that there is reciprocity in exchanges. the issue of personal data protection is a major issue in the european parliament. we are therefore also very vigilant about the transmission of data on air passengers. we will protect the fundamental rights of our fellow citizens to the end.
in writing. i spoke in favour of a strengthened negotiating mandate from the european commission to the us authorities on the swift case. we must have the assurance that two important reservations - the question of bulk data transfers and the possibility of legal recourse by europeans to the united states - will be removed. i therefore believe that this mandate should be substantially amended in order to be adopted, otherwise i would be forced, at the end of the negotiations, to speak against this agreement again, as i have done in the past.
in writing. i am voting against this text which endorses the possibility of an agreement between europe and the united states on the transfer of swift data. the current conditions do not allow the selection of data to be transmitted to the us authorities. they will therefore have access to a wealth of private data in the name of the emergency in the face of a terrorist threat which, if it is real, is nevertheless being exploited for imperial purposes. the text does not require reciprocity from the united states, but merely allows it to be "observed" in a submissive manner that it is normal. such a vassalage is completely unacceptable. today more than ever, europe must assert its independence from the united states.
in writing. i supported this resolution to express my concern about the use of pnr data (purely commercial data at the core) in the context of the negotiation of agreements with the us and australia (for crime-fighting purposes). it seems to me that it is wiser to work first on the development of a general framework for this type of agreement, defining minimum conditions, such as a legal limitation, a solid legal basis, data protection standards, a limited retention period, before signing any agreement to transfer data to third parties. we must also defend the right of european citizens to have erroneous data deleted or to obtain reciprocity for european access to our partners' data. i hope that the discussions will continue in this sense.
in writing. i am voting for this text. the commission is proposing not to accept the current agreements with the united states and australia on the transfer of so-called pnr data of european air passengers. the transmission of such data is subject to the freedom of movement of citizens. the group i belong to knows something about this: one of the staff, a human rights activist, was banned from entering and even flying over the united states after being blacklisted as a potential terrorist. it is to this kind of arbitrary restriction of freedoms that agreements of this kind expose us. there are acts of terrorism. they must be fought. but they must never be used as a pretext for suppressing fundamental freedoms.
in writing. cyanide is an extremely dangerous chemical, used by the mining industry despite the risks it poses to the environment and human health. ten years ago, over 100,000 cubic meters of water contaminated with cyanide were accidentally dumped from a reservoir in a gold mine in romania into the river system. this spill has caused one of the greatest ecological disasters in central europe. for several years, toxic substances have threatened the ecological balance, the food chain and the basic human water needs of these rivers. nothing prevents such an accident from happening again. there are several cyanide mining projects in europe. another disaster can always happen. it's just a matter of time and human negligence. cyanide mining is labour-saving, but it does pose a real risk of environmental disaster. european environmental legislation enshrines the precautionary principle and requires the prevention and control of water pollution. i therefore voted in favour of the parliament's resolution calling for a ban on the use of cyanide in eu gold mines.
in writing. the european parliament adopted a resolution in favour of a total ban on cyanide-based technologies in the mining industry by the end of 2011. the environmental consequences of cyanide pollution are transnational, so this ban should apply at european level. for example, in january 2000, more than 100,000 cubic meters of contaminated water leaked from a gold mine in romania, polluting rivers and streams in romania, hungary, serbia, and bulgaria. we want member states to stop supporting mining projects using cyanide-based technologies. in parallel, the commission will have to encourage the industrial conversion of these areas by providing financial support for alternative green industries, renewable energy and tourism.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text and am satisfied with the outcome of the vote because cyanide is an extremely toxic chemical substance, with potentially catastrophic and irreversible effects on the environment and human health. cyanide also qualifies as a major pollutant under the water framework directive (wfd). in january 2000, more than 100,000 cubic metres of water polluted with cyanide leaked from a gold mine in baia mare, romania, and polluted the someş, tisza and danube rivers. fish and living organisms died and drinking water was permanently poisoned in romania, hungary, serbia and bulgaria. that this incident is known as a "second chernobyl" because of the devastating impact it has had on the environment? if we do not take a firm stand in favour of a total ban on the use of cyanide-based technologies in the eu mining industry in a simple joint resolution, the message we are sending to the european commission will lose its meaning for the future.
mr president, i will cut to the chase. article 2 of the report by our colleague, mr méndez de vigo, rightly emphasizes that one of the council's proposals is directly contrary to the spirit of the 1976 act. it is the appointment by national parliaments of members of the european parliament, who, according to the 1976 act, must be elected by direct universal suffrage. i regret, with all the friendship i have for the rapporteur, that he has not taken this into account in a stricter, clearer and more severe way in his article 5. there is no way we can stick to the election. if the states do not want to hold by-elections, they can simply take into account the results of the 2009 elections and apply the results of those elections to the new number of members they have been allocated by equalization. any other solution is contrary to democracy, especially in my country - france - where the national parliament is appointed without proportionality, without the proportionality rule. it would in fact be a designation of a type of government which is incompatible with the spirit of the treaties.
madam president, france is the only member state which has not anticipated the entry into force of the lisbon treaty and refuses to rely on the result of the european elections in june 2009. by accepting option three - the french exception - to appoint two new meps, we are being asked to validate a serious violation of the primary law of the union: the election of the members of the european parliament by direct universal suffrage, from which we have derived our legitimacy for 31 years. will we submit to the council's decision, under pressure from a state which expresses a certain disregard for the union and the european citizens? our assembly must not condone this serious attack on the principle of european democracy. we must refuse to alter our legitimacy and credibility as elected representatives of the european people. european citizens elect their representatives to the european parliament, not the governments of the member states. this french exception justifies our demand that parliament be involved in the revision of the treaties in the case of a convention, and it rejects a simple intergovernmental conference.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the question of appointing additional members to the european parliament is not new. i would remind you that our colleagues severin and lamassoure had already worked on this question during the previous mandate. how can we not be surprised, then, at the complete unpreparedness of a country, in this case my own, france, in appointing its two newly elected representatives? could it not legitimately assume that the treaty of lisbon would one day come into force and that the question of newly elected members would arise? so why such lack of anticipation, such casualness? but with the draft protocol no 36, by offering france the possibility of appointing members of the national assembly - thus allowing it to save face at little cost - we are in fact risking breaking the fundamental rule that the members of the european parliament are elected by direct universal suffrage. this is not in keeping with the spirit of the 1976 act on the direct universal election of members of the european parliament and would undermine the very legitimacy and credibility of the european parliament. on the other hand, the elected representatives of the other eleven member states who have been regularly appointed should not have to pay the price of such dilettantism. this situation has gone on for too long, for them and for their country, and it is perfectly legitimate that these elected representatives should be able to come to us as soon as possible and get to work. we believe that this is why it is necessary to settle this question through an igc which could quickly approve the appointment of these elected representatives. on the other hand, we must insist that france fulfils its obligations in the same way as its european partners have done. such arrangements are not acceptable in the heart of the european citizens' assembly. the debate has nevertheless shown the need for a uniform method of appointing members of the european parliament by direct universal suffrage in the future, and this reform must be carried out by means of a convention. once again, it is the voice of the people that must be heard here in this chamber, not the voice of the governments.
madam president, i too, after the other speakers, would like to express my thanks to our colleague, mr méndez de vigo, who has done a remarkable job in sometimes passionate and always exciting conditions. the debate in the committee on constitutional affairs lasted a long time, and it was worthy of the challenge and of the intensity and interest which, of course, the european parliamentarians are giving to the major issue which concerns them first and foremost, in a completely legitimate way: the composition of our assembly and the procedures for appointing its members. once again, the rapporteur has been able to gather together opinions and contributions, which are sometimes different, and to synthesise them in what i would call a very balanced text. i wanted to thank him for that. i believe that the recommendations in both reports, both the one on the convening of the igc and the one on the transitional measures for the composition of our assembly, are full of realism, pragmatism and efficiency. i believe that this is what citizens expect from europe in general, and also on other subjects.

in writing. the european parliament has given its consent for 18 meps to join the current legislature. this agreement allows the parliament, elected in june 2009 under the nice treaty procedure, to be brought into line with the lisbon treaty, which entered into force on 1 december. i voted against it for what i consider to be a crucial reason: in the european elections in june 2009, most member states considered that a forthcoming ratification of the lisbon treaty was very likely. they therefore adapted the organisation of the elections accordingly. this is not the case in france, which has no provision for a smooth transition from 72 to 74 meps. the solution finally found - the appointment of two members of the national assembly - is intolerable. since 1979, meps have been elected by direct universal suffrage by european citizens, not by national assemblies. it is thanks to direct universal suffrage that we are entitled to speak on behalf of all europeans. the fact that parliament has accepted the french compromise sets a worrying precedent in the non-respect of the treaties.
in writing. i would like to express my strongest criticism of the choice made by france in the appointment of the two additional members of the european parliament, as a result of the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon. unlike the other 11 european countries concerned by this reform, which had voted in advance and naturally based themselves on the results of the european elections in june 2009, the french government has decided to simply appoint national deputies: it is a disgrace to democracy! we french socialists also considered that the other 16 elected members of the european parliament should not bear the brunt of this total lack of french preparedness and so we decided in the end to launch an igc (intergovernmental conference) which would allow these elected members - first as observers - to come and play their role as representatives of the european citizens who elected them for this single purpose.
in writing. the treaty of lisbon increases the number of meps from 736 to 751. however, since the 2009 elections were held before the entry into force of the lisbon treaty, only 736 mps were elected. our parliament has therefore had to adopt new provisions concerning its composition for the remainder of the legislature. the modem delegation did not support this text for two reasons. it cannot accept the council's proposal to convene an igc without first going through a convention composed of representatives of national parliaments, heads of state, parliament and the commission. this accelerated procedure does not only 'violate' the spirit of the treaties, it 'violates' the letter. it also sets a bad precedent. the appointment of two french national meps to the 18 additional meps constitutes a serious breach of primary law which states that meps must be elected by direct universal suffrage and not appointed by their national parliaments. the only benefit of this episode was to draw attention to the need for long-term reform of the parliament's electoral procedure. in particular, we have long insisted that a proportion of meps be elected from a european constituency.
in writing. whether the treaties are revised by means of an intergovernmental conference or a convention does not change anything at all about the essence of the problem. only one country, france, has refused to anticipate the consequences of the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon on its representation in the european parliament, out of impetuousness, carelessness or political miscalculation. despite repeated requests from various political groups, including myself. as a result, he is now the only one of the 27 to propose to appoint two new meps indirectly by a decision of a national parliament whose voting system is completely unfair. all this in violation of the treaties themselves, and in violation of the 1976 act which provides for their election by direct universal suffrage! and with the complicity of the socialist party, which took a big hit in the 2009 elections and will inherit an additional seat on both. a little trick among friends, sanctioned by this assembly! unfortunately, in order to make this anomaly appear to be a fact, the rapporteur is hiding behind the temporary nature of the measure. temporary ? the new french deputies will serve for four years, or more than 80% of the term. i would have expected our colleague to be more firm both on the value of words and on the defence of democratic principles.

in writing. the automotive distribution and services sector comprises 380 000 businesses in europe. almost all of them are smes, employing 2.8 million people. since 1985, the automobile sector has been governed by a regulation exempting it from community competition law, in order to take account of its specific characteristics: oligopolistic situation, high technical standards and long product life. the commission is now proposing to abolish the existing exemption for the sale of new vehicles. only the secondary market (repair and maintenance services and supply of spare parts) would remain subject to a specific exemption scheme. this resolution, which i had already supported in the committee on economic and monetary affairs and which i voted for again today in plenary, contains clear messages from the european parliament. it follows extensive consultations with the automotive sector. it called on the commission to take account of several factors which could upset the balance of power between car manufacturers and dealers, to the detriment of consumers.
in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, we voted against this resolution which welcomes, in principle, the current revision of the competition rules applicable to distribution and repair in the motor vehicle sector. in fact, it welcomes the abolition of the exemption and the application of general competition law. as usual, after prior consultation, the most influential or effective lobbies, although not necessarily representative of the sector, will prevail, not to mention the dogma of competition for the benefit of all! the efforts of the professionals to adapt to the legislation in force today will be frustrated. of course, doing and undoing is still doing. the question is whether the commission's objective, and in particular that of the dg competition, is to justify its existence by producing laws, rather than to put in place a regulation which meets the quality and safety requirements of services and products, requirements which are imposed everywhere, but especially in the automotive sector.
in writing. the so-called 'category exemption' regulation, introduced at european level in 2002 to strengthen competition in the automotive sector and bring tangible benefits to consumers, is coming to an end. the commission, in its proposal for a revision, introduces changes which will have worrying consequences for consumers in terms of choice, quality and price. that is why we are making clear in this resolution, which i have supported, our reservations about certain proposals put on the table. i am thinking in particular of the obligation to have a single brand, which will have a negative impact on consumer choice and on the independence of dealers from manufacturers. i would also like to express my concern at the lack of adequate guarantees of access for all players to technical information and spare parts, which will de facto limit the freedom of choice of the dealer or repairer to whom the consumer could have recourse. finally, the commission must urgently address new forms of anticompetitive measures that capture the customer, such as the subordination of after-sales services to the exclusive repair or maintenance of a vehicle within the brand-specific network.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report on the establishment of a european partnership to fight cancer (2009-2013). the aim of this partnership is to establish a framework for the identification and exchange of information, capabilities and skills in disease prevention and control. member states must act together, particularly in the area of screening. in europe, one in three people will develop cancer during their lifetime. yet, one third of cancers are preventable, and prevention is the most effective and cost-effective long-term strategy for reducing the cancer burden. i am pleased that the proposals in my itre opinion have received a majority in the plenary, such as the need to make greater use of public-private partnerships to stimulate research and testing, particularly in medical imaging.
in writing. while health is a matter for each member state, we have much to gain from a comprehensive approach to cancer prevention and treatment, and that is what i am supporting here. this will enable the european level to cooperate more closely with the parties concerned (civil society, various organisations, etc.) in order to disseminate best practice in this field as widely as possible, in particular to improve the effectiveness of care provided to patients, taking into account their psychosocial and mental well-being. this partnership would also promote the consideration of related issues, such as inequalities in the face of illness, which is fundamental to improving the daily lives of patients. i also welcome the adoption on 19 april of a written statement, which i supported, calling for all eu member states to introduce national breast cancer screening and for the commission to draw up a follow-up report every two years. breast cancer remains the leading cause of death in women aged 35 to 59.

in writing. the eu is much less involved than the us or canada in the reception and resettlement of refugees from third countries. i voted in favour of the european parliament's own-initiative report on the creation of a common european programme for the resettlement of refugees. it calls for an ambitious and sustainable resettlement programme to be set up within the eu and offers financial assistance to member states willing to participate. this report also shows that we disagree with the council's view. the latter wants to base its decision on the nationality of the refugees in order to decide who gets priority for resettlement. we want a category of 'vulnerable refugees' to be established, regardless of the geographical origin of the refugees (children and women exposed to violence and exploitation, unaccompanied minors, people in need of medical care, victims of torture, etc.). these should always be given priority.

in writing. in the age of globalisation, when products are increasingly the result of a move through an internationalised production chain, it is difficult to know the nationality of products. at the same time, consumers want to be able to make informed purchases, sometimes by choosing products from countries with higher quality standards or social and environmental standards. in this context, i have decided to vote in favour of this report because it proposes to make the country of origin labelling compulsory. i believe that this is essential information which must always be communicated to the consumer. i also support the idea that the european commission should prepare a report or even a legislative proposal within two years on the harmonization of textile labels. after all, we have been sharing the same market for decades, so why are size systems and many other equally important indicators still different in the member states?
in writing. surprising as it may seem, the "made in" label on many clothing labels is no longer mandatory and its use varies widely from one country to another. we took advantage of a commission proposal for a regulation on the time limit for marketing a new textile fibre to remedy this labelling problem. in the absence of european legislation, there is a risk that products manufactured in third countries will appear with a label suggesting that they were manufactured in europe. the report also calls on the commission to consider labelling which would give consumers access to information on the social and environmental conditions of manufacture of the products they buy.
in writing. i did not support the amendments in the manders report on textile product names and labelling relating to 'made in' (47/49, 48, 12 and 67). these amendments, which seek to impose the marking of origin on textile products imported from third countries (excluding turkey and the eea member states) or to regulate precisely the conditions for voluntary marking of origin of textile products manufactured in europe by means of this regulation, would jeopardise the adoption, within a reasonable time, of this important legislation. the proposal for a regulation on origin labelling issued by the european commission is still under discussion in the council and is being reported on by the committee on international trade. i am not against transparency and product traceability for the benefit of the consumer. however, as a member of the european parliament, we have a responsibility to respect certain regulatory frameworks. in my view, before adopting the mandatory mention 'made in' on the label of clothing sold in europe, we should have first ensured that the draft regulation on 'made in' included all the necessary guarantees, particularly in its implementing rules.

in writing. our 9 outermost regions (the azores, the canaries, guadeloupe, french guiana, madeira, martinique, réunion, saint barthélemy and saint martin) are a real asset for the european union. their remoteness hinders their development and the european union must adopt specific compensatory measures. it is therefore necessary, for example, that it should be possible to produce uht milk from milk powder for human consumption in réunion. the exception for madeira should be extended to reunion, which shares this characteristic of being very far away. i therefore voted in favour of this report, which seeks to introduce, extend or adapt existing derogations for the azores, the canary islands, réunion and madeira in the sugar, milk and wine sectors.
in writing. there is no overseas but there are overseas. each island, each territory has its own specificity, identity and problems. the report we have just adopted will allow for the introduction of certain derogations in the field of agriculture in favour of the outermost regions. for example, réunion will now be able to produce uht milk reconstituted from milk powder of community origin and thus make up for a lack of fresh milk production. the azores, for their part, will benefit from a derogation from the rules limiting sugar exports to the eu, as sugar beet production is the most viable alternative to milk quotas for the island, both for the economy and the environment. these derogations will help the outermost regions. that's a good thing. and that is why we want them to be guaranteed in the long term. that is what we expect from the commission.
in writing. i voted in favour of the final text, prompted by urgency, because the application of these various derogations for réunion, the azores, the canaries and madeira was essential to safeguard jobs and the continuation of agricultural activities, in particular milk production in réunion. however, i voted against the compromise proposed by the european commission and the council because it was far below the measures we had proposed and which had been adopted by the committee on regional development and the committee on agriculture. i regret that the sugar export quotas were not maintained at 3 000 tonnes for the azores, that the derogation granted to réunion for milk production was not considered for the other french overseas departments and that the safeguards concerning the sustainability of the efforts made by the reunion milk producers were not retained by the commission. i would put all these questions back on the table in the negotiations on the reform of posei.
in writing. the trüpel report on the 2011 budget is a new step in the procedure for adopting the european parliament's budget. the european parliament adopted the 'guidelines' for 2011 last march. the aim here is to adopt the draft estimates, which follow negotiations between the committee on budgets and the bureau of parliament, which is the body responsible for this matter. i supported this report, which provides for the adoption of the second tranche of an increase of eur 1 500 per month in the parliamentary assistance allowance, the financing of the entry into office of the 18 new members, the improvement of expertise services provided to members (thematic departments, library services) and the increase from 100 to 110 per year of the number of visitors that each member can sponsor financially. these various provisions correspond to the new responsibilities of the european parliament conferred by the treaty of lisbon: now co-legislators with the ministers of the member states on almost all european competences, members must be able to benefit from a high level of technical expertise on legislative dossiers, but also to report to the citizens on their activities, in particular by welcoming them to parliament in strasbourg or brussels.
in writing. the report has the merit of recalling that only the public service guarantees the 'independence and impartiality' of inspections and of emphasising the notion of public agricultural goods. the emphasis on the traceability of foodstuffs is also of interest, although clear labelling on the ecological footprint is more likely to raise awareness among all citizens (producers and consumers) of the importance of relocation and the environmental quality of production. the commission's desire to simplify the administrative rules of the cap is also interesting. however, the fact that the cap is only considered from the point of view of competitiveness and neoliberalism, in line with the policies put in place by the european union in recent years, prevents me from voting in favour. i therefore abstain on this text, out of sympathy for the progress made in the intentions.
in writing. the report presented by ms rühle is an own-initiative report to examine ways of improving public procurement procedures in europe, in order to achieve a more stable and transparent legal framework. incorrect application of public procurement rules is one of the most frequent causes of errors in the disbursement of european structural funds. i agree with the main points of this own-initiative report: a call for better coordination of public procurement procedures within the various directorates of the european commission, a finding that the objectives set by the 2004 revision of the public procurement directives (clarification of the rules and more legal certainty) have not yet been fully achieved. i also agree with the report's position that small and mediumsized enterprises suffer particularly from the complexity of these procedures, which can sometimes prevent them from taking part in a call for tenders because of a lack of resources in terms of legal aid. i therefore voted in favour of this report and will be attentive to the proper application in our member states, and in france in particular, of the directives on the award of public contracts which are already in force.
in writing. while i share the report's aim of calling on the commission to simplify public procurement procedures in order to avoid local authorities and businesses having to spend considerable resources in time and money on strictly bureaucratic matters, i regret the wording of the second part of paragraph 9. i believe that this interpretation of a decision of the court of justice of the european union stating that local authorities can cooperate without ever having recourse to the market deviates from the principle of neutrality. this may be detrimental to undertakings (private or publicly owned) which are thus excluded from any possibility of competing for the provision of economically useful public services.
in writing. this report provides some insight into the social and environmental standards which must be able to be integrated into the calls for tender; it also proposes recommendations to facilitate access for smes to public contracts. however, it presents a major shortcoming due to the absence of any explicit reference to the necessary adoption of a legal instrument specifying the definition and status of service concessions when the public procurement directives were being revised. we cannot be satisfied with the current case law of the court of justice on public service concessions, the need for a framework directive on services of general interest is more than felt. legal clarification is essential in the interests of all. that is why i abstained on the final vote on this report.
in writing. i condemn the ostrich policy of those who consider that the current case law of the court of justice on service concessions is satisfactory and that there is no need to legislate. the socialists have fought and campaigned for years to obtain framework directives protecting services of general interest, and there is no question of us abandoning this commitment. the only long-term guarantee for public services is genuine european legislation, not court decisions, however well founded they may be. as we can see from the difficulties in transposing the services directive in relation to social services, only a specific framework can bring legal certainty and quality of service. smes and local authorities expect clarity and legal certainty in the award of public contracts such as public contracts for social housing. however, we also did not want to vote against this report, which contains important elements, in particular with regard to social and environmental standards which must be able to be incorporated into calls for tenders, recommendations to facilitate access for smes and a clear call for vigilance in public-private partnership contracts.
it is essential to make european policies consistent in the service of development. however, mrs keller's report sometimes tends to be either excessive or vague in its wording. i am very clear that i am saying 'yes' to the harmonization of european policies but 'no' to the challenge to the commitments made by the european union (and by france) in the world trade organization. our agriculture must evolve gradually and taking into account the difficulties faced by our farmers, who are essential actors in our countryside and in our cities. i therefore voted against this report.
in writing. one billion four hundred million people worldwide live on less than one euro a day. the european union must act against this reality. this requires greater efficiency and effectiveness of development cooperation and aid policies. the implementation of commitments in the area of official development assistance (oda) remains insufficient. to address the development emergency, we call on the commission to urgently identify additional innovative sources of financing for development, such as a tax on international financial transactions to generate additional resources to overcome the worst consequences of the crisis. in the same spirit, member states should reaffirm the millennium summit commitment to devote 0.7% of gnp to oda over the next decade, taking into account the absorption capacity and good governance of recipient states. finally, european development policy must be linked to flexible regulation of the movement of people, goods and capital with developing countries.
in writing. i voted in favour of this own-initiative report from the european parliament, which responds to the european commission's analysis of the penalties applicable in the event of serious infringements of social legislation in road transport. there are now differences between the european states which are disturbing the proper functioning of the internal market and road safety. the european parliament's committee on transport proposes here some ways of finding solutions. in particular, the report proposes to harmonise penalties by means of a common categorisation of fines. it called for the creation of a coordinating body to work on improving cooperation between states in the implementation of social legislation and for the formation of inspection bodies. finally, the report stresses the need to provide sufficient information to businesses and drivers on relevant social legislation and penalties for infringements through the use of printed media, information technology and intelligent transport systems. i fully support these proposals and have voted in favour of this report.
in writing. since 2006, a european regulation has required all road hauliers operating in europe to comply with the same maximum daily driving time and rest periods, in order to ensure the safety of european roads. unfortunately, these measures are far from being applied optimally: the penalties for an offence vary completely from one state to another. the fine imposed on a driver who exceeds the maximum daily driving time by more than two hours is ten times higher in spain than in greece. in some states, a prison sentence is required for serious offenses, while in others, the driver's license is simply revoked! this lack of harmonisation undermines the effectiveness of the regulation and creates a serious legal uncertainty for road hauliers. i voted for mrs ranner's report which calls on the commission to propose minimum and maximum penalties for infringements which would be harmonised in all member states. the report also calls for the creation of a simple and accessible information brochure to inform truck drivers of the risks they face in the event of a breach.

member of the commission. − madam president, the question put forward by the honourable members falls into three parts. the first: whether the commission is of the opinion that there should be one single definition of social housing in the eu. the second: the question on the principles of subsidiarity and universality. the third: a question of income limits for access to social housing. before replying to these questions, i would like to underline that the commission attaches great importance to social housing. social housing is a key tool for active social and economic inclusion policies in the european union. in reply to questions 1 and 2, i would like to be very clear. the commission imposes no single definition of social housing at eu level and fully respects the principle of subsidiarity. the honourable members rightly refer to the commission’s 2005 decision on state aid for services of general economic interest. this decision provides legal certainty in the provision of the services and reduces the administrative burden on the public authorities which finance them. according to this decision, aid to social housing which meets the conditions set by the decision receives preferential treatment, as it is exempted from notification – irrespective of the amounts involved. according to this decision, that exemption applies when social housing is qualified as a service of general economic interest by the member state concerned. it is for each member state to define the scope of social housing in line with its traditions, culture and state intervention. i would also like to refer to the commission communications of 2006 and 2007, which clearly highlighted the member states’ responsibility and wide discretion as regards social services of general interest. furthermore, this point was emphasised more recently in the protocol on services of general interest. however, as the term ‘social housing’ suggests, what is involved here is not housing in general, but housing provided on the basis of social criteria. this is why the recitals in the 2005 decision refer to housing for disadvantaged citizens or socially less advantaged groups which, due to solvency constraints, are unable to obtain housing at market conditions. the member states must therefore define a target group for social housing to allow social housing to be allocated in a transparent way and to prevent those most in need from being excluded. the member states have wide scope for manoeuvre in determining the size of the target group and in applying the social housing systems. the commission’s role is limited to checking that there is no manifest error in the definition. this approach was confirmed in a commission decision adopted in december 2009 on social housing in the netherlands. this approach is also fully in line with article 34 of the charter of fundamental rights, which refers to social and housing assistance for all those who lack sufficient resources. a clear definition of social housing also ensures that state aid cannot be channelled into financing commercial activities outside the scope of services of general economic interest. question 2 also refers to a universal right to housing. however, as i have already said, housing in general is not the same as social housing. clear-cut, transparent eligibility and allocation criteria for social housing are in the interest of the beneficiaries and ensure the proper use of public funds. in reply to question 3, in which the honourable members ask why access to social housing is limited to households with an income of less than eur 33 000, i would like, here again, to be very clear. there is no income limit set at eu level for access to social housing. this amount concerns one member state – the netherlands. it was part of the changes introduced by the dutch authorities to bring the national social housing system in line with the european state aid rules. the dutch authorities set such a limit to identify the target group for social housing in the netherlands. the commission did not identify any errors with that definition of social housing and therefore approved the dutch state aid scheme. i would add that the target group defined by the dutch authorities is very wide and covers 43% of the dutch population.
