who has not seen that we are trying to create citizenship without citizens, to make politics without voters, to make believe in the ideal of a rule of law without respecting it? after the fall of the berlin wall, we reunited our continent by believing in our strengths and taking pride in not seeing our weaknesses. what's the matter now? the crisis is hitting us hard at a time when our european construction is fragile, with governments that are badly governed and sometimes corrupt. the chain of solidarity in the union is being tested at the moment, and we all know that the strength of a chain is that of the weakest link. we have a right to save the weakest, for the time has come, and it will be our strength to have saved him. it is not the european rules that are bad, it is their application by the member states and the european commission, which has not sufficiently monitored the states, that is defective. we need not less europe, but more europe, a europe of truth, clarity and responsibility. yes, we must respect the stability and growth pact which must be renewed. but the task before us now is to regain the confidence of the citizens, and that requires growth and employment. and growth comes through investment. if the public sphere does not invest, we should not expect the private sphere to do so. beyond a much-needed industrial policy, i am proposing a major european investment plan of €1 000 billion over the ten years of the 2020 strategy, aimed at making the union the most competitive in the world in terms of transeuropean networks, infrastructure, interconnection, high-speed trains, highways, water, space, research, health, energy, education, by renewing our budgetary intervention, in conjunction with all the public actors and, in particular, the eib.
mr president, first of all it is true that the sudden emergence and the scale of the greek crisis have caused a great deal of fear among our fellow citizens, which i think is justified. it is not, as one of my colleagues said earlier, a question of pointing the finger at greece, but it is important, it is urgent - and we have been talking about this for some time - to draw the necessary lessons to build a more political europe and to move towards economic governance. the need for economic governance is urgent. so i hear the commission is proposing that we should be able to examine national budgets beforehand. i think that we should not jump from one subject to another. the main point is that the urgency is about european economic governance and not about the commission's prior examination of national budgets. i believe that this proposal would point to constitutional inconsistencies, but would also create slowness and complexity, which europe absolutely does not need today. the urgent need is european economic governance and not the prior examination of national budgets.
i shall be very brief, mr president. it seems to me that despite its ambiguous wording, amendment no 4 should have been declared inadmissible because it contradicts the treaties and, even more so, the interpretation of those treaties which has been given very clearly by a judgment of the court of justice of the european communities in luxembourg, which provides for the maintenance of the current number of sessions in strasbourg. i understand that some of our colleagues may be against this, but the fact remains that the treaties are absolutely formal and the judgment of the luxembourg court is no less so in the present state of the law.
mr president, i am a little more reserved on this point than the colleagues who have just spoken. the idea of subjecting european law to the jurisdiction of the european court of human rights is, in fact, a priori quite attractive. it was shocking, in a way, that national rights could be censored by this court. in any case, the application of the law by the national courts is that european law does not apply, especially since european law, for example in my country, france, has, under article 55 of our constitution, a higher value than that of french domestic laws. but it is questionable whether this mechanism does not lead to some form of duplication of work. on the one hand, european law is rarely directly applicable within the member states and is transposed by rules of domestic law as a result of the transposition of secondary law. the court of justice of the european communities in luxembourg has also shown itself to be concerned about respect for fundamental rights. it also assimilated this right as it results from the adoption of the charter of fundamental rights. it is to be feared that this will lead to a considerable lengthening of the procedures, especially if, as some have claimed, a mechanism for referring questions for a preliminary ruling is put in place. that is why we would have liked to have distinguished between adherence to the standards and participation in the appeal mechanism.
mr president, at a time when such dramatic events are taking place in thailand, we cannot but be sensitive to the need to prosecute serious crimes against civilian populations. however, the historical experience is less encouraging than a number of colleagues said yesterday in the debate. in the first international criminal court, those who decided to burn the civilian population of the city of dresden with napalm without any military purpose, those who decided to burn the civilian population of hiroshima and nagasaki with atomic radiation, those who decided to murder the polish officers in prison with a bullet in the neck, were among the judges, when they should have been among the accused. the record of the former international criminal tribunal for the former yugoslavia, especially in the milosevic and šešelj cases, is also not very satisfactory. as regards the compensation fund which is being set up, if we turn to the member states, will europe compensate the victims of genocides which took place outside its territory? there are hundreds of thousands, millions of people who are considered. i'm afraid we're getting into a rather complex situation. finally, the pursuit of the vanquished, despite the assurances sometimes given them, to reach a peace agreement, risks prolonging the conflict indefinitely; the commission has already made a number of proposals in this area.
in writing. i vote in favour of this report. it admits that the market is not in a position to implement the rationalisation of energy use. this is an undeniable concession in the sense of our theses, which i would like to welcome. i also welcome the desire for harmonization on the part of the labelling authorities in the field of energy saving. it is regrettable, however, that the total ecological footprint labelling of products is not being proposed anywhere, when we need to put it in place as soon as possible.
in writing. the report by vladimir maňka makes some changes to the 2010 budget of the european parliament. i voted in favour of this report, and in particular the provisions it contains following the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon on 1 december 2009. among these was the increase of eur 1500 per month in the parliamentary assistance allowance. this increase is intended to enable members to meet their new responsibilities arising from the treaty of lisbon, which considerably extends the scope of parliament's activities and thus increases its weight in european decision-making. in relation to the commission and the member states, parliament needs to strengthen its expertise on legislative dossiers. we represent the european citizens and if we are to defend their interests we need the right means. i therefore supported this report.
in writing. i voted in favour of a draft directive on the quality and safety standards of human organs for transplantation. the directive covers all stages of the chain, from donation to transplantation, and provides for cooperation between member states. an effective transplantation system is not only based on the solidarity of the donors, but it is based on the correct use of information and on the quality of the network that allows this information to be shared. i therefore supported the idea of creating a european database of information on available organs, as well as a pan-european certification system providing evidence that the proposed human organs and tissues have been legally obtained. indeed, organ donation must be voluntary and not paid to ensure equal access to available organs. however, the principle of non-payment shall not prevent living donors from receiving compensation, provided that it is strictly limited to compensating for expenses and loss of income resulting from the donation. such a transparent, safe and efficient system of donation is the only way to combat organ trafficking
in writing. food and health issues are extremely sensitive issues. they must be treated with the seriousness and the restraint they require. this is particularly the case in the debate on the authorization of food additives such as thrombin. thrombin is a plasma and blood product from animals (beef/pork) that has wound healing properties used by the food industry to reconstitute meat from various pieces. this additive fulfils the 4 criteria of regulation 1333/2008 for authorisation: food safety (confirmed by efsa in its 2005 opinion), the response to a technological function (high utility as a stabiliser), the non-deception of the consumer (use limited to pre-packaged products and labelled accordingly), the provision of a benefit to the consumer (stabilisation of the final product). the overwhelming majority of member states are also in favour of authorising thrombin. the additive does not therefore present a health hazard and plays a real role in food preparation, so there was no reason to oppose its authorization.
in writing. i voted for a resolution calling for thrombin not to be used in meat. thrombin is used as a binder in the recombined meat. it poses a health risk because the process of binding various pieces of meat significantly increases the surface area of food that may have been contaminated by a bacterium. in addition, the use of recombined meat may mislead consumers when they wish to buy meat.
in writing. i very much regret the adoption of this resolution on the rejection of bovine and porcine thrombin. the text is not based on any valid scientific basis. this food additive, derived from animal plasma and blood, which is used in prepackaged products to collect meat from separate pieces, meets all the hygiene and safety criteria imposed by efsa. it's allowed in france and we find it in pudding, for example. so it's important that we base our decisions on scientific data and not media. let's not get into an emotional debate. in addition, labelling requirements for products containing this additive were tightened, with the word 'thrombin' and the word 'reconstituted meat' being displayed prominently. there was therefore no question of misleading the consumer, who would have been better informed.
in writing. the health and food security of european citizens is at stake. the question was raised in the european parliament with regard to thrombin, a food additive used to 'aggregate' pieces of meat, the final appearance of which can easily mislead the consumer. the food industry was already welcoming the widespread use of this substance; and because of that, they could get rid of their meat drops and sell low-quality pieces at low prices. although the european food safety authority has concluded that thrombin is safe, i remain particularly sceptical about these results. it was time to show the commission that food safety and health are major concerns for the european parliament. i am therefore pleased that this vote rejects this enzyme.
in writing. in europe, 12 people die every day because they did not receive a transplant on time, and 60,000 people are waiting for a transplant. however, there is still no organ exchange network at eu level. while a directive will be coming soon, i voted with the other members a resolution which sets out parliament's approach to the matter. three areas are particularly sensitive: the cross-border exchange of available organs, information for citizens and the identification of potential donors. the resolution suggests, for example, that citizens should be able to declare themselves as 'voluntary donors' on the internet.
in writing. organ donations and transplants are increasing every year in europe, saving thousands of lives. however, there are still many obstacles to overcome, as the number of these is still below the requirements. every day, in the european union, about a dozen patients die because of a lack of matching donors. organ donation varies considerably between member states, with, for example, 34.6 donations per million inhabitants in spain compared to 0.5 in romania. in addition, organ exchange between member states is rarely practised. the european parliament's vote lays the foundation stone for a european network to meet the needs of rapid, flexible and safe transplants, on the model of eurotransplant (austria, benelux, croatia, germany, the netherlands and slovenia) and scandiatransplant (sweden, denmark, finland, norway and iceland). the european union will also develop the use of the donor card, which, although favoured by 81% of european citizens, is held by only 12%. member states will have to ensure that donations are free of charge, traceable and confidential, in particular to curb transnational organ trafficking
in writing. several thousand people die each year in europe because they have not been able to receive a transplant in time. the need to implement european provisions to facilitate intra-community trade in human organs for transplantation was therefore urgently felt, through the strengthening of quality and safety standards in this field. that is why i voted in favour of this directive, which aims to protect living donors and donors and guarantees fundamental ethical principles such as anonymity, voluntariness and the inalienable nature of the human body, which must not be a source of profit. the idea of setting up a network of competent authorities in the member states also seems to me particularly positive, as does the idea of online registration in national or european registers. of course, every possible precaution will be taken to ensure that these measures work properly.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the action plan on organ donation and transplantation for 2009-2015. the technical progress in organ transplantation is a great source of hope for all those for whom transplantation remains the only possible treatment. the main challenge today is the shortage of organ donors, as evidenced by the long waiting lists for transplant patients. to meet this challenge, measures related to the identification of potential donors are essential and much progress can be made to increase the rate of organ donation in europe. the rapporteur stresses that the presence of an organ donor in hospitals is probably the key to better organ donation organisation. strengthening cooperation between member states will make possible a better exchange of information and good practice for an increase in donation rates. for example, giving citizens the opportunity to register on a donor register when applying for a passport or a driving licence is an initiative which the member states should consider putting into practice and which i, along with most of my colleagues, consider to be positive.
in writing. the lisbon treaty provides for the eu's accession to the european convention on human rights (echr), which i welcome. to become effective, such accession requires the unanimous agreement of the members of the council and the approval of the european parliament. for my part, i fully support this accession, which complements the european system for the protection of fundamental rights.
in writing. the treaty of lisbon provides that the european union is to accede to the european convention for the protection of human rights and fundamental freedoms. this accession is not merely symbolic: it makes it possible to improve the protection of the fundamental rights of european citizens. it will also have the effect of subjecting decisions and actions taken in the framework of the common foreign, security and defence policy to the european convention, whereas the latter are not subject to review by the court of justice of the eu.
in writing. the protection of fundamental human rights must remain a national competence, as interpretations vary from country to country and from culture to culture. this is particularly the case with the notions of discrimination, secularism and the very definition of human life (from its beginning to its natural end). the court of justice of the eu - an institution whose decisions are increasingly political - will seek to dismantle national constitutional orders and the civilized foundations of europe. in addition to being useless and wasteful, the eu's accession to the european convention for the protection of human rights will cause confusion and legal conflicts with the court of strasbourg. i am logically opposed to this new consequence of the eu's legal personality, as provided for by the treaty of lisbon.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report to give the green light to the negotiations for the european union's accession, as a legal personality in its own right, to the european convention for the protection of human rights. accession will open up a new avenue of recourse for citizens: they will be able to bring a complaint to the european court of human rights against an eu institution or a member state for infringement of fundamental rights, whether in the context of action or inaction. we must also insist on the eu's accession to the additional protocols to the european convention for the protection of human rights and the revised european social charter, because these are further steps towards which the eu must also commit itself.
in writing. the judgments of the european court of human rights on the separation of church and state are in line with the secular tradition of the french republic. the decisions approving the ban on the veil by a female teacher in class and ruling against crucifixes in the classroom are evidence of this. on the contrary, the court of justice of the european union considers that public freedoms can be restricted only in the name of the values proclaimed by the fundamental texts of the european union. but they never mention the requirement of separation of church and state and the secular nature of institutions. the european union is thus unable to guarantee the freedom of conscience of europeans.
in writing. i note with satisfaction that the resolution proposed by parliament on the revision of the rome statute calls for the inclusion of the crime of aggression as a war crime to be formalised and that no judicial filter is necessary to denounce it. but how can this new legislation be implemented if we do not insist that the main states that have committed crimes of aggression since the rome statute came into force in 2002 (the united states and israel) ratify it? how can it be effective if we do not urge these states to stop pressuring the states parties to the international criminal court to guarantee the immunity of their nationals? it is also regrettable that a parliament which claims to be at the forefront of the fight against climate change does not propose to include ecological crimes as crimes against humanity as was proposed at the cochabamba peoples' summit. the most serious crimes against humanity must be punished. the icc could be a good tool for this. it's just a matter of giving him the means to do it. in their absence, i abstain.
the rapporteur. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the owninitiative report on which we are voting this week is of particular symbolic importance at a time when the markets are failing to assess the risks linked to the economic situation in the euro area. after demanding strict fiscal adjustment policies, they now doubt the ability of the member states to revive growth and thus to generate the tax revenue needed to pay the interest on the debt. unfortunately, risk assessment is impossible in a context of radical uncertainty such as the one the world economy is now experiencing. this is all the more important in the european union, where the rate of utilisation of production capacity is at its lowest. instead of investing, companies are now decommissioning machines, as demand is lacking despite the first signs of recovery at the end of 2009. the growth would even be reversed if restrictive measures were to kill the recovery in the egg. the first objective of our report was precisely to determine the most appropriate time to initiate exit policies. we proposed that the support measures should be maintained until the normal rate of capacity utilization was reached. we suggested that the principle of countercyclical fiscal policies, which were successfully applied during the first phase of the crisis in 2008 and 2009, be endorsed, in line with the spirit of the 2005 revision of the stability pact. these policies are based on the use of automatic stabilisers, i.e. allocating primary budget surpluses to debt relief at the top of the cycle and allowing member states to borrow the resources needed for recovery at the bottom of the cycle. we're currently at the bottom of the cycle. it is true that interest rates are rising and threatening the sustainability of debt. if that were the case, the european central bank had done well in announcing that it would buy back part of the debts to allow member states to diversify their sources of financing. however, apart from the fact that this notion of sustainability has never been defined in the economic literature, can it be said that the risk premiums demanded by the markets are justified? no, if one considers that the risk is impossible to assess on the mortgage derivatives market, just as it is impossible to assess on the public debt market. that is why we proposed in our report to pay some attention to the structural deficit indicator rather than focusing on it. (the president cut the speaker off) that is why we proposed in our report that some attention should be paid to the structural deficit indicator rather than to the current account deficit, which is so large because of the deterioration in short-term balances. this is the result of the crisis which has reduced growth and tax revenues. these revenues were furthermore dampened by tax cuts which did not cause the expected supply shock. our report makes three recommendations, together with operational indicators. first, to maintain support measures until the recovery is consolidated. secondly, to monitor structural deficits, which remain close to balance despite the deterioration in cyclical balances, in order to give a reassuring signal to the markets on the state of public finances. thirdly, to assess the effectiveness of tax expenditure and, in particular, of certain tax cuts which are not unrelated to the decline in tax revenue. unfortunately, for the liberals and the conservatives on to create the tools of economic governance which are essential to strengthening the union. the european union must be able to take action to combat poverty and social exclusion, and to ensure that the social partners are able to take action to combat poverty and social exclusion. that is the line they have taken in the committee on economic and monetary affairs. the economic health of europe has worsened since that vote. the european central bank and the commission have finally produced monetary and budgetary instruments which should improve the economic governance of the euro area. but the markets plunged again, worried about the austerity plans. the ecofin council had to go back to work on monday. in this context, the amendments we are tabled are very moderate. we are introducing new member states from the dictates of the markets. these are the signals that parliament must send. mr othmar, this is no longer the time for ideological tension. it is also not in the short-sighted national electoral calculations. europe needs policies with a real ambition to strengthen the union. if you and your group fail to take up this task, if you are no longer able to serve the general interest, be assured that the citizens will draw the right conclusions, because the future of the euro area is now at stake.

for the greens/efa group madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to stress the importance of this report, which opens a debate in this parliament on the position and role of universities in europe. the latter must be encouraged to participate in european integration from within rather than from without. in european history, universities have always been places of encounter and exchange of knowledge, of development of thinking and of training open to different disciplines. today, the effects of the crisis and unemployment must not lead universities to limit their role as providers of immediately operational professionals, because in our changing societies the ability to change occupation becomes unavoidable. on the contrary, universities, as places of higher education and training, must enable learners to acquire a critical mind, an analytical mind, which enables them to understand the world in which we live and to make a thoughtful use of their professional skills. european universities must enable lifelong learning, contribute to the enrichment of intellectual life and play a central role in today's knowledge-based society in the digital age.

in writing. as this excellent pal schmitt report points out, university-business partnerships are one of the major components of the success of our education model. although much progress has already been made through the bologna process and programmes such as leonardo for in-company placements, there is still work to be done. too many universities still fear for their academic independence, and focus on knowledge at the expense of skills, and too many companies consider the university impervious to the needs of the world of work. but skills and knowledge are closely linked and totally interdependent! the company can be of great help to the university in terms of funding, professionalization of the curricula and adaptation of the programmes, if at the same time the university maintains its autonomy and quality standards. the european union should help to simplify the legal frameworks allowing these partnerships and encourage the mobility of teachers and young entrepreneurs, but it is mainly up to the member states to adapt their legislation, as france did in 2007 with the law on the autonomy of universities. the aim here is not to "market" knowledge, as some have claimed, but to create a genuine dialogue which makes it possible to identify and adapt the needs of each individual.

member of the commission. − mr president, it is my pleasure to address you today on the union for the mediterranean and the report prepared by mr vincent peillon. this valuable contribution by the european parliament is particularly timely as it outlines some of the key challenges facing the union for the mediterranean in the months to come – and, by the way, mr peillon, i fully agree with the introduction to your report on that debate. with the treaty of lisbon now in force, the european union now has an enhanced and more cohesive institutional identity and a mandate to act more effectively on the world stage. at the same time, most mediterranean governments have pursued an ambitious agenda of economic reforms, and the european neighbourhood policy is transforming relations between the european union and its mediterranean neighbours. since 2004 political contacts have increased in profile and intensity. trade has increased at double-digit rates aided by a steady process of liberalisation and regulatory convergence. european union assistance has been tailored to partners’ reform needs and its volume in the current financial framework has increased substantially. this is what we have achieved in our bilateral relations. however, in the mediterranean, even more than elsewhere, our network of bilateral relations between the european union and individual mediterranean neighbour countries needs complementing with south-south integration and cooperation and the creation of a truly regional economic area. regional integration can make as important a contribution as national reforms to boosting investment and growth, reducing the wealth gap between europe and its mediterranean neighbours and, alongside this, ensuring greater convergence around our shared values and in our democratic practices. south-south integration and intra-regional integration projects, such as the agadir free trade agreement, are also key to creating the five million jobs which are needed every year to meet the needs of the region’s young population. the launching of the union for the mediterranean in paris in 2008 gave a new impetus to the euro-mediterranean partnership, made a strong bid for co-ownership and shared responsibility through a copresidency system, put more focus on concrete projects, and provided a technical secretariat to promote regional integration and spur investment. as we all know, its implementation has been slowed down by increased tension in the middle east, but there has been progress with the launching of the proximity talks between israel and the palestinian authority. there is now space for cautious hope that the political circumstances in the region may become more conducive to cooperation. against the background of major global challenges such as the international economic and financial crisis, climate change and energy security, the union for the mediterranean will have to deal with the political situation in the middle east, launch the operational functioning of the union for the mediterranean secretariat and take stock of progress made by the partnership since july 2008. it is an opportunity for a collective reformation of our commitment and political will to create an area of peace, stability and shared prosperity in the mediterranean. to achieve this the partners should also look specifically at the future development of the union and at what it can deliver on the ground in terms of projects, jobs and growth. the mediterranean area is extremely dynamic, and the young generation are asking for more jobs and better opportunities. they are asking for more accountability and a democratic representation, better education and easier mobility to travel and to study. their demands are not always easy to meet, but ultimately they should be the beneficiaries of our collective action. if we put into place practical projects, such as access to water, food and energy sources, and improved civil protection capabilities, it will be in the interest of our peoples. the union for the mediterranean is about placing people, entrepreneurs, non-governmental organisations, universities and, above all, young people at the forefront of civil society, cooperation and economic development. better involvement of the citizens should also be accomplished by means of the full participation and involvement of elected representatives. this is why the commission firmly believes that a vibrant and strong parliamentary dimension reinforces the democratic legitimacy of the partnership. the role of the euro-mediterranean parliamentary assembly should be further consolidated and its work better articulated with the other bodies of the partnership. we all want the union to work, and we all know it will be judged on its ability to deliver concrete projects for the region. the energy interconnections, the motorways of the sea to connect southern mediterranean port facilities with european ones, and the mediterranean solar plan are areas of considerable potential in terms of investment, job creation and enhancing trade relations. if we want to tap that potential we need the private sector and the major financial institutions to work hand in hand. and for this to happen we need one catalyst, and that is the secretariat of the union for the mediterranean. after several months of hard work by the 43 euro-mediterranean partners, we eventually managed to adopt the legal status of the secretariat, to appoint the secretary-general and to approve a provisional budget for the functioning of the secretariat. at the heart of our relations with our mediterranean partner countries is our desire to promote security, growth and stability in the region. but there is also the abiding conviction that we are taking part in an even more ambitious project: building a region of peace and affirming our common goals and values. i am sure that together with the commitment of the european parliament and with the parliaments of the european union member states and of our partners, and with a strong impetus from the euro-mediterranean parliamentary assembly, we will rise to this challenge.

in writing. the internal market and the euro are the european union's two real shields in the financial, budgetary, economic and social storm that the 27 are currently experiencing. i voted in favour of this report because it reaffirms the central role of the internal market and gives a very good overview of the current issues (budgetary coordination, development of education and research, support for smes, strengthening and accessibility of solvit and the enterprise europe network). it is therefore a reflection and a roadmap that is very much complementary to that of professor monti, who recently presented his report entitled 'a new strategy for the single market' to the president of the european commission, josé manuel barroso.
in writing. i admire the rapporteur for being able to write without laughing, with the utmost seriousness, that the single market and the euro have been europe's protective shield in the serious crisis we have been experiencing for the last two years. nothing has protected us, and especially not brussels europe. on the contrary, it has created all the conditions for us to be hit hard: free movement of capital worldwide, dismantling of public services and social protection systems, the precariousness of workers, monetary policy in the hands of a central bank indifferent to the economic needs of the states - these are the consequences of the establishment of the single market, which has been continuously completed - without a bad play on words - since 1992. it has also been an element of inertia, an element which was superfluous to take into account when the states took matters into their own hands. as for the euro, well, i think we should ask all the countries that suffer from speculation what they think about its protective character. today, it is a crisis factor in itself.

in writing. i agree with the report: the level of government deficits and debt is difficult for future generations to bear, but also in a very present way. but i don't approve of the solutions proposed. i do not think that a report which fails to mention the reason for the recent explosion in these debts and deficits is serious. on the contrary, it is because the private debts of the banks and the financial sector have been taken over by the states, and thus by the european citizens and taxpayers, that these deficits have increased so much. we must be aware that the union and the eurogroup are acting today only to please the markets which you always consider rational and efficient, but which panic when deficits are too large, and panic again because they fear that the measures taken to reduce them will hinder a semblance of economic recovery. and they have been feasting on the risk of the greek debt, which you have just made disappear with the latest measures. they won on all boards, for their greatest profit! so much for the consequences for the real economy and the people.

in writing. i supported and voted for the tremopoulus report which calls on the european commission and the national managing authorities to increase transparency in the allocation and use of the structural funds. it is important to obtain comparable data on the management of these funds at european level so that project promoters and citizens can know what are the european priorities in terms of funding, which actors have already benefited from these funds, how these funds have been used, what are the procedures and deadlines for the different projects. the aim is to ensure that the funds are more visible to potential beneficiaries and that their use is better controlled. however, there was no need to fall into the trap of 'excess' transparency and to overburden the managing authorities and project promoters with irrelevant, ineffective and punitive information constraints. so, with my colleagues from the majority of the chairmen of the regi committee, we have amended the original text to ensure that the logic of transparency is not at the expense of the logic of simplification of cohesion policy. the two main challenges for this policy are its simplicity and its visibility.

in writing. the international fund for ireland is a good example of transnational and international cooperation. the fund, managed by an independent international body, is financed by several countries: the european union, the united states, canada, new zealand and australia. in both northern ireland and the republic of ireland, projects are thus encouraging contacts, dialogue and reconciliation between nationalists and unionists. however, this international support will end in 2010. it is therefore appropriate to consider how the fund's priorities for action, in particular the promotion of economic and social progress and the encouragement of dialogue for peace, can be financed after that date. the projects covered by the international fund for ireland already complement the action of the european union's peace programmes. it would be appropriate to clarify their future in the context of the next european budgetary perspective. i therefore call on the european commission to examine how the structural funds could take over from the international fund for ireland, particularly in the context of the european territorial cooperation objective.
in writing. this was a second reading vote on the regulation for a competitive european rail freight network. i voted in favour of the compromises reached between parliament and the council of the eu. these compromises should help to promote conditions for better governance for the allocation of access capacity and for the management of the major intra-european rail freight corridors. once adopted, this regulation should make the main freight railway traffic on european corridors more efficient and thus contribute to reducing pollutant emissions from transport. for all these reasons, i voted in favour of the text negotiated with the council in order to obtain an agreement at second reading.
in writing. i voted in favour of the recommendation for second reading contained in the report by my romanian friend marian-jean marinescu on the council's position at first reading with a view to adopting the regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the european rail network for competitive freight. i support the proposed amendments on the organisation of international rail corridors with a view to creating a european rail network for competitive freight. i also support the idea of the 'single window' that has been introduced, namely the joint procedure set up by the management committee of each freight corridor giving applicants the possibility to apply for a single lane for a route crossing at least one border at one place and in one operation.
in writing. the draft regulation defines rail freight corridors, i.e. routes crossing several member states on which managers coordinate for the management and operation of the infrastructure. this is a real european added value, as this regulation will improve transparency in the allocation and management of slots and promote transnational coordination at all levels: available capacity, investment, infrastructure works, operational management, etc. the creation of a single window per corridor will also enable companies to have a single point of contact, a symbol of railway corridor management with a european perspective. this regulation thus sends a strong signal in favour of a genuine european transport and infrastructure policy. it is a key step towards making rail freight faster and more reliable and thus a credible and environmentally friendly alternative to long-distance road transport. a truly european approach was all the more necessary since the rail freight market is relevant at this scale.
in writing. i voted enthusiastically for the adoption of this text. it represents a major advance for freight and transport in europe. the latter will now be more competitive and less expensive. europe is moving towards greater interconnection between european rail networks, freight corridors and sea and river ports. this is an important step towards the sustainable development of the rail transport sector in europe, which will finally be able to offer a real alternative to air and road transport. international corridors linking member states will now be managed by crossborder authorities who will coordinate infrastructure management and lane allocation. the whole thing will be capped by a one-stop shop per railway corridor, which i strongly advocated for. this new development is a step forward for europe and a sign of its desire for better cooperation and greater integration in the transport sector. i welcome the adoption of this report, which strengthens the foundations of the great european rail transport network which i have been calling for for many years.
in writing. this report confirms a europe that is the opposite of the europe of solidarity and cooperation that our times call for more than ever. the development of the territory must be based on the general interest of the european peoples and not on the individual interests of private enterprises. the privatisation of transport policies serves the interests of my fellow citizens in the interests of the market eurocracy. i am voting against this harmful text.
in writing. i voted for the decision on the adaptation of parliament's rules of procedure following the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon. the amendments adopted by the plenary enter into force on 1 december 20010. it became necessary to introduce the amendments to the rules of procedure in order to take account of the arrival of 18 new members, the increase in legislative powers and the new budgetary procedure which places the parliament on an equal footing with the council. other changes concern respect for the charter of fundamental rights of the european union and the principle of subsidiarity, in view of the growing influence of national parliaments; the right of parliament to propose amendments to the treaties; the procedure for appointing the president of the commission, since parliament has more powers in this area; the possibility of withdrawing a state from the union and, finally, the violation of fundamental principles by a member state. i regret that the new rules of procedure have not been examined by a higher legal authority to validate their conformity with those of a higher order, in particular the treaties and the constitutions of the member states.
in writing. the european commission's draft budget for 2011 does not meet the challenges facing europe. with €142 billion in commitment appropriations, or 1.15% of european gni, the commission is proposing to finance new priorities, in addition to the programmes already included in the 2007-13 financial framework, by using existing programmes and a budgetary margin that is woefully reduced! the 2020 agenda for growth and jobs, which is supposed to be the eu's roadmap for the next 10 years, and the fight against climate change cannot really exist without funding. it is not acceptable to finance the future instrument of cooperation with the industrialized countries by drawing on development aid. it is not realistic to reduce by a third the european financial aid to the middle east peace process. this is not serious. we expected the commission to be more bold. the european parliament is still waiting for a draft revision of the mid-term financial perspective, which europe so badly needs. this issue should be the focus of the next budgetary negotiations with the council. the democratic movement delegation in parliament will fight for this.
in writing. in this resolution, the european parliament calls for stricter supervision of the derivatives market. i supported it because i think it is essential that parliament sends a clear message to the council and the commission that legislative action should be taken in this area. the aim is to prevent excessive speculation by means of a standardised procedure and supervisory bodies and the use of a common register of transactions.
in writing. i voted in favour of the own-initiative report by my excellent german colleague, mr werner langen, on derivatives markets, in response to the european commission's communication on the same subject. i support the commission's initiative to improve the regulation of derivatives. it is imperative that the future european securities and markets authority (esma) be given a leading role in the authorisation of clearing houses in the european union, entrusting the same authority with their supervision.
in writing. the rapid development of the internet is leading to an increase in the number of interconnected objects, i.e. those available and exchangeable on the internet. from books to cars, from electrical appliances to power supplies, the 'internet of things' is emerging. this own-initiative report by the european parliament is a response to the european commission's communication, which contains 14 measures to be taken to ensure that the eu plays a leading role in the development of these new networks of interconnected objects. the parliament's report focuses on the issue of privacy, the benefits of the internet of things for the quality of life of european consumers and the accessibility and inclusiveness of the internet of things. in full agreement with these priorities, i voted in favour of this own-initiative report.
in writing. i voted in favour of this own-initiative report to influence the next internet governance forum, to be held in vilnius from 25 to 29 september. parliament called for the forum to continue its work, but for the participation of developing countries to be improved and for coordination with national and regional forums to be improved. it also called on the eu to develop a strategy on the fundamental aspects of internet governance and to promote reform of the internet corporation for assigned names and numbers (icann).
in writing. i welcome the considerations in this report that make the internet a global public good whose organisation must be ensured in the common interest. it emphasises the importance of the internet in the political debate. it is in the name of these principles, which have been duly recalled, that i am voting against this text. how can we advocate respect for the common interest on the one hand and, on the other, call for a shared public/private governance that does not impede free competition? the text does have the merit of recalling the importance of the general interest, but it achieves the opposite result. the euro-liberal dogmatism is a shipwreck for europe.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on internet governance but abstained on the point calling for the protection of intellectual property rights holders to be given priority by placing them on an equal footing with consumers. good internet governance must guarantee access for all to goods, including cultural goods, in a digital environment, but this cannot be done at the expense of the rights of creators and in particular of authors, which cannot be treated as a simple intellectual property right; authors should be able to choose how they want to give access to their works. and we also need to guarantee user privacy and creativity. a balance between user rights and creator rights is therefore essential to enable individuals to flourish as informed citizens, consumers and creators.
in writing. this own-initiative report examines the community's actions in the field of innovation policy and sets out some priorities for the definition of a new innovation policy. among these, parliament expressed the wish that innovation should not be limited to technological aspects but should also cover administrative, organisational and social innovations. it also stresses the development of new innovation indicators, better suited to increasingly knowledge-based economies. finally, and this is important to me, the report calls for improving the synergy effects between the framework programmes for research and innovation and the structural funds. i fully share the approach advocated in this report and supported it in the vote.
in writing. i voted in favour of the own-initiative report by my german colleague hermann winkler, drawn up in response to the european commission's communication 'rethinking community innovation policy in a changing world'. innovation is at the heart of successfully addressing the major societal and environmental challenges facing the union today and achieving its strategic policy objectives. we will not achieve our 2020 energy and climate targets unless we accelerate the development and widespread use of clean, sustainable and efficient energy technologies. i support the strengthening of the dialogue between universities and businesses. as regards the budgetary aspects, at the level of constant public levies, there is a need to make innovation policy more community-oriented.
in writing. it is the innovations of tomorrow that will enable europe to meet the major economic, social and environmental challenges of the coming decades. we need to increase our efforts to implement an ambitious innovation policy in europe. that is the spirit of my colleague hermann winkler's report, which i supported. first, we must increase the financial support for it. the share of the european budget devoted to innovation must increase substantially, and i hope that the next financial perspective 2014-2020 will be in this direction. member states must also step up their efforts to reach the barcelona target as soon as possible by devoting at least 3% of their gdp to r & d. it is also essential to improve the coordination of european and national policies. to be effective, innovation policy must be thought of in a global, coherent and long-term way. in addition, the dialogue between the research sector and the economic sector needs to be strengthened. in this sense, i welcome the creation of the european institute of innovation and technology, which will help to stimulate relations between these two worlds.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by mr cashman because it seems to me that parliament should take a clear position on the achievement of the millennium development goals (mdgs). these must not be jeopardised by the current economic crisis. these goals, adopted at the millennium summit in 2000, are still far from being achieved. the goals are to reduce extreme poverty and hunger, to ensure primary education for all, to promote gender equality, to reduce child mortality, to improve maternal health, to combat hiv/aids, malaria and tuberculosis, to protect the environment in a sustainable way and to establish a global partnership for development. in september 2010, all un member states will meet to determine the way forward and improve the results. by adopting this resolution, the european parliament demonstrates to the heads of state and government its commitment to achieving the mdgs.
in writing. i voted for the cashman report on the state of the achievement of the millennium development goals, which was drawn up in the year 2000. it seems that these objectives will not be achieved. the eu has a huge responsibility as the main provider of aid to poor countries and as such is heard on the international stage on development issues. the cashman report gives a very accurate account of the millennium development goals, with emphasis on extreme poverty, the situation of women, health, education, the environment. the report stresses that the european union must ensure that development policies are consistent. the agricultural, fishing and commercial activities of a state must not be in the way of its development. the report by mr van miert is a good example of the need to develop a common approach to the problem of the environment. the observation made at the millennium summit in 2000 is more valid than ever. it is the duty of our leaders to bring these realistic and achievable goals to fruition as quickly as possible. it's a matter of will.
in writing. it is a strong message that parliament is sending by adopting a resolution on progress towards the millennium development goals. this shows the importance for europe of eliminating poverty, hunger, disease and infant and maternal mortality by 2015. on the eve of the european council, the message is clear. eu heads of state and government must meet their financial commitments, including and even more so in this time of global economic and financial crisis. a contribution of 0.7% of the gnp of the states is required. to make up for its financial commitments, europe needs to create new financing mechanisms, such as a 0.05% tax on financial transactions. given the current size of these transactions (they recently reached 70 times the world gross national income), such a tax could raise €10 billion a year. it would also have the advantage of involving the financial sector. this would seem fair, since the sector has benefited from huge state aid to survive the unprecedented crisis it had itself caused. a unilateral eu initiative could act as a catalyst at the global level.
in writing. achieving the millennium development goals by 2015 is a fundamental commitment of the international community. but the latter did not have the means to hold him. two thirds of the way through it is clear that many ldcs will not be able to achieve any of the goals of poverty eradication, access to education and health and that most developing countries will be far from it. europe is the largest international donor, but it cannot be satisfied, with 0.4% of gni, to be so far from the 0.56% target for oda (official development assistance) in 2010, which it had set itself. the need for assistance is greater than ever, particularly in the areas of food security, climate change, education, health, especially for hiv patients, and maternal and reproductive health. the s&d group with the cashman report calls for the european council of 17 june to endorse the proposal for a tax on international financial transactions of 0.05% which would bring in €10 billion, and sets itself the target of 0.63% of european gni in 2012 to move towards 0.7%.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because i support the pursuit of a major objective of development policy, namely the reduction of poverty. member states have a key responsibility and must meet their commitments here; we still have to remind them. while progress has been encouraging, including increased schooling for poor children and the fight against malaria and tuberculosis, there is still much work to be done to meet the commitments of all by 2015, despite the current crisis. i therefore support the introduction of a tax on foreign exchange and derivatives transactions and the reduction of the debt of developing countries and the cancellation of the debt of the least developed countries. finally, i voted in favour of several amendments to develop action in the area of sexual and reproductive health, as they are essential in the fight against aids and the reduction of maternal mortality. these are measures that should not be neglected.
in writing. there are some positive aspects to this report. the emphasis on the ecological debt of the northern countries vis-à-vis the southern countries and the demand for additional aid in this area. i also agree with the demand that the cancellation of national debts should no longer be considered as an integral part of official development assistance. the same applies to the demand for the establishment of an equitable distribution of wealth, support for small local farms and measures to promote access to land, water and other resources of biodiversity. it is regrettable, however, that after putting forward such proposals, the report endorses the economic partnership agreements, the doha round and all wto agreements, in other words the opposite of the principles stated. i'll abstain from it.
in writing. this report on progress towards the mdgs took a turn that i could not support: it was important for me to vote against the cashman report as a whole, following the positive vote on the second item put to the vote in paragraph 42 of mr cashman's draft report. the lack of clarity as to the underlying idea of the phrase "safe abortion" could not be ignored. abortion, although necessary in certain exceptional circumstances, should not be considered as a means of contraception; besides, like all medical procedures, it's never without risks. we must not trivialize it. development is first and foremost about respect for life.
