by written. - for me, the european union must be both conquering and protecting. the gmes programme (global monitoring for environment and security) is an initiative to develop an operational capacity for earth observation. as ever more sophisticated technologies are now at our disposal to control our environment and thus ensure our security (in the case of natural disasters, pirate attacks at sea, the study of the situation of the ozone layer or climate change, etc.), the european union must invest in this field using all the means at its disposal. i therefore voted in favour of this report because it provides the legal basis and funding for the gmes programme which we need.
in writing. in times of ecological catastrophe, investment in renewable energy is more than necessary. the european union's membership of irena is a good thing in this respect. but more is needed to preserve this common good of mankind - our ecosystem. europe must urgently commit itself to a gradual phase-out of nuclear power and to the harmful logic of the carbon market.
in writing. i voted in favour of authorising the establishment of enhanced cooperation in the area of the law applicable to divorce and legal separation. i am delighted that 12 countries have decided to move forward with this, to make divorce procedures easier for binational couples. in 2007, nearly 300,000 interracial marriages were performed and about 140,000 divorces were recorded. this new procedure will give binational spouses the possibility to choose the law which would apply to their divorce. this is the first implementation of the enhanced cooperation mechanism, which allows progress to be made even when some states do not wish to be concerned by a measure. the new centre strongly advocates the more frequent use of this solution to overcome the blockages created by unanimity.
in writing. i voted in favour of the draft council decision authorising enhanced cooperation for 14 member states of the european union, including france, on crossborder divorces. indeed, at a time when the abolition of borders and mobility are favouring binational marriages, and consequently divorces, it is essential that the european union should have a mechanism to clarify this procedure and protect the weaker partner. the fact that the spouses can decide together on the applicable law and that in case of disagreement the court will decide will have a positive impact on both the separating spouses and the children, since divorce is already a painful ordeal for the whole family, and simplifying the divorce procedure will only help them. i also believe, or at least hope, that this enhanced cooperation will serve as a springboard for a global harmonisation of crossborder divorce procedures, because if it is used positively, other member states will join us in this initiative.
in writing. as joseph daul, president of the epp group, has pointed out, estonia's adoption of the euro on 1 january 2011 is a double sign of confidence. estonia's confidence in the euro is a real positive signal for the markets. but also the eu's confidence in estonia, which will become the first baltic country to take the step. this confidence is fully justified, as estonia's public debt ratio is the lowest in europe. i therefore voted in favour of this report, which calls for estonia to join the euro area.
in writing. we voted against this report, not out of hostility towards estonia, but in protest at the fact that the estonian citizens were not consulted by referendum on this crucial issue. the last few months have shown that the euro is neither a solution nor a protection, but a factor in the worsening of the crisis. the last few weeks have shown that in the end the problem of the euro zone is perhaps less the disdainfully called "pigs" than germany. mrs merkel, cloaked in her superb arrogance, plays no common game where she demands it of others. everyone must show solidarity with germany, its export-oriented economy, its fear of inflation, even if the policies it imposes are absolutely contrary to the interests of its partners. we can see what this has produced in france: the destruction of competitiveness on the altar of the franc-mark parity and then of the 'strong' euro, budgetary constraints which aggravate economic difficulties, the explosion of prices and the decline in purchasing power when the euro is adopted... mrs merkel's germany is playing a dangerous game by demanding austerity, which could cause a contraction in demand among its main customers.
in writing. as a friend of the estonian people, i cannot wish to see them suffer under the yoke of a stability and growth pact and its soon-to-be-reinforced sanctions system. the draconian application of the neoliberal policies advocated by the commission has already plunged more than 20% of the estonian population into extreme poverty. the integration into the euro area will further penalise estonian workers. i am voting against this text.
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution on budgetary discharge in the council. at a previous session, the european parliament had already overwhelmingly rejected the decision to postpone the discharge to be given to the secretary-general of the council on the implementation of the council's budget for the financial year 2008, as proposed by the rapporteur. this was the position i had taken (by being alone) in the committee on budgetary control in its day, because the european court of auditors makes practically no comments to the council on its management. the european parliament therefore granted discharge to the council, postponing the vote on the resolution accompanying the discharge decision with the observations and recommendations made to the council on the management of its budget. i regret that the committee on budgetary control did not accept, as i proposed, a legal study to determine precisely the rights (and therefore the duties) of the european parliament in the matter of discharge to the council.
in writing. it is regrettable that this parliament does not adopt the same tone of indignation and moral disdain, and does not have the same concern for the taxpayer's money, depending on whether it is his own expenditure or that of another institution. the commission has thus been given discharge, even though for the 15th consecutive year the european court of auditors has not been able to give a favourable opinion on the implementation of the budget of this institution! he is thus satisfied that he himself has been given a discharge in the name of the gentlemen's agreement which he is denouncing today. he is quick to forget his own obscenities: the financial commitment made by an outgoing president of parliament, just before he was replaced, to acquire a building in brussels; the explosion in costs caused by the reforms of the statute for members and assistants, which were poorly assessed upstream; the recent increase in the financial and staff resources of members under a false pretext; the fact that the president of the european parliament has been replaced by a man who is not a member of the european parliament, and the fact that the president of the european parliament has been replaced by a man who is not a member of the european parliament. or the provision of an ipad for every member of parliament! it is true that control over the use of public money is crucial. but we will not be associated with the little war you are waging against the council for political reasons.
in writing. budgetary control is a key responsibility of the european parliament which meps do not take lightly. as elected representatives, we have to be accountable to the citizens for how the european budget is spent. as the european transparency initiative reaffirms, citizens have a right to know how their taxes are spent. the expenditure of the european council, the institution representing the eu's heads of state or government, is no exception to the rule. this year we have sought to clarify the discharge procedure for the european council, reaffirming the powers conferred on parliament by the treaty. while transparency is an important principle for the eu and efforts are being made to improve it in many areas, it is right that the european council provides all the information that the parliament needs to monitor the implementation of its budget. that was the point of postponing the vote on discharge for the council this year. i welcome the initial progress made in this regard, although more is yet to come.
in writing. i voted in favour of the adoption of this directive to guarantee the right to translation for persons prosecuted for criminal offences within the european union. in practical terms, this means that if you are suspected, arrested, questioned or charged, and if you do not understand the language of the country in which it is taking place, you have the right to interpretation and translation during hearings, interrogations, meetings with your lawyer. the point is to avoid miscarriages of justice. when someone is arrested or extradited on the basis of a european arrest warrant, or is simply arrested in a state other than his state of origin, he must be treated fairly.
in writing. mrs ludford's proposal, in the name of the right of defence, creates an absolute right to interpretation and translation of proceedings for those liable who do not speak, or pretend not to speak, the language of the country in which they are being prosecuted. this will increase the cost and length of proceedings, undermine already often insufficient justice budgets and further increase deficits, much to the chagrin of mrs merkel. moreover, the procedures for exercising this right will lead to an increase in the number of persons released on grounds of procedural defect. all this in the interests of an absolutely taboo phenomenon: the over-crime of non-european foreigners in all countries experiencing mass immigration. the worst part is that mrs ludford seems to think that no law enforcement or judicial service has ever considered the usefulness of using interpreters and translators not only for the purpose of conducting investigations or trials but also to comply with the so-called rights of the defence as they result, in our democracies, from national provisions and respect for international commitments. this report is superfluous. that is why we did not vote for it.
in writing. i voted strongly in favour of the adoption of this text, which represents not only a breakthrough in the area of the rights of the defence, but also a historic adoption in that it is the first european criminal law measure adopted in codecision. i am very happy that it was adopted by such a majority. this historic legislation, which grants all european citizens the right to translation and interpretation, as soon as they are informed, suspected, prosecuted, questioned and tried in another european country whose language they do not speak, is a great step forward in the progressive construction of a european area of justice. i also welcome the roadmap contained in the stockholm action plan on procedural safeguards. the rights of persons involved in criminal proceedings must be strengthened and a balance must be struck at all costs between the progress made on the prosecution side and the long delay in the rights of the defence: i am thinking of measures in the field of legal information, legal aid, information for relatives, and for vulnerable persons, which are also necessary.
in writing. after several years of successive failures, i welcome the fact that progress is finally being made in the establishment of procedural safeguards for suspects at european level, safeguards which aim to protect the individual against arbitrariness. in cases involving european citizens arrested for criminal offences committed in another member state, it will now be possible to guarantee them access to interpretation and translation of essential documents in their own language. the europe of justice is on the move and i will continue to support it in the initiatives that will complement it in the coming months, such as the rules on interviews and the assistance of a lawyer.
in writing. this text contains some improvements. it is essential to enable any suspect to obtain, without delay, quality translation and interpretation services in the context of criminal proceedings. the inclusion of sign language in these services is a necessity. however, the braille translation should not be overlooked. i shall abstain on this text. it seems to me unacceptable that only documents considered essential should be considered translated. any suspect has the right to know in detail what is being argued for or against him. it is no more acceptable that an oral translation can be offered as a substitute for a written translation. each suspect must be allowed to review all elements of his case at will. without that, a fair and just trial is a figment of the imagination.
in writing. for many of my fellow citizens, the enlarged european union is not homogeneous enough in socioeconomic terms to prevent unfair competition between companies in the 27 member states. this is the case, for example, in the highly competitive transport sector. in addition to the cohesion policy, which i am fighting for every day, partly because it helps to reduce the development gaps within the european union, we need common rules within the internal market. i therefore voted in favour of the amendment calling into question the exclusion of selfemployed drivers from the european legislation on the working time of lorry drivers. like my colleagues in the french delegation of the european people's party, i intend to impose fair competition between all european heavy-duty drivers and to ensure safety on our roads by reducing driver fatigue. i voted in favour of the whole report, as this amendment was adopted.
in writing. i followed the recommendation of the committee which adopted the report by my slovak colleague edit bauer recommending that parliament reject, at first reading by the ordinary legislative procedure, the proposal for a directive amending the 2002 directive on the organisation of working time of persons performing mobile road transport activities. the report calls on the european commission to withdraw its proposal and to submit a new one. i regret that the european commission has hesitated in its reply as to whether or not to withdraw its proposal. i also regret the rapporteur's position of having her report rejected for an amendment which takes the text of a full directive. the real problem is to combat the false independent road haulage companies. hopefully this series will be able to do that.
in writing. i voted against the commission's proposal to include selfemployed road drivers in the 2002 road transport working time directive for the following reasons: 1- a truck driver who is tired is a danger on the road. it is true that he is self-employed or not, and that his fatigue is due to driving or loading his goods. only the driving activity itself and activities directly related to it (such as loading, unloading, cleaning and maintenance of the vehicle, assistance to passengers or formalities with the police and customs authorities) are taken into account in the calculation of the maximum working time. general administrative work (accounting, management, etc.) is not included. the inclusion in the working time directive does not therefore constitute a danger to the activity of the selfemployed. 3- attempting to define "fake selfemployed" through this text was counterproductive. voting for the definitive exclusion of selfemployed workers from the working time directive was to favour the false selfemployed and, in the end, to encourage unfair competition.
in writing. i voted with determination to reject the european commission's proposal not to include selfemployed road drivers in the scope of the road transport working time directive. i am particularly sensitive to the situation of road workers and, in particular, selfemployed road workers, and i am very pleased that the european commission's proposal has been rejected, in this case but also definitively, because i am strongly in favour of including selfemployed drivers in the scope of this directive, in view of the significant risks and negative impact of excluding selfemployed drivers. the european union is estimated to have 1.9 million professional drivers of road haulage vehicles, 31% of whom are selfemployed; i believe that it is necessary to frame their activities within the framework of this directive to ensure a level playing field and to improve road safety. today's europe (with unprecedented growth in road transport volumes and road traffic intensity over the last decade) needs measures to enhance safety on its roads more than ever and, therefore, a framework for the working conditions of professional drivers, which have unfortunately deteriorated.
in writing. i voted against the commission's proposal to exclude selfemployed bus and coach drivers from the scope of the working time directive. not only the health and safety of the drivers is at stake here, but also the safety of other individual drivers, as a tired driver can become a dangerous driver for himself and others. i find the attitude of the rapporteur on this matter scandalous, who continued to negotiate with the council and the commission without any official mandate. this situation is all the more unacceptable because it seems to reflect the interests of markets rather than those of individuals. the social europe must not be trampled on in this way, and that is what i have said.
in writing. to regulate the working time of selfemployed road hauliers seems to us to be contrary to the freedom of enterprise and the very status of the selfemployed. we therefore voted in favour of mrs bauer's report, which seeks to exclude this category from the scope of the directive. how can the working time of a selfemployed person be controlled? how can the non-road working time (administrative, commercial, etc.) of someone who is not and who cannot be recorded by the tachograph be taken into account? beyond the cost of implementing such regulation, it would simply be inapplicable and would be the final blow to an industry already badly hit by the crisis. on the other hand, the fight against the fake independent road hauliers, that is, the drivers who, under the appearance of independence, are in fact employees in disguise, must be intensified and a precise definition must be implemented to distinguish between the "real" and the "fake". fighting social dumping, yes. but it is not the independent road hauliers who are paying the price for the european policy of opening up the transport sector to competition, and cabotage in particular.
in writing. i voted for the sommer report because it represents a balanced compromise between consumer information, which must not be excessive at the risk of being counterproductive and too costly, and lack of information, which would risk undermining the quality of the choices made by the consumer. i am particularly pleased that the european parliament has rejected the principle of a tricolour light which is supposed to indicate the level of health hazards in food. everyone knows that a little chocolate, a little wine, is good for your health! too much chocolate, too much wine, that's bad! a color code of "green, orange, red" would have made no sense! once again the epp group has proved the european parliament right...
in writing. this reform of consumer information has been sloppy and politicized. the commission is not so much concerned with providing clear, useful and easily understandable information as with making moral statements by means of labels. the rapporteur has tried to pass, without always succeeding, common sense amendments, such as the removal of the famous 'nutritional profiles', which have no scientific basis but are the result of an ideological desire to control what is on our plates, by making us feel guilty. it is true that brussels will certainly fail less in this area than in all those which fall within its competence, such as the control of financial speculation or illegal immigration, the fight against counterfeiting, etc. it is a sign of both powerlessness and tyranny: powerlessness in the face of great political, economic and social problems, tyranny over defenseless individuals. these profiles have been maintained. let's hope they disappear on second reading. the only good surprise was the requirement to indicate whether an animal was slaughtered without stunning, that is, in accordance with a ritual, to avoid that it could be sold unknowingly to consumers who do not share the religious convictions that require such procedures!
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on consumer information on foodstuffs. i am pleased with this vote which will enable consumers to have clear, legible and reliable labelling on a number of food products in the future. the idea of a colour code, wanted by the socialists and the greens, on packaging indicating whether the quantity of essential nutrients is high (green), medium (yellow) or low (red) has been rejected thanks to the european people's party and i welcome that! the basis of a balanced diet is a varied diet. the colour code would have the effect of stigmatising certain foods and i do not see how it would help our fellow citizens to balance their diet. we have managed to avoid over-regulation which would harm consumers and our smes. i am also pleased with the exemption from nutritional labelling for wine, which is the pleasure sector par excellence. we should not jeopardize our wine sector, which is already subject to detailed regulations.
in writing. i have advocated clearer labelling of the nutritional values on the front of all pre-packaged food packaging, in particular by supporting the introduction of a 'colour code' to make it easier to identify the content of essential nutrients, which is advocated by consumer associations and health professionals. the food industry must stop hiding the reality of the detrimental effects on nutritional balance that certain foods clearly cause. i also voted in favour of an amendment to supplement the information on the origin of products by specifying their true origin, that is to say the place where the food is wholly obtained. finally, i also rejected the proposal to include alcohol in the regulation.
in writing. i am very pleased with the outcome of the vote on the sommer report. the european parliament has opted for a readable and educational labelling system that will promote balanced consumption patterns. i also welcome the adoption of amendment no 205 which will make it possible to include a mandatory label for meat from animals slaughtered without stunning. the consumer must be informed about the respect of animal welfare practices, which are at the heart of european food policy. it is not a question of stigmatising religious communities or of hindering their production and distribution of meat, but simply of allowing the european citizen to consume with full knowledge of the facts.
in writing. supported by the five largest political groups in the european parliament, this joint resolution calls on the member states to go further in their commitments to this long-term economic strategy of the european union. after the lisbon strategy (2000-2010) which was marked by its lack of concrete results, the eu 2020 strategy does not have the right to disappoint. the member states will therefore have to make the reforms and adopt the measures necessary to achieve the objectives set. personally, i am pleased that my colleagues supported my call for further simplification of procedures for the structural funds and included in the resolution the following sentence that i had prepared: i therefore urge that the rules for implementing cohesion policy be further simplified to promote conviviality and accountability and to increase responsiveness to future challenges and the risk of economic crises
in writing. of course i support the objectives of strategy 2020, particularly in the areas of employment, research, development and innovation, the fight against climate change, poverty reduction and improving the level of training. but i fear that, in the absence of binding commitments made and respected by the member states, these objectives will not be achieved. if we continue to use the open method of coordination, despite the repeated requests of the european parliament, the same causes will produce the same effects. what has not worked for the lisbon strategy over the last 10 years will not work for the europe 2020 strategy either. we need more of a community method. and we need measures that are directly operational. the success of the eu 2020 strategy depends on this.
in writing. europe is clearly suffering from a lack of economic governance. while monetary policy is unified around the euro, each member state unfortunately continues to pursue its own economic policy, often without taking into account the reforms of its neighbour, or even sometimes by 'smearing' the situation of its public accounts. this was the source of the greek crisis and could well cause other crises in the future if we are not careful. i therefore agree 100% with the wording of paragraph 15 of this resolution on economic governance. it is true that 'member states should not regard their respective economic policies as a matter of purely national interest but also as a matter of common interest and should formulate their policies accordingly'. beyond that, the proposed measures seem to me to be really moving in the right direction: strengthening the powers of eurostat, creating a european monetary fund, issuing euro-bonds, adopting binding measures with regard to the implementation of the eu 2020 strategy, taking better account of the european parliament in the field of economic policy, etc. for all these reasons i voted in favour of this resolution.
in writing. to emerge from the financial crisis, europe needs ambitious and far-reaching reform of its economic governance. the european parliament stresses the need to rely on: (i) more of the community method rather than on the strengthening of intergovernmentalism; and (ii) operational measures rather than on simple open coordination and peer review, which led to the failure of the lisbon strategy. the strategy advocated by a large majority in parliament is based on five pillars: a more proactive stability and growth pact; genuine economic governance led by the commission; an acceleration of the transition to a sustainable economy, based on the monti report and a european programme of investment in the infrastructure of central and southern europe; new permanent instruments (european monetary fund and european bond market) to be better prepared for future crises; a better calibrated eu2020 strategy, with sanctions and incentives for its proper implementation.
in writing. the current crisis is a direct consequence of the liberal policies advocated by the european union. the stability and growth pact is directly responsible for the present suffering of the people of the euro area. it is an aberration to want to apply it more rigorously. the commission's request for more powers in this area is another. it is the people who produce the wealth that the ruling eurocracy shares. it is high time that the people take back power in europe, because it is not the barroso commission or the epp, sd, alde and green groups, which signed this resolution, that will build the europe of solidarity we need.
in writing. in one year's time, in july 2011, the european commission will present a quantified proposal for the multiannual financial framework 2014-2020. it is essential that the european parliament thinks ahead to the challenges ahead and formulates its budgetary priorities. i therefore voted in favour of the creation of this special parliamentary committee, whose work will last for one year and whose task will be to: (a) define parliament's political priorities for the post-2013 mff, in both legislative and budgetary terms; (b) estimate the financial resources needed to enable the european union to achieve its objectives and implement its policies as from 1 january 2014; (c) define the duration of the next mff; (d) to propose a structure for the future cfp, indicating the main areas of union activity; (e) to propose guidelines for an indicative allocation of resources between the different headings of the mff; (f) clarify the link between a reform of the system of financing the eu budget and a review of expenditure. finally, i would like to thank my colleagues very warmly for having chosen me to sit on this committee as an alternate member, alongside michel dantin, alain lamassoure and damien abad.

in writing. it is regrettable that council regulation (ec) no 1236/2005 concerning trade in certain goods which could be used for capital punishment, torture or other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment has not been implemented by all member states. i find it unacceptable that some people have not hesitated to allow the export of articles that could be used for torture to countries that do not respect human rights. it was therefore urgent to bring them to order by adopting this resolution. the member states should be encouraged to contribute to the promotion of human rights in the world and to monitor more closely the international trade in instruments of torture, rather than taking part in it. i think that sanctions should be taken to dissuade them from doing so. in addition, this resolution rightly calls on the commission to update the list of instruments of torture, since these instruments are constantly evolving. i therefore voted in favour of this text, but i think we need to go further.
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution against the trade in goods used for torture. while it is welcome that there has been a community regulation on international trade in certain goods liable to be used for capital punishment, torture or other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment since 2005, it is now clear that there are serious shortcomings both in its scope and in its implementation: firstly, many member states have not communicated - or even introduced - sanctions for violations of this regulation, and do not submit any annual activity report, although mandatory; second, it is time to address the lack of oversight of export criteria for the products concerned and to address courageously the issue of currently exempt goods transiting through the eu; finally, the list of prohibited articles should be extended (it does not currently cover certain so-called 'police and security' equipment, such as pointed sticks, wall or floor restraints, foot restraints, handcuffs for wrists and fingers, or certain electric shock stunning devices worn on the body).
in writing. the opening of the transatlantic air 'market' serves the general interest. it increases competition between airlines to the detriment of airline employees. it increases air traffic at the expense of the ecosystem. it contains no real guarantee regarding the protection of personal data (pnr) which the united states registers at will to the detriment of the rights of european citizens. this resolution, this machine for deregulation which is characteristic of everything that foreshadows the future great transatlantic market, i am voting against.
in writing. the first railway package, which was adopted in 2001 and contains three directives on the development of community railways, licensing of railway undertakings and allocation of railway infrastructure capacity, railway infrastructure charging and safety certification, was intended to revitalise the railway sector as a first step towards creating an integrated european railway area. however, according to the commission's latest report on the monitoring of rail market developments, the share of rail in transport has not increased but has only stabilised at a low rate of around 10% in the rail freight market and at less than 7% for passenger transport. in this resolution, which i have supported, parliament therefore calls on the member states to implement the railway package more effectively and on the commission to ensure that it is properly implemented.
in writing. today's resolution does not take the problem in the right direction. it is not because the member states have applied the first railway package badly or not at all that this sector is experiencing difficulties or malfunctions, but quite the opposite. the liberalization of network activities has of course led to a pure profit-making logic and to the disorganization of the sector. in france, high-speed lines and services are preferred to slower or regional services. prices have gone up. but the needs and expectations of users are, in many cases, totally neglected to the point that the schedules are inadequate. anyway, they're getting less and less tight. the network is maintained accordingly and deteriorates on many lines, at least those that are not closed. in britain and belgium, this logic is partly responsible for railway accidents. similar problems are already arising for users in the electricity and postal sectors. you're forced to regulate phone rates because of the abuse. don't you think it's time to stop charging?
in writing. the liberalisation of the railway market, imposed on member states by the 2001 directives, has not led to an improvement in service for citizens. the infrastructure is deteriorating because of insufficient investment. but should we condemn the states which have chosen not to dismantle the historical operators to the point of rendering them ineffective? this resolution is a proof of the ideological stubbornness of the liberals, far removed from common sense and reality. i can only vote against.
in writing. first of all, i would like to thank my socialist colleague hannes swoboda for his proposal to include france in the scope of this resolution, following the floods which took place this week in the south of the country and which claimed the lives of more than 25 people. given the scale of the material and human damage caused by these floods in central europe and france, it seems logical to me that the european union solidarity fund (eusf) should be released as soon as possible and used effectively to help rebuild the damaged areas; that is why i voted in favour of this resolution. but to do this, a new regulation on the eusf is also necessary, because access to the fund is currently subject to a procedure that is too long and complicated. similarly, i believe that a large proportion of other european funds should be devoted to projects for the prevention of risks and natural disasters, with a view to sustainable land and habitat development, use and management, in order to respond effectively to the new climate challenges.

president of the european council. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i have no major problems with certain criticisms. i have a problem with the general approach, so i'll explain. when i was here in february, when we were talking about the outcome of the first informal european council, there were strong doubts whether we would succeed in creating a financial support plan for greece and whether that country would be able to take the necessary steps to correct what went wrong in the past. yet, a few weeks later, we adopted a €110 billion plan and greece made an effort of at least 10 percentage points of gdp to correct the budgetary pull. we didn't believe it, but it happened. if we had said a few weeks ago that we would be creating a potential bailout of 750 billion, of which 500 billion would come from europe or the european union in general, we would not have believed us, but it has happened. some have said: 'the mediterranean countries have a different culture, they are not capable of taking any real reform measures, it is a waste of effort!' when i see what is happening in these countries now, in painful circumstances - which no one is happy about - i say that there is a profound cultural change. i hear criticism about the climate, when the european union has the most ambitious climate programme in the world. we even gave a legal basis to our 20-20-20 program. everyone is jealous of us. but when i hear the criticism, i feel like we're doing nothing. it bothers me. i am not saying that we should sin with a kind of happy optimism, but what bothers me is that every achievement is considered "too little, too late" and superfluous. when i look at the results of the last few months, i am also pleased with the positive effects of our action. we're talking about better governance here. of course the euro has helped us a lot in the financial crisis! i cannot for one moment imagine what the consequences of this financial crisis would be if we did not have this common currency at our disposal for 350 million people! union must step up its investment in skills and training to support sustainable employment. the unemployment rate in the european union remains far too high and atypical contracts therefore have their place in the labour market. for young people, the atypical contract may, for example, be a first experience on the labour market. if the atypical contract can give young people a chance and encourage a job through a permanent contract, then i say yes. for people who are faced with a long period of inactivity, here again, if the atypical contract plays a transitional role towards returning to the labour market, then i am in favour of this form of contract. finally, if the atypical contract is used as part of a transition from one job to another or from one occupational status to another, once again i say yes, because the main thing is to keep the person in the labour market. i will also stress the fundamental role played by the social partners and civil society organisations in the development and implementation of employment policies. i call on all member states to involve them fully, because their interventions vary far too often from one member state to another. finally, their social and institutional recognition must be strengthened. with this report, the european parliament is sending a strong signal to the governments of the member states and to the commission. the security of career paths is a sine qua non of social europe. the ball is now in the court of the european council, which i hope will uphold the spring 2010 council resolutions on employment. the european union needs clear guidelines and concrete measures to safeguard employment in our regions and create new prospects under the 2020 strategy.

in writing. the paris convention regulates the frequency, quality and organisation procedures of international exhibitions. the rapporteur, whom i supported, asked that those member states which were interested in this convention and which had not yet acceded to it should do so as soon as possible. this is a question which seems to me to be very important. the paris convention can only be signed by states and not by the european union. it is therefore essential that as many countries as possible sign this convention. this convention will enable the new signatory states to engage, as others have done before them, in the dissemination of innovation and thus contribute to the education of european citizens.
in writing. i strongly support the adoption of this agreement, which provides for the application of the 'prüm decisions' to iceland and norway. although these two states are not members of the european union, they are nevertheless part of schengen cooperation, which means in practice that no internal border controls are carried out between these states and the other states of the schengen area. this situation fully justifies the increased involvement of these states in crossborder cooperation with a view to combating terrorism and international crime effectively. the agreement will enable the norwegian and icelandic authorities to cooperate more actively in these areas by implementing the two 'prüm decisions', which provide for the exchange of information on dna profiles, fingerprint data and vehicle registration records.

in writing. shadow rapporteur for the adle group on this dossier, i voted in favour of this report which will allow the participation of switzerland and liechtenstein in frontex. the frontex agency was set up in 2004 to enable operational cooperation between member states in the management of external borders. for reasons of efficiency, it is important that all the states associated to the schengen agreements participate.
in writing. i voted in favour of the arrangement laying down the detailed rules for operational cooperation between switzerland and liechtenstein in the activities of the frontex agency. operational since 2005, this agency has the heavy burden of coordinating cooperation between member states in the field of external border control. the expansion of the number of countries participating in frontex actions is therefore a welcome initiative as it will further strengthen the operational and budgetary powers of the frontex agency. the geographical situation of these states will require them to participate more in the strengthening of controls at air and land borders rather than at sea. strengthening border control at these borders is one of the major challenges facing the union in view of the considerable number of irregular crossings of land borders each year. of course, under this agreement, this participation will be on a voluntary basis, but i very much hope that the forthcoming revision of the regulation establishing the frontex agency will force member states to cooperate more in the management of our common external borders.

in writing. the karas report is part of the european response to the greek crisis. improvements in economic surveillance and governance are more than necessary today, in particular to address the market distrust that remains a burden for greece and the european union as a whole. the report therefore aims to strengthen eurostat to avoid a repeat of the greek case in the future, and more specifically the erroneous statistics. i voted in favour of this report, as i believe that the european commission's proposal is acceptable at the moment but that it is also the minimum of additional surveillance that can be accepted. in addition, the rapporteur rightly advocates the prospect of closer cooperation between the european commission (eurostat) and the european central bank, all while respecting the role and independence of the two institutions.
in writing. the current crisis is not due to statistical inaccuracies but to the dogmatism of the liberal elites who govern. the report calls for full respect for the stability and growth pact. it encourages the introduction of unannounced controls on state budgets. it has turned suspicion into political doctrine by calling for sanctions against states that falsify their statistics. the european project cannot be confused with this authoritarianism which denies popular sovereignty! it is high time to build the europe of solidarity, cooperation and shared trust that we need.
in writing. i welcome the report on the european union strategy for the baltic sea. the concept of the macro-region provides concrete answers to many contemporary challenges that transcend national borders. the baltic sea strategy is the first attempt at a macro-region. it will enable different territories, but facing similar problems, to undertake joint actions within a flexible institutional framework. this macro-region will not be a competitor of the states, but a complement. it will be based on the principle of partnership between the various levels of public authorities, the private sector and the voluntary sector. this new form of governance will undoubtedly add value to local, national and european policies. the concept of macro-region is worth applying to other territories marked by strong economic, environmental and cultural interdependence. the rapporteur rightly points out that the baltic sea strategy is a pilot project which can serve as a model for future macro-regional strategies. the atlantic arc should, i think, be at the heart of the thinking on these future strategies. because of the common problems facing the coastal regions of brittany, cornwall, galicia and the algarve, among others, the creation of an atlantic macro-region will contribute to a common and harmonious development.
in writing. encourage cooperation between the baltic sea states to protect the area and to address common economic, social, energy, transport and other challenges. yes, why not, although it seems to me that this cooperation could very well be achieved without the intervention of the european commission. but, to be honest, the main thrust of the report is the promotion of the macro-regions as an additional, and perhaps in the future, unique, 'level of governance' of the european union's 'cohesion' policy. this cohesion would consist in the aggregation of regions on both sides of frontiers, if possible in the form of european groupings of territorial authorities, these groupings being called upon to have legal personality and to choose "sovereignly" the national law governing them. and so much so that it is necessary to seek or invent common interests to which the regions can be grouped, and to create a european tax to finance all this. whatever the rapporteur says, anything is possible to abolish national frontiers and to rearrange the european landscape. that is why, beyond the interest that the baltic sea and its problems may inspire, we voted against this report.
in writing. the report's only merit is that it calls for the cleanup of the baltic sea. this cleaning is necessary for the preservation of our ecosystem. it must be carried out as soon as possible. however, this text is marked by the same dogmatism as most of the reports submitted to our vote. while he claims to be environmentally responsible, he cites the development of nuclear power in the region without condemning it. the commission's stated intention to create highly competitive european macro-regions is completely unacceptable. the aim of these measures is once again to dismantle the welfare state. the rehabilitation of the baltic sea cannot be the rehabilitation of liberalism!
in writing. it should be noted that the european union's regional policy is the main european factor of economic recovery since, as the report points out, it is the most important community source of investment in the real economy. but it is important that the economic recovery of our regions is not only immediate, but also medium- and long-term. that is why the kratsa report, for which i voted, is aimed at tackling structural problems, particularly those relating to competitiveness and employment. today, all actors in our regions are affected by the crisis. small and medium-sized enterprises, for example, are finding it increasingly difficult to use microfinance and microcredit. strengthening the attractiveness of our regions is therefore a fundamental objective which will eventually allow for increased investment, if necessary, in our regions.
in writing. cohesion policy is an important source of funding for europe's regions and as such plays a key role in tackling the economic and financial crisis. i agree with the rapporteur that objective 2 is of particular importance. while the structural funds must give priority to helping regions whose development is lagging behind, other regions must have access to financing adapted to their problems. since the 2006 reform, objective 2 has contributed to strengthening regional competitiveness and employment, with €54.7 billion of funding for the period 2007-13. this investment in the competitiveness of regional economies is all the more relevant in times of economic crisis. it is through an effort of innovation, research and development that the european union will be able to regain and stabilise sustainable growth and skilled jobs. in the context of the debate on the european financial perspective after 2013, it is essential that the european parliament reiterates its commitment to objective 2. cohesion policy must remain a strong and well-funded policy, and i therefore stress the need to preserve the financial means of objective 2. this is essential to facilitate the convergence of all european regions.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by mrs rodi kratsa-tsagaropoulou on the contribution of eu regional policy to the fight against the economic and financial crisis. as the community's main source of investment in the real economy, eu regional policy can make a decisive contribution to the european plan for economic recovery. as much as €55 billion has been earmarked for business support measures under the european regional policy for the period 2007-13. this aid is essential - especially for smes, which have been greatly weakened by the economic crisis - and must be increased. investment in research, development, innovation and education must also be strengthened to support economic growth and employment in our regions - i am thinking in particular of the south-west constituency of france, which i represent. finally, the eu's regional policy will only be truly effective if there is genuine cooperation between local, regional, national, crossborder and european public authorities.
in writing. the report aims to improve passenger rights in bus and coach transport, an ambition which i welcomed with a positive vote. i have therefore advocated greater convenience in these transports for disabled persons and persons with reduced mobility, and greater guarantees for all passengers, not only in the event of accidents but also in the event of delays or cancellations. however, i thought it best to abstain on amendment no 14. although it provides for the possibility for member states to grant a derogation from the application of the regulation in respect of scheduled urban, suburban and regional transport services, i believe that it does not go far enough and still imposes too many constraints, particularly in the area of assistance, which would be detrimental to small and mediumsized enterprises. this was a second reading vote. the important thing now is to reach an agreement with the eu council so that this regulation can enter into force.
in writing. in recent months, the commission has focused its attention on consumer law, in particular that of passengers of all modes of transport. it cannot, however, treat the bus and coach sector, which is mainly composed of smes, as an airline or railway company is treated, or impose obligations which are proportionately more stringent and much more costly for a small company, which may not survive, than for a large multinational. the enormous gap between parliament's very dogmatic amendments and the more pragmatic compromise reached in the council is also significant. i also think that there is a fundamental inequity in the strictness of the proposed accident obligations for companies which are by definition 'captive' to european territory, while airlines or shipping companies are governed by international agreements which allow them to disconnect compensation from the damage actually suffered, as the tragic case of the rio-paris flight tends to prove.
in writing. bus and coach passengers should enjoy rights similar to those already granted by european legislation to air and sea passengers. bus passengers cannot and should not be the only ones who are not protected by community regulations. this is the key message i wish to convey by voting for this text, and i deeply regret that a common framework for all modes of transport could not be agreed. in particular, i voted in favour of the many amendments which aimed to introduce greater liability for carriers in the event of loss or damage to baggage and especially in the event of injury or death of passengers. in particular, i strongly supported the proposals to consolidate the rights of disabled people and people with reduced mobility, their accessibility to transport, but also their information in accessible formats, because we have a responsibility in this area. i am disappointed that a compromise could not be reached with the council, which has shown very little inclination to move forward. but if this is not an easy subject, we must have a european framework to protect the rights of these passengers and the conciliation will lead us, in the autumn, to discuss this again.
in writing. i voted in favour of the cancian report on passenger rights in bus and coach transport. this regulation is essential in terms of protecting the rights of travellers, since it lays down european rules on the information to be given to passengers before and during their journey, assistance and compensation in the event of interruption of that journey, or specific measures for persons with reduced mobility. the council has clearly departed from the ambitious approach adopted by our assembly at first reading, and today we are confirming our determination to reach a major text and are moving slowly towards conciliation. in this context, i am particularly pleased that we are sending a clear signal to the council by adopting today all the amendments relating to the liability of carriers, whether it be compensation for loss of or damage to baggage, or compensation for injury or, even more tragically, death of passengers. i am sure that the council has taken note of our determination.
in writing. i voted in favour of this draft regulation on the rights of passengers travelling by sea or inland waterway as i believe it is essential to increase these rights for my fellow european citizens. the rights of disabled persons and persons with reduced mobility must be strengthened, in particular, through this report and the dynamic of protection of travellers within the european union. i also appreciate the fact that this report takes account of exceptional circumstances which, although they are extraordinary, can cause serious problems for travellers when they occur. the report is designed to facilitate assistance, re-routing, reimbursement and compensation for passengers in such circumstances. this was a second reading vote. the important thing now is to reach an agreement with the eu council so that this regulation can enter into force as soon as possible.
in writing. i voted for the alaya sender report on the rights of passengers travelling by sea or inland waterway, because i believe it is important that these passengers enjoy the same rights and guarantees as air passengers. whether in the event of delay, breakdown, loss of baggage or, more seriously, accident, carriers must assume their responsibilities and passengers must be protected and, where appropriate, properly compensated. i welcome the adoption of specific provisions requiring transport companies to accommodate disabled persons or persons with reduced mobility and to train their staff accordingly.
in writing. this report aims to accelerate the deployment and interoperability of intelligent transport systems (its) in road transport at eu level. i am always concerned about improving territorial cohesion within the union and i believe that this directive will be a step forward in this direction. i therefore supported it, especially since the directive as adopted by the parliament's committee on transport deals with the question of the protection of personal data in a balanced way. i hope therefore that an agreement will be reached with the council at second reading, because this is a directive which can only strengthen the confidence of european citizens in the transport of the european union.
in writing. i voted enthusiastically in favour of this text because it encourages the development of so-called 'intelligent' transport systems, i.e. the use of new technologies in the field of transport. these systems will allow better monitoring and management of road traffic, as well as greater safety and security for road users. they will make road transport safer and cheaper, as well as reducing congestion and greenhouse gas emissions. in this respect, the adoption of this text represents a major step forward for the european citizens, who will be the first to benefit from the arrival of these new transport technologies, and i welcome this.
in writing. i voted with conviction for the adoption of this legislative resolution, as it provides for the simplification of the administrative formalities applicable to ships entering or leaving the ports of the member states. i am glad that it was adopted by an overwhelming majority: from now on, ships will no longer be subject to complex and repetitive administrative formalities; a standard form will be established, as well as a new electronic system which will allow information to be shared quickly and easily between the ship and the port authority. this text represents a major step towards the creation of a large european shipping network without barriers, which i have been calling for for many years.
in writing. three factors are making it necessary to reflect deeply on the future of the european transport system: the enlargement of the european union to 27 member states, our environmental responsibilities and our commitment to passenger safety. this is the subject of this report, which i think is relevant on at least two levels. first, the notion of 'efficient co-modality', which affirms complementarity and not competition between different modes of transport. secondly, the need for sustainable transport, which requires us to work towards a decarbonisation of transport, as well as the development of intelligent transport systems. i nevertheless supported the amendment tabled on paragraph 32, which introduced the concept of a european transport fund. it seems to me that an independent fund dedicated to transport would risk undermining the coherence of cohesion policy, 60% of which is allocated to transport. the organization of the structural funds must be considered in a concerted and comprehensive manner in the context of the next multiannual financial framework.
in writing. the report on a sustainable future for transport is a positive signal for an efficient and integrated transport europe. without an acceleration of the mutual recognition and authorisation procedures for rolling stock, market access will continue to be time-consuming and costly. less road transport, more rail, river and sea links for freight, a protected and protected environment - these projects paint a picture of an ideal europe. but the reality is a little different. all these projects are lagging behind due to lack of political will, coordination between member states and funding. clearly, there is a lack of collective ambition. the european union will face many challenges by 2020: the european commission's forthcoming white paper on european transport policy for the next ten years is an opportunity to develop a comprehensive, integrated and transversal strategy to meet the challenges of the years ahead. the resolution we have just adopted is a strong signal to the european commission, a first step in this strategy, and it wants to give transport its place in european policies.
in writing. the report calls for safer, more efficient, less polluting transport - nothing but the very agreed and very obvious. however, several points caught our attention and prompted our negative vote: - the usual focus on co2 emissions with binding quantified targets, while only passing mention is made of sox and nox emissions from maritime transport, with all the other ecological virtues; - the proposal to create a european road transport agency, whose relevance is more than questionable, given the criticism of reduced efficiency, high costs, and the haphazard management of many of the existing multiple european agencies; - the proposal to create a european fund for transport, and therefore additional expenditure, without specifying how they will be financed - and, the reaffirmation that the solution to all the problems would come from a greater liberalisation of the road sector and the expansion of cabotage, in particular. it is well known that this liberalization has had negative effects, particularly on the maintenance of existing railway infrastructure and thus on safety. we also know, or should know, to what extent the opening up of national transport to foreign operators poses problems of unfair competition.
in writing. this text does not provide the means to establish high social and environmental standards in the transport sector, which are admittedly indispensable. by placing itself in the context of the carbon market, by validating the possibility of an increase in air traffic, by advocating the resolute liberalization of this sector for greater competitiveness, this report nullifies any ecological requirement worthy of the name. by only being concerned with infrastructure and never with the wage conditions of the workers in this sector, it shows a social indifference which is a signature of the harmful liberalism which is killing the european project. i vote against it.
in writing. the treaty of lisbon has confirmed the right to petition the european parliament, which is truly part of a process of completing european citizenship. however, the persistent confusion between european and national competences and the competences of the european institutions underlines that european citizens are not yet fully aware of their rights. that is why, in voting for this report, i supported the introduction of better information on the petitions procedure. a european petition should enable citizens to share with parliament their concerns about the impact of the various policies and legislation of the european union on their daily lives. the report proposes a number of possibilities which seem to me to be sensible, such as improving the website dedicated to petitions on the parliament's portal or setting up a one-stop shop to provide guidance to citizens.
, in writing. i voted in favour of this european parliament resolution because it concerns the 2009 activity report of the parliament's committee on petitions. the resolution also calls for the european parliament to be given the right to vote in the european parliament. it is therefore an instrument of democracy and citizenship. the main themes of the petitions concern the environment, fundamental rights, justice and the internal market, and they come mainly from germany, spain, italy and romania. i welcome the progress made in implementing the recommendations of the ep's committee on petitions to improve its work, but also the proposals made to allow european citizens to exercise this right better, such as the request for simplification of procedures, and in particular the possibility of introducing a petition via the internet. one small regret: french citizens rarely use this procedure.
in writing. the economic recession which has affected the whole of the european union has exposed young people more than ever to the risks of poverty, and in particular unemployment. the precarious situation of young people has an economic cost, but above all a social one. this own-initiative report was intended to identify the current difficulties and to propose some solutions. in particular, it calls for the development of economic and political investment in job creation, education and training, the strengthening of social security systems, the dynamisation of the labour market and the promotion of decent work. i fully agree with these objectives and have voted in favour of this report. of course, it is not just a matter of loudly stating these objectives, but it is now necessary to conduct a real economic and social policy at european level in order to improve young people's access to the labour market.
in writing. more than 20% of young people in europe are now unemployed and many others are in precarious jobs without social protection. the proliferation of traineeships makes young workers vulnerable and is a vector of social dumping against other employees, by exerting downward pressure on wages and by substituting for normal jobs. the turunen report calls on the commission and the member states to take action to make access for young people to quality work placements and jobs a priority and to guarantee them decent incomes. it is unacceptable that some states provide for a lower minimum wage for young people. the report also calls for the creation of a 'european youth guarantee' which gives every young person in the eu the right to be offered a job, an apprenticeship, further training or a job combined with training after a period of unemployment of four months, and for the development of a 'european quality charter for traineeships' including standards for their maximum duration, minimum allowances and social security benefits.
in writing. 5.5 million europeans under the age of 25, or nearly one in five young people, are now unemployed, not counting those in precarious jobs. the young people under 25 are the first to be affected by the current economic crisis. the training policy for young people must therefore be ambitious in order to enable them to acquire skills more suited to the needs of enterprises: more traineeships and apprenticeships must be organised, but it must also be ensured that they are of good quality (the content of the traineeships, the duration of the apprenticeship, the allowances paid to the trainee, etc.) in order to protect young people from possible abuse by employers. despite its limited 'social' powers, the european union must therefore promote a mobilization in this field, and that is why i voted with conviction in favour of this resolution which proposes some ways of dealing with the difficult situation of european youth.
in writing. given the many difficulties faced by young europeans unemployment, wage, financial and social insecurity , it was urgent that the european parliament act more firmly to remedy this situation. that is why i voted in favour of the report by mrs turunen, because i believe that it contains many guarantees for the protection of european youth, such as the drawing up of a 'european quality charter for apprenticeships', the creation of a minimum income for every young person and the introduction of the 'european youth guarantee'. even if not all the proposals will be binding, i believe that young europeans need to be taken into account more effectively in the policies of the union, because they represent the future of the european union.
in writing. young people should not be unemployed for more than four months, and i agree with that. the report on youth employment proposes a 'european youth guarantee' to enable young people to benefit from a decent income and quality traineeships. in view of the worsening unemployment of young people in the outermost regions, and particularly in réunion, i fully support any measure to promote the integration of young people into the world of work and to combat their precariousness. if the right of every young person to be offered a job, an apprenticeship, further training or a job combined with training after a period of unemployment of up to four months is a matter of proclamation, concrete measures must now follow from this report by parliament. that is why i voted for this report.
in writing. i supported the report by my colleague emilie turunen, whose aim is to propose answers to the difficult situation of european youth, faced with unemployment - which currently affects one in five young people under 25 according to eurostat -, precariousness and abuse by employers. the training policy for young people must be ambitious and enable them to acquire skills adapted to the needs of enterprises so that they can more easily integrate into the labour market. there is a need for more traineeships and apprenticeships, which develop and improve these skills, and for companies to be encouraged to increase the opportunities they offer young people. it is also important to ensure that the quality of the food is good. as such, the establishment of minimum standards for the educational content of traineeships and apprenticeships would contribute to this. extended to the length of the vocational training period and the level of allowances paid to trainees and apprentices, these standards would also help to protect young people from possible abuse by their employers.
in writing. i abstained on this report on youth employment which, despite some positive points including the adoption of some amendments which i had proposed in the committee on culture (creation of jobs in the social economy, fight against discrimination, rejection of the trivialization of traineeships, recognition of non-formal education, etc.) remains focused on flexibility (flexible and serious contracts) and the short-term needs of enterprises. it stressed the consequences of the massive unemployment of young people, also in the light of the crisis, but at the same time reaffirmed the continuation of measures to assist economic actors which had not proved their worth and had only led to an increase in the precariousness of young people's employment. in addition, the report remains faithful to the dogma of the 'modernization' of education; it even speaks of prioritizing cooperation between enterprises and 'educational service providers' and calls for early cooperation between schools and the world of work.
in writing. in these difficult times of economic crisis, our european social model must be more than ever the key to returning to growth. it should not be seen as a burden but, on the contrary, as a driving force for the progress of our societies. i voted in favour of the gruny report which aims to launch a broad european initiative for employment. the idea is to make it possible to set up a business anywhere in the european union in three days and at no cost. the formalities for recruiting the first employees could be carried out via a single interface, by strengthening the activation plans, especially for the low-skilled, by personalised advice, intensive training/re-skilling of workers and upgrading their qualifications, etc. i believe that preserving employment and creating new job opportunities for the youngest, but also for those who are on the labour market but are no longer employed, is the sine qua non for restoring the confidence of our citizens in our european social model. and it is this trust that is essential for our future, socially, economically and politically.
in writing. the supposed popularity of self-employment is evidence not of a new enthusiasm for business creation but of a deep discouragement of the unemployed in the face of the impotence or inefficiency of employment services. the precarious nature of contracts and employment is the consequence of policies to open up markets to foreign competition. this openness weighs on the level of wages and employment, which is almost the last adjustment variable left for firms in a world of unfair competition. the immigration policies currently being pursued in europe are also having an impact on the wages and employment conditions of the least qualified workers, as is shown by a large number of statistical studies. this is not to mention their disproportionate costs to public finances and thus their responsibility for public deficits and debts, and for the tax burden on european citizens. but ignoring all this, the rapporteur persists in a general political logic which leads to precariousness, unemployment and the proliferation of the working poor. he advocates flexicurity', knowing that in the world created by the european union, companies will inevitably only retain 'flex'. the unemployed and the working people should not look to brussels for salvation, quite the contrary!
in writing. i voted for the gruny report on atypical contracts, secure career paths, flexicurity and new forms of social dialogue because in recent years atypical forms of employment (part-time, shift work, etc.) have increased considerably and because workers need to be protected. the crisis must not be used as a pretext for the development of precarious work. all employees must be protected by labour law, regardless of the form of their contract. the report also calls on the member states to review flexicurity policies in a more protective way for workers, and stresses the importance of social dialogue and the social partners in tackling these issues.
in writing. i voted against this resolution because it is part of the promotion of flexible employment, flexicurity and their usual corollaries (employability, employability and adaptability and entrepreneurship). the resolution also aims to simplify the various types of employment contract, under the pretext of reducing the number of atypical employment contracts and facilitating transitions between different types of employment contract. while recognising the social consequences of the current crisis, including the increase in the number of poor workers and atypical forms of work, the resolution also deplores the failure of enterprises to develop new forms of employment contracts which offer sufficient flexibility to respond to crisis situations. in short, this resolution remains marked by a neo-liberal approach, the disastrous effects of which we have been able to see for many years in the field of employment and labour rights.
in writing. mr fernandes received my full support for his report on the european commission's green paper on the management of bio-waste in the european union. i think he was right to consider all the issues, including prevention and recycling in the first place. biodegradable waste has a role to play in a broader issue, namely the fight against climate change. it is therefore essential to divert bio-waste from landfills, which are the worst long-term solution. on the contrary, as the report emphasizes, they should be used for composting or for the production of bioenergy. finally, the current management of bio-waste reflects a great diversity between member states. i am in favour of a single legislative act, as proposed in this report. finally, i would add that the management of bio-waste can support the social cohesion of the european union, since a recycling industry, for example, is a strong job creator.
in writing. i voted in favour of the green paper on the management of biodegradable waste in the european union. there is a large difference between the member states that recycle the least (90% landfill, 10% recycling and energy recovery) and those that have adopted the most efficient approaches (10% landfill, 25% energy recovery and 65% recycling). biodegradable waste plays an important role in the fight against climate change and offers interesting potential in terms of soil protection and the promotion of renewable energy production. member states should take measures to promote the separate collection of bio-waste for purposes such as composting. a genuine european market for compost must be created, because it is the most suitable treatment for green waste and has the advantage of being used to fertilize the soil. proper management of bio-waste would therefore have not only environmental but also economic benefits.
in writing. this text is in the right direction. the proposal to take waste out of landfills, to prefer composting to incineration, to ensure that incineration makes energy use of waste, is partly in line with the ecological planning we are advocating. i'm glad to hear it. however, the promotion of biofuels and the encouragement of the privatisation of waste management which he advocates are taking up the liberal trends without any regard for their failures. i'll abstain from it.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution, in which the european parliament calls on the european commission to take action on the treatment and management of bio-waste i.e. waste from food and food preparation, green waste (garden, park, etc.), industrial waste (wood, etc.) , in particular by presenting a specific draft directive. the european parliament thus reaffirms a request made during the review of community waste legislation in 2008. the european parliament calls for the compulsory selective sorting of biowaste, the recycling of biowaste and the classification of compost according to its quality. the commission and the member states must take measures to make europeans aware of the environmental benefits of the treatment of bio-waste. this waste represents between 118 and 138 million tonnes of organic waste and therefore ends up, for the most part, in the collection of normal waste, whereas it could be recovered for different purposes. it is therefore urgent that the commission should take up this matter, especially now that, after the failure of the copenhagen summit, environmental problems are at least taking a back seat.
mr president, the eurozone is experiencing an economic decline unprecedented in its history, the lowest growth in the world, the highest unemployment and a continuing decline in its competitiveness. this total failure was made evident by the recent sovereign debt crisis in greece, which will soon affect spain, portugal, italy and france, with the result that the populations of these countries will be impoverished on a widespread basis. you promised convergence and harmonization of european countries. today you are hurrying us towards social and political breakdown. you alone bear the responsibility for this ongoing tragedy, for by imposing a single, uniform and totalitarian monetary policy on such divergent economies, you have encouraged unbridled speculation in some and economic atony in others. how can spain, which had a 2% budget surplus in 2007, now have a 12% deficit if the ecb's single and uniform interest rate has not encouraged unprecedented property speculation in this country covered with empty houses? the whole european banking sector is in fact being contaminated by this new subprime crisis, the consequences of which are frightening. the only answer you have is to continue to err when you have failed in everything, by increasing the grip and powers of the european union by upstream control of national budgets and by imposing an unprecedented policy of austerity on the peoples of europe. errare humanum is, perseverare diabolicum. it is the same as saying that the devil is a liar.
