in writing. this proposal for a regulation lays down the measures necessary to protect the euro against counterfeiting. among other provisions, it provides for the obligation for credit institutions and a number of other economic agents, such as cash handlers, to check the authenticity of euro banknotes and coins they receive and intend to put back into circulation and to ensure the detection of counterfeits. the absence of a common framework for the authentication of coins results in practices which differ from one member state to another and cannot therefore ensure uniform protection of currency throughout the community. i worked closely with mr binev on this draft regulation as rapporteur for my political group. like him, i support the european commission's proposal, which i have approved by my vote.
in writing. following the entry into force of the lisbon treaty, the european parliament takes its full place in the european legislative process. the adoption of this report will inform the european parliament of any proposed amendment to the statute for delegated acts (article 290 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union). this is an important point because the european parliament must be able to take part in the debate on the technical adjustments which may be necessary in the list of goods benefiting from a temporary suspension of the autonomous duties of the common customs tariff on imports of certain industrial products into the autonomous regions of madeira and the azores.
in writing. to provide a framework for judicial cooperation in criminal matters, to facilitate investigations, to combat effectively crossborder crime: this is the object and purpose of international agreements on mutual legal assistance and in this case the agreement on mutual legal assistance in criminal matters between the european union and japan. the difficulties that a 'european investigator' (a judicial, police, customs authority, etc.) would have in seeking evidence in a third country are easily imaginable; the european union is also a major player in the fight against crime and today, globalisation and crossborder crime require cooperation between states, a regulatory framework, an 'operational interface' between the european union and third states in the criminal field. the added value of this agreement is undeniable: investigations, the acquisition of evidence, the collection of testimonies, the obtaining of 'bank documents', the identification or tracing of persons are just some of the areas where cooperation is now envisaged, under the auspices of the european union and japan, for greater efficiency and speed. the european parliament has therefore given its approval without difficulty to the conclusion of such an international agreement, and i warmly welcome this.
in writing. i would like to congratulate the rapporteur on this very good text which was voted on by a large majority in our assembly. as rapporteur for the opinion on trade registers for the committee on the internal market, i would like to stress the importance of such work. data on trade within the european union is crucial for the proper development and growth of our common market, and i look forward to the commission's legislative proposals on this subject. a mandatory participation of all member states in a common trade register would be beneficial to the union as a whole. however, this could only be done by taking care not to add additional administrative burdens to our businesses and by preserving the privacy of data which must be, in order to preserve a climate of trust.
in writing. the financial crisis continues to plunge europe and many parts of the world into stagnation, without politicians considering the keys to a way out of the crisis. and many of them even think that we just need to turn our backs for a while and the situation will return to what we had before september 2008. i don't agree with that. if we do not integrate the environmental option into our thinking pattern, the same causes will have the same effects. the environment is a chance to develop a new model of development. the sources of employment are considerable if we empower ourselves to be leaders in the sustainable economy.
in writing. the european union's cohesion policy plays a key role in developing the employment potential of a sustainable economy by helping to reduce regional disparities and boost the economy. in this context, the regional and local levels should make greater use of the european structural funds to take initiatives to create new sustainable jobs. the erdf contributes to the formation of regional clusters by bringing together research, innovation and infrastructure in the field of new technologies at local level. local and regional authorities are best placed and most competent to create the conditions for the growth of these centres, which can give a major impetus to local economic development and create new jobs in the regions. smes also play a key role in promoting innovation in europe. they should be encouraged to use the european social fund to develop entrepreneurial attitudes and skills. however, the lack of coordination between european, national and regional funding systems is an obstacle to the achievement of these objectives. it is therefore necessary to improve coordination at all levels in order to achieve greater synergy between the various common policies.
in writing. the development of green jobs in europe is a necessity. on the one hand, they support sustainable growth and on the other hand, they contribute to the ambitious numerical targets that the eu has set itself in the fight against climate change. i voted in favour of the report by my colleague, mrs elisabeth schroedter, which supports the introduction of measures to encourage them. in order to increase their numbers, companies must be encouraged to invest in clean technologies - i am thinking in particular of the introduction of tax relief for smes. the regions must also be encouraged to use the european structural funds and the cohesion fund to create new sustainable jobs. but it will be necessary to ensure that national training and education systems are adapted to meet the demand for skilled workers, as well as to ensure the re-skilling of those whose jobs are threatened by these structural changes in the economy.
in writing. free trade agreements allow the countries that sign them to enrich themselves through trade in a wide variety of products and to express their respective comparative advantages. i therefore look forward to the forthcoming conclusion of the free trade agreement between south korea and the european union. however, there is still a need to be extremely vigilant about the terms of trade agreements being prepared. in this context, any excessively rapid and potentially destabilising developments in trade flows must be avoided. to do this, a safeguard clause must be put in place, in particular to protect our car industry. in concrete terms, i welcome the adoption of this report because the european parliamentarians ask that in the event of import surges an investigation be opened at the request of a member state, the european parliament, the internal advisory group, a legal person or an association acting on behalf of the union industry and representing at least 25% of it, or at the initiative of the european commission. if it is found that european producers are suffering serious injury as a result of a large increase in imports of the product concerned, safeguard measures may be taken in the form of protective customs duties.
in writing. the european parliament has approved amendments to the safeguard measures that will accompany the free trade agreement (fta) with south korea. however, this is only a partial vote, the final vote having been postponed to the 18-21 october part-session, in order not to close the door to an agreement at first reading with the council. all the impact studies of the european commission already show a comparative advantage more favourable to korea than to the eu. the least we can expect from the commission is to present us with a credible safeguard clause. we believe that our request for regional safeguards should be taken seriously, because the impact of opening up to korean products can vary considerably from one member state to another in a market of 500 million inhabitants, whereas the impact of european exports to a country of 50 million inhabitants is much more predictable. it is equally essential to include a right of initiative of parliament and the industry concerned for the opening of a safeguard investigation, as well as an increased role for parliament to decide whether or not to take safeguard measures.
in writing. this agreement is the first trade agreement to be concluded after the treaty of lisbon, the first agreement to be endorsed by the european parliament, so it is important that the european parliament is heard. to mark the assertion of the european parliament's new powers in defining eu trade policy, we therefore voted the amendments proposed by the parliament's committee on international trade (inta), but we decided not to vote on the text of the resolution as a whole, in order to try to reach a better agreement with the council. a better agreement, for which several main points will have to be revised: we want a real safeguard clause, an effective clause which will cover regional distortions between the different states of the european union and which will above all prevent situations where a 'serious damage' to producers in the european union could occur; the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial interests are protected.
in writing. our farmers must be able to earn a living from their work, on the one hand, and to produce food that meets high quality standards, at an affordable price for the consumer, on the other. the report by mr bové, thanks to the work done in the committee on agriculture, is balanced and proposes some solutions to these challenges. strengthening producer organisations, proposing standard contracts in certain sectors, encouraging self-regulation initiatives, these are good ways of working in my view. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. in every agricultural crisis, this demand comes up again with insistent insistence from farmers and consumers alike: finally establish transparency of farmers' prices and incomes along the entire agricultural production chain. this report does exactly that, and we have every reason to be pleased with it. i regret, however, that the proposal to give preferential treatment to cooperatives, smes and producer groups in public procurement failed by only a few votes.
in writing. this report on food prices and farmers' incomes in europe was adopted by the european parliament on tuesday 7 september. this report is the result of a broad consultation of all the political groups, with a significant contribution from the epp. i welcome the proposals made to the european commission to give producers more say in their negotiations with distributors. i join the rapporteur in calling for european competition law to be adapted to avoid abuses of dominant positions. i think it is appropriate to propose the creation of standard contracts containing volume and price clauses, which will enable farmers to enjoy fair incomes. we need new market regulation, which gives the common agricultural policy the instruments to cope better with crises. as with fishery and aquaculture products, i am very committed to promoting quality products and sustainable production. it is therefore essential that products imported from third countries comply with the same requirements as european products, in order to avoid unfair competition.
in writing. the european parliament calls for fairer incomes for farmers as part of a better functioning food chain. the constant fall in farmers' incomes is unacceptable when, at the same time, the profits of the other players in the supply chain, the multinational distribution and marketing companies, are increasing. we therefore call on the european commission to take a number of concrete measures (combating dominant positions, unfair commercial and contractual practices, late payment, etc.) to restore a transparent, efficient economy, which guarantees a fair price for production and allows farmers to live off their activity.
in writing. the objective of a policy in favour of agriculture should not be merely to guarantee affordable or cheap prices for the consumer. it should also be to guarantee fair remuneration for farmers' work, to give priority to short circuits, to encourage consumers, producers, processors and distributors to think 'local and seasonal', quality products, etc. and to put an end to certain practices of large-scale distribution or intermediaries. we have had the opportunity to repeat this here many times: agriculture, because it feeds people, because it maintains landscapes, because it is the foundation of civilizations, is not an economic activity like any other. as such, the rules of competition, and especially the rules of international trade, should not be applied to it. it is scandalous to see agricultural raw materials, on which human lives depend, treated as financial products in highly speculative markets. mr bové's report is a step in the right direction. it is a pity, as the europeanist majority in this parliament demands, that it still largely fits within the erroneous conceptual framework of the european union and its dogmas.
in writing. i voted with determination for this text which calls on the european commission to take concrete measures to ensure that farmers receive fair incomes and that the food supply chain in europe is more efficient. this is an important vote because farmers do not receive a fair return for their produce and are often the first victims of sometimes abusive commercial practices. this text is a step forward because it indicates that the bargaining position of all the players must be rebalanced and that fair competition must be established everywhere in the food markets, in order to guarantee a fair income for farmers and ensure price transparency for consumers. i therefore welcome the adoption of this text, which is an important step forward for farmers and consumers. indeed, if we want to maintain a dynamic agriculture and if we want to have a good quality food supply chain in europe serving consumers, farmers must get more for what they produce.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text because the effects of 'contract' farming imposed by buyers are likely to weaken the bargaining position of farmers. new legislation is therefore needed to enhance the integration of primary producers with the other links in the chain and to ensure price transparency for consumers. the proposal to create standard contracts with volume and price clauses would allow producers to strengthen their bargaining position with the downstream. such model contracts could be useful instruments to prevent practices such as contract modification, late payment, and resale at a loss. in some sectors, such contracts should even become compulsory.
in writing. i voted for the bové report on food prices because we must ensure farmers' incomes while protecting consumers' purchasing power. the recent crises in many commodities, such as milk, have highlighted the plight of many farmers. the selling prices are falling and the producers are no longer able to make a decent living. at the other end of the chain, consumers never benefit from these price reductions when they occur, whereas, on the contrary, when prices rise, particularly because of speculation, these increases are immediately reflected in the final price. greater transparency in the role of intermediaries, and in particular of large retailers, is particularly urgent.
in writing. i am glad that this report makes the point of the disastrous state of european agriculture, but i am also sorry that the only proposal that is being made is to have more and more europe, more european laws and europeanist and bureaucratic interventionism. the european parliament has been a very active participant in the debate on the future of the european union, and it has been a very active participant in the debate on the future of the european union. a policy which has failed and has exacerbated rural desertification, the quasi-monopoly and unfair practices of the big distributors and buyers, the various forms of speculation which ruin our farmers. while it is more than necessary to support farmers to enable them to have a fair income in a food supply chain that is both secure, more efficient and of higher quality, common sense would also want this to be done at national level. we must renationalize the cap and not reinforce the liberal and globalist logic of the european commission
in writing. the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) aims to support workers, mainly in regions and sectors that have been disadvantaged by the opening up of the global economy. it is a potential annual allocation of €500 million for the reintegration of workers into employment. the financing and operation of the egf must be improved: they must be simplified in order to make its mobilisation easier and faster. that was the meaning of the amendments i tabled in the committee on economic and monetary affairs on this report. the gef must be an effective tool in a european social policy which is sometimes failing. i therefore believe that it should be maintained, while simplifying it, and i have therefore supported mr portas' report.
in writing. the globalisation adjustment fund aims to offset the negative consequences of globalisation for the most vulnerable and least skilled workers who have lost their jobs for economic reasons. this is all the more necessary in the current economic crisis. the added value of the globalisation adjustment fund is the visible, specific and temporary nature of its financial support for personalised vocational reintegration programmes. it is essential that the derogation introduced in june 2009 to help workers who lose their jobs as a result of the economic and financial crisis be extended until the end of the current multiannual financial framework. in order to speed up and simplify procedures, it is also necessary to ensure more effective coordination between the commission and the european parliament, so as to reduce the time taken for decision-making. the commission should therefore take parliament's timetable into account and inform it in good time of the difficulties it encounters in assessing member states' applications. finally, it is desirable that the commission should be more accountable for the use of the fund by regularly transmitting to the european parliament information on the implementation of financial contributions by the member states.
in writing. in the context of the mid-term review of the union's financial instruments, i voted in favour of this resolution because the committee on budgets has drawn up a report on the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf), a scheme to support the reintegration and retraining of workers for whom the link between redundancy and globalisation or the economic crisis is clearly established. for us socialists, the analysis of this report has revealed a sharp divergence of analysis between the right and the left. it is essential, from the socialist point of view, to make this fund sustainable, because globalisation has negative consequences for our entire industrial fabric, even beyond the crisis. on the contrary, the right-wing view is that this fund should be limited in time, to 2013, because globalisation can only be virtuous in its eyes in a stable economic context.
in writing. i voted for the portas report. i support its main objective, which is to make the egf sustainable, because beyond the crisis we are going through, globalisation has long-term negative consequences for our industrial jobs, which the european right refuses to accept. i also helped to amend this text so that smes and subcontractors are taken into account when the egf is granted. their employees are particularly vulnerable because of their dependence on multinationals, so it is essential that the egf offers them real prospects for vocational reintegration in the event of redundancy. i am also pleased that there is recognition of the need to carry out studies on the state bodies responsible for preparing the dossiers, in order to optimise the use of the egf, which is often unknown and little used, particularly in france. the european right has refused to extend the egf beyond 2013, so i will be mobilizing in the debate on the next financial perspective of the eu to ensure that it is maintained permanently.
in writing. as the mobilisation of funding for workers who have lost their jobs as a result of globalisation or the financial crisis should be accelerated, i voted in favour of a set of recommendations to improve the procedural and budgetary arrangements of the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf). this fund was established in 2006 but few applications were submitted, partly due to a complex intervention and co-financing criteria. that is why my colleagues and i wanted to make changes to this mechanism. this text therefore represents considerable progress, as it calls on the commission to simplify the procedure further in order to address the most obvious weaknesses and calls for a reduction in deadlines. in addition, until now, the fund has been financed from different budget lines. the text proposes a separate line for this in the 2011 budget which is an important development. i therefore welcome the adoption of these recommendations, which are essential at a time when our fellow citizens are being hit by the economic crisis.
in writing. although it is a rather technical report, the one we adopted yesterday in the european parliament's plenary session is very important in the ever more intensive construction of a european area of freedom, security and justice, a european judicial area and thus in the consolidation of the european internal market. the brussels i regulation has made enormous advances in the judicial field: it determines the courts with jurisdiction in civil and commercial matters in the event of crossborder litigation and governs the recognition and enforcement of judgments in civil and commercial matters from other member states. the aim is to revise the regulation to modernise its provisions and to improve certain procedures: communication between judges, authentic instruments, arbitration and, above all, the question of exequatur. without going into detail on these complex legal issues, i look forward to the revision of this regulation, a revision which will allow for better legal protection of european citizens: a better 'free circulation' of judgments and judicial decisions, more 'mutual trust' between the courts and judicial systems of the various member states, in other words a strengthening of legal security in europe and the rights of citizens.

in writing. presented in march 2010 by the european commission, the europe 2020 strategy is intended to set the eu's course for the next decade. if we can only regret the lack of involvement of the european parliament in the elaboration of the strategy, which was the work of mr barroso alone, there is one area in which parliament has a say: the integrated guidelines for employment. the 10 targets are to create more and better jobs, to strengthen decent work and to improve education and training systems. i therefore voted, with the majority of my fellow meps, on wednesday 8 september 2010, for a report which sets out these objectives and in which we call, in particular, for better use of the european social fund, for greater attention to the working poor and the fight against social exclusion, and for access to affordable and quality public services to be guaranteed. finally, if we want this strategy to be truly inclusive, we must ensure that these guidelines are consistent with cohesion policy.
in writing. parliament delivered its opinion on the integrated guidelines for employment. the 10 countries have set themselves the objectives of creating more and better jobs, strengthening decent work and improving education and training systems. parliament has taken action to ensure that the european social fund is better used, that greater attention is paid to the working poor and to the fight against social exclusion, and that access to affordable and quality public services is guaranteed.
in writing. with the unemployment rate in europe at 9.8%, with the labour market situation continuing to deteriorate and with the full effects of the economic crisis still to be felt, the european union needs to implement an ambitious european employment strategy. the european parliament has therefore adopted, as part of the eu 2020 strategy, employment guidelines for the member states: 10 guidelines on job creation, job quality, youth employment, employment of people belonging to vulnerable groups, the fight against social exclusion and the importance of optimum use of the european social fund. these are very ambitious objectives, but above all they are guidelines which must and will have to be implemented by the member states, and a strong signal from the european parliament to the member states at a time when employment is the most important concern and concern of our fellow citizens.
in writing. i voted in favour of the öry report on the guidelines for employment in the member states in the context of the eu 2020 strategy. the text strongly emphasises the priority of the fight against unemployment in a context of economic and social crisis. the text focuses on several elements: the employment rate must be raised to 75% across the union within 10 years, and a special effort must be made on the most vulnerable populations on the labour market: young people, the elderly, unskilled women, disabled people and people with immigrant backgrounds, who are most likely to be victims of discrimination in hiring and employment. the text also recalls the basic notions of decent work and the fight against poverty.
in writing. i voted for this report. as a representative of an overseas region, i can only be aware of the policies promoting employment and the fight against poverty, since the employment rates in the french overseas departments are the lowest in france (43.9% in réunion, for example, compared with 62.3% in all the eu member states). raising this figure from 10% in 2014 to 75% in 2020 is a goal i have always fought for. this is all the more so since it is aimed primarily at young people in difficulty, women and the disabled. the proposal also addresses poverty and aims to reduce by 25% the number of citizens living below the poverty line. these objectives should mobilise all the social and political forces, both french and european, so that the state can put in place the necessary means to achieve them within the time limits.
in writing. while the economic crisis has not yet had its full effect on unemployment rates, it is imperative that an ambitious european employment strategy is implemented. i agree with the council's objective of 75% participation of the european population in the labour market by 2020, but we need to go further. for example, the employment rate of vulnerable groups such as young people aged 15 to 25, older workers, unskilled women in the labour force and disabled people should be raised. or further reduce the school drop-out rate below the 10% mark. i also believe that the difficulty of integrating the longterm unemployed into the labour market must be the subject of specific policies, and i ask the council to give itself the means of reducing it by at least 10% within 10 years. to achieve this, as my colleague csaba őry proposes in his report, at least 25% of the longterm unemployed must be able to take part in an activation measure which may take the form of further training, training and/or retraining.

i'm the reporter. - mr president, european transport policy is not only about economic objectives, but also and above all about ensuring the highest standards of passenger safety. this is a goal to which we have moved closer in recent years and we still need to continue our efforts to ensure an optimal level of aviation safety. it is in this context that we are discussing today the draft regulation on the investigation and prevention of accidents in civil aviation. after several weeks of difficult negotiations, we managed before the summer to reach an agreement with the council at first reading, guaranteeing concrete progress in the field of investigation, accident prevention and care for the families of victims. if the text is confirmed by our votes tomorrow, it means that the measures provided for in the text can come into force by the end of 2010. (the president declared the common position adopted as amended) what measures are envisaged in this report? firstly, this regulation strengthens the independence of the safety investigation and the investigators. they will be guaranteed access to evidence and will be given the means to determine the causes of an accident. secondly, this text clarifies the role of the easa in the event of an air accident. it is clearly established that the agency, having a role as certifying authority, ...{another fuss in the chamber} well, i have the impression that nobody is interested. we can stop if you want, i can't even hear myself talk. (the president declared the common position approved as amended) it is clear that the agency, as a certifying authority, cannot under any circumstances investigate accidents itself because it cannot be both judge and party. however, it must be able to access the information necessary for the certification tasks and also to provide its expertise to the safety investigation. therefore, the regulation provides that in accordance with annex xiii to the chicago convention, easa will participate in the investigations as an advisor. the third step in the regulation is the creation of a network of safety investigation authorities, which formalises and strengthens the existing cooperation between member states. while having a flexible structure without legal personality, this network will improve the quality of safety investigations through, inter alia, increased cooperation between member states, sharing of good practices and improving the training of investigators. in addition, this regulation also deals with the relationship between judicial investigation and technical security investigation and, on this point too, the regulation makes concrete progress, despite the diversity of the judicial systems of the member states, first by guaranteeing immediate and unlimited access to evidence for security investigators, and secondly by establishing prior agreements between judicial authorities and investigation offices. finally, and this seems to me to be the most important, the protection of the victims and their families. the text stipulates that in the event of an accident, the list of passengers on board the aircraft must be available within two hours at the latest, which will reduce the painful wait of the families. the regulation also provides for a series of measures for the families of victims. this is the possibility, at the time of booking, to indicate a contact person to be notified in the event of an accident; the obligation to inform the families of the progress of the investigation before it is made public; confidentiality of the presence on board of a person if requested by his family; the appointment of a contact person to liaise with the families of the victims throughout the investigation; the obligation for member states to have an emergency plan in case of an accident; the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council adopt a common position on the proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work. finally, the obligation for all airlines serving the european union to have a minimum insurance policy to compensate the families of victims was recalled. the last important point of the regulation is the issue of occurrence reports, and this is a major advance in accident prevention, since the text provides that easa and the competent authorities of the member states have access to the database of aviation incidents. this database will be analysed so that preventive measures can be taken and accidents can be avoided. these are the main lines of the compromise. i would like to thank the fictitious rapporteurs very warmly, with whom we have had an excellent cooperation and who have enabled us to achieve this result.
for the gue/ngl group mr president, air transport is the safest mode of transport, as it is the one that has achieved the most spectacular results in reducing co2 emissions. we must therefore do everything to ensure that it remains so. the networking of the member states' accident and investigation offices is a good idea, provided that each of them remains under the control of the public authorities in order to avoid being subjected to the destructive notion of immediate and maximum profitability. the relocation of maintenance work outside the union, the counterfeiting of spare parts, the hiring of low-cost crews and, in some cases, the privatisation of air traffic control pose serious threats to safety. the union must intervene and assume its responsibilities in this area. it cannot simply publish blacklists and organise crash investigations. it must strike at the shareholders of airlines who fail to create the optimal safety conditions where it hurts them. it is true that some accidents are caused by human error, but these errors always reveal the shortcomings of certain airlines in terms of organization and working conditions, ergonomics, training and qualifications.

member of the commission. − mr president, honourable members, as we speak commissioner potočnik is in new york for the united nations discussions on the international year of biodiversity, so i am sure you will understand that he is unable to be here in person today. it therefore falls to me on behalf of the commission to thank mrs de lange for having prepared this very timely report on the protection of biodiversity and the implementation of eu nature legislation. i would like to highlight the word ‘timely’, as the eu is now at a political crossroads concerning its policy on biodiversity and nature protection. the commission shares meps’ deep concern about the extremely fast pace of human-induced biodiversity loss. the commission is aware of, and alarmed at, the huge degradation of the ecosystem services which biodiversity provides, and on which we all depend for our survival. since the 2010 target was adopted, we in the eu have accomplished a number of things of which we can be proud. the eu’s natura 2000 network of protected areas has expanded to cover almost 20% of the eu’s territory, and is still expanding both on land and at sea. despite this, however, we have failed to achieve our previous eu target of halting biodiversity loss by 2010. in spite of this failure and in spite of difficult discussions on an unprecedented economic crisis in europe, the spring european council endorsed a new biodiversity vision and target. our new target reflects a high level of ambition. it calls on the eu to half the loss of biodiversity and the degradation of ecosystem services by 2020 and restore them, where feasible, while stepping up the eu contribution to averting global biodiversity loss. in his speech on the state of the union, president barroso recently declared his commitment to this course, an issue to which he attaches the greatest importance and that needs to be tackled urgently. we know what the main challenges to meeting the targets have been. one of the key problems is the very nature of biodiversity policy itself. biodiversity is complex and cross-cutting. ownership of the problem is widely spread, and this diffusion has been a handicap, because in the end it boils down to the usual problem that when everyone is guilty, no one is to blame. this is a time of metamorphosis in the eu and many policies which have a very significant impact on biodiversity are in the process of being reviewed. this is the case of the common agricultural policy, the common fisheries policy and the cohesion policy. we are thus at a very important crossroads, where we can follow the right road by fully mainstreaming biodiversity in those policies and reach our ‘safe way home’, or we can make the mistake of taking another road and never reaching our final point – the agreed 2020 target – and face irreversible biodiversity loss and potentially catastrophic consequences. much is said in the resolution about the very worrying trends of biodiversity loss in europe and globally, the huge pressures exerted on species and ecosystems, the possible solutions, the value of ecosystem services and their very strong links with the millennium development goals and the fight against climate change. we have an enormous task ahead to preserve life on our planet, but we should not be discouraged by the magnitude of the challenge. the commission is certainly not discouraged and we will be developing a new eu strategy to deliver on the 2020 biodiversity target. the commission is also working on a communication on financing the natura 2000 network of protected areas. a better use of the available funding will certainly provide higher biodiversity and nature conservation benefits. we fully agree with the very strong emphasis included in the report on the crucial need to fully implement nature legislation, without which we will never be able to meet our new target. we look forward to the discussions with the members of parliament, with a view to working together to shape the package of measures that will allow us to attain our new biodiversity target. i should like to take this opportunity to welcome the very valued contribution to this debate provided by mrs de lange’s report.

madam president, i would have liked to have had mrs ashton or at least members of the council present for such an important debate. china -- and that's a good thing -- has decided to become a leader in green technology. 38% of its massive stimulus plan is invested in these new industries. it is already the world's leading producer and exporter of solar panels and wind turbines. this is a welcome development, which can help to reduce the level of pollution in china and the world, if production is carried out in accordance with wto rules. but it is not. chinese exporting companies are massively supported by state banks and municipalities. while some green technology markets are open to foreign companies and investment, many remain contingent and sometimes closed. subjected to this unfair competition, our european industries are threatened. commissioner, china is a signatory to the wto agreements. the european union must ensure that it strictly observes the rules.
madam president, i think it is really time to look at europe's relations with china and even to define a new strategy. i propose three directions. firstly, we need, as the president-in-office of the council said, reciprocity. one example: chinese companies cannot continue to set up in our country while our companies are barred from their public market. you have to choose. i therefore expect measures to be taken in this direction. secondly, the union cannot continue to tolerate social, health and environmental dumping without taking action, which is directly responsible for too many relocations from our european territory. and the commission should no longer regard the ridiculous cost of labour or the deplorable working conditions as 'natural competitive advantages'. i would urge the commission to change its doctrine on this point. thirdly, we cannot ignore the issue of human rights any longer, and beijing's overt support for iran, north korea or burma, for example, is clearly problematic. the objective of the european union has always been to promote the emergence of democracy and democracies. we must not give in on this issue either.
madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, first of all i agree with my colleague that the council is not present at this parliament's meeting. i think that is a bit reckless of the council, and i should like to say so myself. as we approach the next summit on 6 october, it is imperative that china and the european union make a determined attempt to move forward together on the issue of climate change. last year at this time we were already busy in this house urging europe to do everything possible to achieve an ambitious and binding agreement in copenhagen. we have seen that the result has not lived up to our hopes and ambitions. a year later, the worries are the same, if not even more acute. if we are to be able to persuade our partners today, we must show that our resolve is absolutely intact, that we are, for example, giving ourselves the means to honour our commitments to the countries of the south. to do this, the introduction of innovative financing - and i heard president sarkozy's speech at the un yesterday - is becoming a necessary matter. the introduction of a carbon tax at our borders, for example, is not to be excluded. it would act as an incentive mechanism for countries that are not going far enough in their climate commitment; i would like to thank the rapporteur for his report, which is a very good report and i hope that the commission will be able to support it.
in writing. i would like to express my deep disagreement with the way olaf is currently functioning. if fraud must be combated, it must be done in the service of european citizens and therefore in an independent, effective and respectful way of the protection of personal data of all citizens. as it stands, olaf is unable to meet these requirements. however, this text deals specifically with the conversion of precarious contracts into contracts of indefinite duration. no employee, in any organization, should be denied the right to a decent contract. i'll abstain from it.
in writing. e-commerce is an important contribution of the internet to economic activity. it is therefore important to remove the barriers to the single market in this sector, as the fragmentation of national legislation is holding back the dynamism of this profitable sector. i agree with the rapporteur that there are some shortcomings in the way consumers view online commerce. it is regrettable that 61% of crossborder transactions cannot be completed because online shops do not serve the country of the consumer concerned. in addition, users are concerned about the security of the payment system. the ability to make online purchases is generally conditioned by the quality of the internet connection. the priority should be to increase the number of internet users, in particular by improving the quality of the connection performance and an effort on the attractiveness of prices. it is also necessary to strengthen the confidence of online shoppers. like the rapporteur, i am in favour of the creation of a european trust label and better supervision of the internet, particularly in terms of the protection of personal data. particular efforts should also be made to protect minors using the internet.
in writing. i voted in favour of the arias echeverría report on e-commerce: e-commerce is one of the sectors with the greatest potential for growth and jobs in the coming decades, and the european union must exploit this potential to the full. it should also be noted that e-commerce facilitates and encourages the development of new niche markets for certain small and medium-sized enterprises that would not otherwise exist. i also support the idea that in developing our policies and regulatory frameworks relating to e-commerce, we pay particular attention to the needs of vulnerable consumers who would otherwise not have access to a wide range of consumer goods. i am thinking of people who are isolated or less mobile, citizens with low incomes or individuals living in less accessible, remote or peripheral areas. finally, i amended the text in committee to place more emphasis on the necessary development of consumer education tools online: we need to increase the digital skills of the greatest number of people, and improve their knowledge of their rights and obligations (main consumer rights on the internet, electronic commerce, data protection provisions in particular).
in writing. i could not vote for this report, even though it contains a number of positive elements, in particular on the defence of consumer interests and the consideration of the interests of smes in the e-commerce market. i particularly condemn the praise given to the commission for implementing the 3rd postal services directive which aims at liberalising these services and which will lead to further deterioration of the postal service in the eu, not, as the report claims, lower prices and better services. i cannot also deplore the fact that some member states have not yet transposed the services directive, because i hope that the commission will be able to quickly draw up a report to show the climate consequences of the implementation of this text. i regret that this text is largely in the spirit of openness to competition which we denounced in our rejection of the lisbon treaty.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report, which aims in particular to improve the prevention of air accidents and the assistance to victims and their families. i fully support the rapporteur's approach, which calls for an analysis of the incidents at european level, which has not been done so far. the report also proposes improvements in the assistance to victims and their families, such as the introduction of a maximum of two hours for the families to be informed of the names of passengers on board. the ball is now in the hands of the transport ministers, who will, i hope, adopt this legislation as soon as possible.
in writing. air traffic has grown tremendously in recent years. despite many technological improvements, the risk of accidents has increased. it is therefore essential to adapt community legislation on this subject. i therefore welcome the proposals by mrs christine de veyrac to adapt the 1994 directive on accident prevention to the current situation on the aviation market. the creation of a network of national investigating authorities will reduce the disparities between member states, in particular through pooling resources and sharing good practice. the rights of victims and their families must also be protected. i agree with the rapporteur that the obligation for airlines to provide passenger lists within one hour of the announcement of an accident applies not only to community airlines but also to all airlines operating in europe. finally, i welcome the rapporteur's proposal to define the european aviation safety agency as an 'adviser' in relation to its participation in safety investigations. it is important that the regulation does not give the agency the means to be both judge and party in safety investigations.
in writing. strengthening the independence of safety investigations in the event of an aircraft accident, better support for the families of the victims, optimal protection of data and privacy during these investigations; the commission has already taken a number of measures to improve air safety and these are the reasons why i voted in favour of this report. i voted enthusiastically for this text, which provides in particular that airlines must produce the list of passengers on board the aircraft within two hours of an accident, in order to inform the families. in addition, the establishment of a european network of safety investigation authorities is a very good thing in that it will make it possible to formulate recommendations on aviation policies and regulations but also and above all to pool resources and share good practice. this is therefore an important text and i welcome this important step forward in ensuring ever higher standards of passenger safety.
in writing. i support the report by christine de veyrac which aims to improve safety in civil aviation. in this context it is essential that the exact causes of incidents and accidents be brought to light. this requires that the independence of the investigations be guaranteed, that they be carried out without any pressure from the authorities responsible for regulating or certifying air operations, which may be held liable in the facts. the networking of civil aviation safety authorities in europe will also promote best practice through the exchange of information and the recommendations made by this network will help to improve european regulations in this field. the text also includes provisions to ensure that the families of victims are better taken into account in the event of an accident, such as the obligation for airlines to produce a list of all persons on board within two hours of the announcement of an accident and the prohibition on making this list public without informing the families and only if they do not object. these are two important advances, and i welcome them.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because it aims to improve the independence and transparency of investigations into air incidents and accidents. i welcome the adoption of this text, which should speed up the conduct of investigations and improve the information of the victims' families, while guaranteeing the privacy of individuals through welcome provisions. this text thus responds to the requests of the families of victims faced with investigations that often leave them destitute. this new community legislation should make it possible to provide better information to families whose members have been victims of an accident. the commission has already taken a number of measures to protect the privacy of passengers, such as the obligation to inform the family within two hours, and the obligation for airlines (community and non-community) to provide the authorities with the list of passengers on board the aircraft. the text adopted will also improve and speed up the conduct of investigations without pressure by the authorities responsible for regulating or controlling the aviation sector, by providing access to the various flight documents and by making the final investigation report obligatory for publication no later than 12 months after the incident or accident in question.
in writing. we all remember the gas crises of 2006, 2008 and 2009. they had led to the cutting off of gas supplies to millions of europeans, who were collateral victims of the disagreement between russia and ukraine. i welcome the work done by members on this subject. this resolution allows for network interconnection and better crisis management. for me, this is a great symbol of what european solidarity can be. together, in solidarity with each other, we are stronger, that's obvious.
in writing. the security of gas supply to the union is one of the essential dimensions of the necessary development of a european energy strategy. in the current context of energy dependence, it is important to bring together producers, distributors, consumers and public authorities to speak with one voice and not to make the union the weak link in energy geopolitics. in this respect, i agree with the rapporteur in welcoming the proposal for a regulation to guarantee the security of gas supply. this regulation, in combination with the legislation on the internal energy market, will contribute to reducing the union's vulnerability to external supply disruptions. it will also strengthen the leadership of european gas companies in the world. the rapporteur stresses the essential role of companies in managing gas crises. i support his call for their role in the early warning system to be strengthened. as regards the declaration of a community emergency, i agree with the rapporteur that the 10% threshold proposed by the commission does not cover the possible 100% supply disruption in certain areas. it should therefore be possible to declare a community emergency for a specific geographical area.
in writing. reducing the eu's energy dependence must be the first priority of our common energy policy. the means to achieve this are known and coincide with the commitments made to combat climate change: to achieve 20% energy savings - in particular by improving our energy efficiency - and to increase the share of renewable energy to 20% by 2020, while diversifying our energy sources. europe must also guarantee energy solidarity to each of its members, and to this end it must improve the management of the gas and oil stocks of the member states and provide for the construction of infrastructure to deliver energy to countries threatened with shortages. we need a european public policy, jointly funded by the european union and the member states, to meet the energy and environmental challenge, but also to help create growth in the coming decades.
in writing. this text makes natural gas a common commodity. it's not a real one. it is an energy resource and therefore a common human good. it has the distinctive feature of being fossil. for these two reasons, it must be used with the parsimony required to protect our ecosystem and with due regard for the general interest of european citizens and of humanity. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. but to try to impose the continuation of this logic even in the event of a supply disruption is to make fun of european citizens! it is high time to create a public energy hub to serve the european citizens.
in writing. we all remember the suspension of gas supplies from russia to ukraine in the winter of 2008-2009, which had the dramatic consequence of depriving 17 member states of gas supplies, leaving many citizens without heating, even when outdoor temperatures were at their lowest. we must do everything we can to prevent this from happening again ! i voted in favour of the report by my colleague, mr alejo vidal-quadras, on the legislative proposal on the security of gas supply in europe. i welcome the introduction in the new legislation of a guarantee of supply to so-called 'protected' customers (such as homes and essential services such as hospitals) by gas companies for a period of 30 days in the event of a crisis. this is a real breakthrough. in addition, the possibility for the european commission to declare a 'union emergency' or a 'regional emergency' will facilitate the establishment of rapid and coordinated measures to resolve, as soon as possible, any future crisis.
in writing. the european parliament has approved a readmission agreement between the eu and pakistan, which will facilitate the deportation of the many pakistani nationals who are in europe illegally. while agreements with third countries are needed to define the procedures for the readmission of persons in europe illegally, the case of pakistan is a special one. islamabad has not yet ratified the 1951 geneva convention relating to the status of refugees. the agreement also covers people who have transited through pakistan, including many afghans who can now be more easily returned to the war-torn country they fled. this is not acceptable. in addition, this summer's floods have plunged pakistan into one of the biggest crises in its history. the current situation does not allow for safe return to this country which is already struggling to accommodate huge numbers of displaced persons. the construction of a humane and reasonable immigration policy is a key social issue which must be conducted in accordance with the rule of law: that is why, pending pakistan's ratification of the geneva convention, i did not support this readmission agreement.
in writing. i voted against the eu-pakistan readmission agreement. this is the 12th agreement of its kind, but the first to be ratified by the european parliament. however, despite our many requests to the european commission, no evaluation or assessment of the previous agreements has been provided, which would have allowed us to have clear ideas about the conditions for implementing these agreements. more specifically in the case of pakistan, whose political situation is very sensitive, this agreement is questionable in many respects. pakistan, not known for its scrupulous respect for human rights, is not a signatory to international conventions on refugees or stateless people. this should have been a sine qua non condition in the negotiation. in addition, there are still many areas of uncertainty in the agreement: there is no guarantee that minors will be excluded from its scope, and the procedures and deadlines are unclear. in approving this agreement, the european parliament not only sets an unfortunate precedent, but has also missed an opportunity to show the image of an institution concerned with respect for human rights and desirous of greater transparency around these agreements.
in writing. the assembly has repeatedly condemned pakistan for its discriminatory policies and the persecution of afghan refugees. just a month ago, terrible floods brought millions of pakistanis onto the roads. this agreement ignores all human reality. not only does it contravene article 13 of the universal declaration of human rights, but like any such agreement, it is also contrary to the principles of refugee protection in the convention. voting for such a text would be a denial of international law and of the humanism which the eu still claims to be the heir to. i vote against it.
in writing. this is the first time since the entry into force of the lisbon treaty that the european parliament has voted on a readmission agreement. these agreements are symbolic of the migration policies that are building a fortress europe, which are driving out people driven by poverty and war seeking refuge on our territory. parliament now has the tools to force the council and the commission to put their words into action. the agreement submitted to us has many shortcomings and contains no guarantees as to the situation of those who will be returned to that country. we are well aware of the human rights situation in pakistan, which is not even a signatory to the 1951 geneva convention. the gue-ngl group calls for an evaluation of the existing readmission agreements as it would highlight the devastating effects of these policies which despise human beings who did not have the chance to be born on the territory of the union. the european parliament is not going to be left out of this vote. today he has lost the opportunity to make his voice heard on the actual implementation of the human rights speeches.
in writing. turkey has been part of a customs union with the european union since 1996, and economic and trade relations between the two have been very developed. turkey is the seventh largest trading partner of the european union, while the european union is turkey's largest trading partner. such exchanges should be strengthened. however, these must continue to be beneficial to both parties. that is why i voted in favour of the amendments of my political group, the epp, calling for more reciprocity. turkey must stop using the anti-dumping instrument for protectionist purposes, must challenge its technical barriers to trade and better enforce intellectual property rights.
in writing. we have approved the efd resolution, which is not satisfactory. but it clearly states that the deepening of the current eu-turkey relations replaces and makes turkey's membership of the european union obsolete. however, any further deepening of relations between the eu and cyprus should be closely dependent on the eu's recognition of cyprus, which it continues to refuse and whose territory it illegally and militarily occupies. turkey, a proud country and former ally against the communist threat, is a bridge between europe and asia. it is a bridge, but it is not a european country, geographically, demographically, historically or culturally. finally, it should be noted that the promises made in ankara in 1963, in the midst of the cold war and for strategic reasons, no longer have any meaning, and that we would waste less time, turks and europeans alike, thinking about a privileged partnership than about an accession which our citizens do not want and which many turks also oppose.
in writing. mr metin's report would have us believe that the customs union, which emerged from the eec-turkey association agreement of 1963, would be a success in terms of economic and commercial integration between the present european union and turkey. that this would have helped to support european growth, and hence french growth... not only has turkey failed to meet its commitments in this process, but over the decades we have seen the phenomenon of relocations and massive job losses. this is far from being an economic and social asset for our country and our european neighbours in the context of the globalist concert. but instead of acknowledging this, the report goes so far as to criticise the use of national technical rules and standards to protect national markets. the rapporteur considers these to be excessive anti-dumping measures, thus hampering turkey's trade with europe. all this is of course in the direction of strengthening the process of turkey's accession to the european union. this time, from the point of view of industrial and commercial profit for the europeans, globalists and ultra-liberals who are greedy for profit. of course, we reject anything that might lead to that.
in writing. turkey, like all states, is a sovereign state and as such must be respected. it is unacceptable that the european union should allow itself to threaten to stop the accession negotiations, which are otherwise undesirable for the necessary social and fiscal harmonization from above. this house would be unworthy of the friendship of the turkish people if it voted for a text which obliges them to destroy their agricultural jobs (50% of jobs in turkey) by abolishing all taxes on agricultural products and which makes the rights of investors prevail over those of the people. i am voting against this text.
in writing. this own-initiative report deplores the lack of progress in the protection of biodiversity. due to a lack of political will, funding, transposition of european legislation, etc., the absolute minimum target of halting biodiversity loss set for 2010 has not been reached and is being postponed to 2020. the report then lists the measures to be taken to ensure that this essential objective is met. concerned about the state of our environment and supporting the approach proposed by the rapporteur, esther de lange, i voted in favour of this text.
in writing. the current rate of biodiversity loss is alarming. the rapporteur believes that the rate at which species are becoming extinct is between 50 and 1000 times faster than the natural rate. at european level, the natura 2000 network aims to contribute to biodiversity by conserving natural habitats and species of wild fauna and flora. the rapporteur rightly regrets, however, the differences which still exist between the member states in the transposition and interpretation of the natura 2000 directives. the fragmentation of funding in the field of biodiversity is also a problem. most of the expenditure is spread over the eafrd, the common fisheries policy, cohesion policy and the seventh research framework programme. synergies will have to be found in the next multiannual financial framework. finally, i welcome the recent commission communication on a long-term strategy for biodiversity. it is desirable that this communication and the consultation which it entails should lead to the formulation of precise policy objectives and the implementation of relevant actions at european level.
in writing. the figures for the evolution of biodiversity are extremely worrying. by 2050, species extinction could increase tenfold. in europe, 42% of mammals, 43% of birds, 45% of butterflies, 30% of amphibians, 45% of reptiles and 52% of freshwater fish are threatened with extinction. this is not acceptable, not only from an ethical point of view, but also from an environmental and economic point of view. the european commission must therefore ensure that biodiversity is better integrated into its various policy areas, including agriculture, regional policy, industry, development cooperation and research and innovation. the union should also aim to strengthen international efforts to halt the loss of biodiversity and thus contribute to the achievement of the millennium development goals by 2015. the european parliament has almost unanimously adopted this report and will have to act accordingly when we debate the reform of the common agricultural policy, the fisheries policy or the new financial perspectives.
in writing. i voted in favour of this own-initiative report because the european union must do everything possible to halt the loss of biodiversity by 2020 and restore ecosystems. i deeply regret that the target of halting biodiversity loss by 2010 has not been met. the european commission must ensure that biodiversity is better integrated into other areas of union action, in particular agriculture, forestry, fisheries, regional and cohesion policy, industry, development cooperation and research and innovation. our public spending alone will not achieve the union's main objective, which is why corporate social responsibility must also integrate this biodiversity dimension.
in writing. 80% of the french republic's biodiversity is found in its overseas territories (upe and oct). 42% of the territory of the island of reunion has just been classified by unesco as a world heritage site. these are objective reasons for the need for the european union to make a special effort to protect biodiversity and to exploit its real potential in the octs and the overseas countries and territories. however, the french outermost regions and all the octs of europe are not eligible for the natura 2000 and life+ programmes. this gap should be corrected. that is why i have proposed that a special budget line be included in the draft budget for 2011. this budget line will create a specific programme, called best, for the oct and the ors for the protection and enhancement of biodiversity. this programme was promoted after the reunion conference and supported by the european council under the french presidency. it is time to make this initiative a reality.
in writing. human activities are causing biodiversity to decline at an unprecedented rate. in europe, nearly half of all mammals are threatened, and the situation is similar for birds. if this evolution continues at the rate observed in recent decades, it will leave a natural environment irreversibly damaged. i am deeply concerned about the current situation, and while the international political agenda does not give the urgency it should to combat the loss of biodiversity, i support the report by my colleague esther de lange. the text proposes several ways of strengthening the fight against biodiversity loss in europe and calls for specific policies to support investments - both public and private - that have a positive impact on biodiversity, while those that are harmful to it must be discouraged. to be truly effective, it is clear that this eu fight must be accompanied by action at international level, and it is imperative that the commission and the member states support the integration of biodiversity protection into global processes, such as the millennium development goals.
in writing. 2010 was supposed to be the year when the european union finally had to take care of biodiversity. it is clear that its strategy in this area has been a fiasco despite its repeated commitments since 2001, in particular to deal with the risks of extinction of many species. i therefore supported the report by mrs de lange, which was adopted by the european parliament on 21 september. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover all the activities of the european union. it adopted three key measures, which it called for to be implemented as a matter of urgency: an integrated approach to biodiversity in all relevant sectoral policies (agriculture, fisheries, transport, etc.), the application and enforcement of community environmental legislation by the member states, and increased funding for measures in this field beyond the life instrument. at present, member states do not provide sufficient support for life projects. beyond that, it is about raising awareness among our citizens of the state of biodiversity and the serious risks to ecosystems. only 17% of european citizens are aware that biodiversity is in serious decline.
in writing. storm xynthia, floods in madeira, forest fires in greece, etc. europeans are regularly tested by natural disasters with incalculable human and economic consequences. this own-initiative report recalls that an anticipatory approach is more effective and less costly than an approach consisting simply of responding to disasters and sets out a list of actions to be taken. i voted in favour of this report because i think it is very useful and that the european commission should draw inspiration from it as soon as possible, particularly as regards forest fire prevention. the next step for me will be to set up a european civil protection force to help states cope with major natural disasters.
in writing. in the first six years of the european union solidarity fund, 62 applications for financial assistance were submitted. almost a third of these were natural disasters, which were classified as "major disasters". i am pleased, for example, with the assistance provided by the solidarity fund in my region of brittany following the storm xinthia. european solidarity is essential to manage the economic, social, environmental and human consequences of natural disasters in the best possible way. the rapporteur recalls that disaster prevention must be a priority for cooperation between member states in this field. it is therefore proposed to create a network of national, regional and local authorities to exchange good practice on prevention measures. i also agree with the rapporteur that we should create a financial framework at union level for the prevention of natural disasters, in order to strengthen and coordinate existing instruments. cohesion policy plays a leading role in disaster prevention. it contributes to reducing disparities between regions in this area, in particular by improving the capacities of regions particularly exposed to risks.
in writing. after the 2004 indian ocean tsunami, the january 2010 haiti earthquake and the february 2010 xynthia storm, how many more tragedies will it take before we finally have a community approach to natural disaster prevention? natural and man-made disasters are becoming more frequent, and it is therefore necessary to ensure that national measures are more effective and better coordinated and that european measures are more flexible. beyond prevention, i would like to remind you that there is a michel barnier report on the table since 2006 for the establishment of a rapid reaction force for natural disasters: what are we waiting for to adopt it? what are we waiting for to apply it?
in writing. fires in portugal, floods in saxony, forest fires in greece, xynthia in western france - these last years have shown us how necessary and beneficial a genuine european strategy for dealing with natural disasters is: a strategy for prevention but also a strategy for the european union's response and capacity to react to such disasters. i therefore voted in favour of this report, which calls for a comprehensive, coordinated and balanced european approach in this area, based on the fundamental principle of european solidarity. i very much hope that the commission will soon present concrete proposals to strengthen cooperation and exchange of practices between member states in this field, to enable a better networking of the competent authorities, to improve procedures, to facilitate a quicker triggering of the european solidarity fund and above all to ensure that disaster prevention is included in the next financial perspective of the european union.
in writing. in recent years, the member states of the european union have been the victims of a considerable number of natural and man-made disasters: fires, storms, floods, droughts, etc. the human, economic and social costs of these disasters, which are often transnational, are dramatic. i believe that it is essential to consider the prevention of these disasters at european level, and i support the report by my colleague, mr joão ferreira. while cooperation between member states and pooling of resources should be increased in order to increase the effectiveness of prevention mechanisms across the union, the cross-cutting integration of prevention of these disasters into eu policies should also be improved. in addition, better coordination and cooperation between member states in the field of research and development in the prevention of natural or man-made disasters should be encouraged.
in writing. in the context of the international summit on the achievement of the millennium development goals in new york and the adoption by the european parliament of the report on poverty reduction in developing countries, it seems important to me to emphasise the role that microcredit can play in achieving these goals. microcredit generally consists of small loans to entrepreneurs who cannot access conventional bank loans. in developing countries, it is the basis for many micro-economic projects that promote wealth creation and, consequently, development. grassroots project financing helps to create economic networks in the countries concerned and involve small local actors. microcredit makes it possible to make these actors responsible for their own development and to reduce their dependence on conventional development aid. by reaching sectors as diverse as agriculture, craft industries and the social economy, microcredit can thus have a real impact on local development. i therefore call on the european commission and the member states to give serious consideration to this responsible form of development aid.
in writing. the united nations summit on the implementation of the millennium development goals opened yesterday. although some progress has been made, we are still far from the target set for reducing poverty by 2015. the first imperative to achieve this is job creation in developing countries, whereas according to a recent joint report by the imf and the ilo, there were more than 210 million unemployed people worldwide in 2010, with the crisis having led to the loss of 30 million jobs since 2008. the ilo calls for employment to be seen no longer as a consequence of other policies but as a primary objective and pillar of growth strategies. sustainable development, support for employment and decent work require support for diversification of the economy, respect for ilo standards, the right to a social protection base for all, investment in public services, and the provision of basic needs such as access to water, health and food security. more employment will also be a condition for stability and the strengthening of democracy. that's the meaning of the theocharous report.
in writing. this report is acceptable. although it does not call into question trade liberalization and relies on the wto, a considerable number of the measures proposed are likely to improve the living conditions of the citizens of the countries of the south. the promotion of social protection systems, the integration of the social economy into cooperation agreements, the defence of a quality health system for all and free access for all to basic, higher and vocational education, the defence of access to drinking water, the encouragement of respect by the eu for the electoral choices of the population are, among other things, to be credited to this text. it even advocates the establishment of independent parliaments with real legislative, budgetary and control powers. the implementation of such recommendations might help to ensure that the laudable intentions of this own-initiative report are respected.
in writing. i abstained on this report, which contains contradictory provisions to say the least. on the one hand, it calls for a review of privatisation policies, particularly in public services, and supports investment measures in favour of these, affirms the positive impact of squats and the social economy on development, and notes the need to implement the ilo conventions on international labour standards. but at the same time the majority of parliament has adopted a paragraph which calls, which i find unacceptable, for the member states and the commission to respect the foundations of the free market.
the commission's vice-president - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner dalli regrets that he cannot be here tonight to discuss this matter himself and i ask you to excuse him. i am, however, pleased to replace it with the formal adoption of a first reading agreement on the important issue of pharmacovigilance. let me take this opportunity to thank all those who worked tirelessly to get this agreement, including the rapporteurs, co-rapporteurs, non-rapporteurs and especially mrs mcavan, rapporteur for the committee on the substance. the proposal which will be put to the vote in parliament tomorrow will improve patient protection against the adverse effects of medicines. the pharmacovigilance system for medicinal products for human use in the european union will be strengthened and modernised. it will not only provide better protection for public health, but it will also ensure the proper functioning of the internal market and streamline existing regulations and procedures. in addition, the legislation will increase transparency and patient participation in the field of pharmacovigilance. finally, with the new scientific committee on pharmacovigilance set up within the european medicines agency, the ema will ensure access to the most advanced scientific and medical know-how to assess the safety of medicines and to recommend risk mitigation measures. the commission is very pleased that a pre-negotiated common position was reached between the institutions before the summer holidays and fully supports the substance of the agreement reached. under this agreement, the proposed amendment to raise the grade of the director of the ema has been withdrawn and the commission will issue the following statement:'in response to the request of the european parliament and the council concerning the grade of the director of the european medicines agency, the commission, in order not to delay the adoption of this important proposal, undertakes to re-publish the vacancy notice for the recruitment of the next director of the ema to the grade ad/15 instead of ad/14. the commission considers that this issue should be addressed in the context of
