mr president, i would like to congratulate our rapporteur, mrs mcavan, on her work. first reading agreements are no longer really relevant in this house because they often lead, it is true, to reducing the power of parliament, but this is undoubtedly a very good first reading agreement. i must also say that our fictitious rapporteur, mrs parvanova, has done an excellent job. the progress made is not insignificant, particularly in a field which is dear to me: that of transparency. for me, transparency should be the rule, and access restriction the exception. this is absolutely essential if we want to move towards a counter-expertise that is developing. the right to keep proprietary information secret must not be exercised to the detriment of health and environmental information. that is why i tabled several amendments aimed at ensuring a high level of transparency. i would have preferred to go further, but the result is already satisfactory. on the text itself, one provision which might seem anecdotal, but probably is not is important: it is the request to the commission to look into the question of water and soil pollution by pharmaceutical residues, accompanied by an assessment to measure, if necessary, the impact of this legislation.
mr president, commissioner, we are discussing pharmacovigilance. this is an important pillar of the pharma package we have been working on for some time, and this first reading agreement will help to protect patients better against the risks associated with the use of medicines. this agreement is therefore a major step forward for patient safety, as rare features can be detected more quickly and unsafe medicines can be withdrawn from the market more quickly, if necessary. in reality, it is not a question of reinventing pharmacovigilance, but simply of improving things by means of a better knowledge of the risks associated with medicines, through greater cooperation between the competent authorities. the interest of this regulation is to improve knowledge of adverse reactions through the development of the eudravigilance database within the european medicines agency, which will become the single entry and consultation point for all information related to a medicinal product. this will improve communication between the competent authorities. national authorities will also have a greater capacity to reassess the benefit-risk balance, by reactively capturing and integrating any signals or new data, and to adapt information to healthcare professionals and patients accordingly. but you also need to be careful not to frighten the patient with exaggerated admonitions. the commission has already taken steps to ensure that the information is not used in a way that would be harmful to the consumer. a drug is a complex product. it is important to explain, to inform and above all not to alarm. it is clear that today the leaflet has lost its relevance. it's sometimes hard to read. we should now consider how to develop it, together with all the partners, in order to better understand patients and, above all, to give patients confidence in the medicine.
mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, pharmacovigilance, which consists of analysing the side effects of medicines and requesting their withdrawal from the market in the event of an alert, has attracted little interest amongst the pharmaceutical industry. this is a matter of vital importance for the safety and quality of our health systems, and i cannot - as much as i am pleased to see you, commissioner - but regret the absence of mr dalli. because i was appalled by the commission's proposals, which put pharmacovigilance systems at risk for the benefit of the pharmaceutical companies. fortunately, the work of parliament and the council has led to some improvement in the situation. this will not make it possible to generalize the granting of advance marketing authorizations for new medicinal products. progress in transparency is also welcome. but i think this agreement represents a missed opportunity to improve pharmacovigilance and i am particularly concerned about the lack of guarantees of system independence. thus, while the role of the committee for risk assessment is strengthened, it is not entirely independent of the european committee for the grant of marketing authorisation. but as we know from experience, this committee is reluctant to reverse its decisions. as for the national structures, there is absolutely nothing on the subject. secondly, i regret that member states do not have to report any conflicts of interest of experts in the european committee. finally, and most importantly, this agreement puts an end to the best guarantee of independence, namely public funding for pharmacovigilance activities, which will now be financed mainly by private fees. i congratulate mrs mcavan on the progress made on the commission's original proposal, but in view of certain problems i wonder why this dossier should have been closed in one reading, when, given time, we could have strengthened patients' confidence in quality and safe pharmaceutical products.
mr president, i would like to return to the environmental impact of medicines. since 1965, europe has set three criteria for obtaining marketing authorization, namely efficacy, safety and pharmaceutical quality of the medicinal product, but nothing on the impact of medicinal products on the environment. but you know that right now, estrogen found in river water changes the sex of fish. you also know that there are also high levels of drug residues in sewage treatment plants and in hospital waste water. we had a lot of talk about it. there was a debate and in the pharmacovigilance directive this was finally taken into account in the form of a recital, which asks the commission, on the basis of data provided by the european medicines agency, the environment agency and the member states, to publish a report on the scale of the problem and an assessment of the desirability and usefulness of amending the european union legislation on medicines or in other areas. what i am asking the commission to do is to report on the basis of these data, because indirectly this affects human health, since in many cases it is the consumption of water that has caused the side effects that have been observed.
mr president, commissioner, i would like to make a brief statement to congratulate all those who have worked on this subject and to express my surprise at the fact that one point has not been dealt with, namely cross-pharmacovigilance. indeed, in vertical, single-product, the report is extremely comprehensive and the work is remarkable. however, most of the problems are due to prescription medication, as 92 per cent of patients are treated in multiple rounds. a drug that, vertically, has no particular side effects, will have highly toxic side effects if it is crossed with another drug. it is of the utmost importance that we have a database of drug cross-reactions, which is available to professionals and patients alike. this is all the more necessary as many patients have prescription treatments to which they add self-medication, without any indication, in general, on the capacity for sometimes highly toxic cross-effects. i think that this subject has been touched upon but not dealt with, and that is extremely regrettable.
on behalf of the alde group. mr president, thanks to the work of everyone, and in particular the rapporteur, we have achieved at least one objective: that of having reached, after very difficult discussions, agreement on the key point of the authorization procedure. our position on this issue was common sense. the aim was to ensure the sustainability of the system, i.e. to avoid echa being overburdened with a single application and unable to respond, and to promote a system which encourages low-risk products. the compromise reached on this point is balanced. it gives both time to time, since the system has four years to set up, and a premium to the least dangerous products. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. the toxicity of certain products, such as pesticides, is obvious and i fully agree with what mr jørgensen has said about the impact on health and the environment of a number of products. for this reason, we reject any provision which could lead to questioning the quality of product evaluation or to undermining the system of incentives for substitution of substances of very high concern. that is why a series of amendments which have just been tabled are completely unbalanced and cannot be supported. do not be mistaken! this is the result of an arbitrage that prioritizes short-term interests over the protection of health and the environment. let us never forget that the health and the environment are not only the defence of our own values, but also the economic interest of the community in defending them.
for the greens/efa group mr president, i think there are some advances in this text, two of which are fundamental: the obligation to label the presence of nanoparticles in a product, and above all the fact that each of these nanosubstances will also be subject to a separate assessment, which is not the case at present. another breakthrough is the possibility of excluding endocrine disruptors from the substances used with concrete and really applicable exclusion criteria. but there is a but. we disagree on the concrete means for the european chemicals agency because this agency should normally be responsible for the evaluation and authorization of biocidal products. we want to extend echa's remit - which we agree with - but in this case it means giving echa the means to really do its job. we cannot ask echa to do much more, to reduce the time needed to evaluate substances, and at the same time to reduce its resources. otherwise we risk being faced with a lightweight assessment, which is quick but insufficient because it is too superficial. i therefore ask you, mrs klass, to reconsider your budget proposal for echa's tasks in this area. as it stands, i tell you, your proposal is not serious, and this will undermine the quality of the work of this european institution which is essential to the security of european citizens and consumers. this is a big issue. you cannot ask for more if there are no means for it, or else it will be an administrative agency that will respond to the industrial lobby.

madam president, the treaty of lisbon gives the european union new powers in new areas. it provides that the union must have the means necessary to achieve its objectives and carry out its policies. however, since the start of the current multiannual financial framework, annual budgets have generally only been able to be agreed on the basis of existing margins. as the rapporteur recalls, the margin has narrowed considerably and is not expected to increase by 2013; the crisis has passed through here. this leaves no possibility of meeting unforeseen needs. such a situation is dangerous, even intolerable. it is therefore essential to revise the multiannual financial framework in order to ensure the resources necessary for the implementation of the new competences provided for in the lisbon treaty. it is also important to allow the financing of the political priorities defined in the framework of the europe 2020 strategy, as our colleague mr kelly said just now. i would remind you, commissioner, that the treaty of lisbon has given parliament equal powers with the council in budgetary matters. parliament must therefore make its views known in the budget debate, as proposed by our colleague mr böge, whom i congratulate again on his report.

president of the european council. − mr president, the european council meeting of 16 september was convened primarily in order to focus on the union’s external relations. we also had a short scheduled discussion during lunch about the task force on economic governance, and an unscheduled discussion about the roma situation. allow me to address each of these in turn. first, regarding foreign affairs. when i took office eight months ago, while visiting our capitals i noticed a degree of frustration following the copenhagen summit. there was a perception that the european union was sidelined. our economic outlook was not good, whereas other economies in the world were growing rapidly. moreover, we started to realise how the economic strength of emerging countries is being transformed into real political power. the g-20, although created at the instigation of the european union, is also a sign of this trend, as is the debate about representation in the international monetary fund. this affects us: new players do not always share our interests and our world views. the lisbon treaty requires the european council to define the union’s strategic interests and give strategic direction to the work of other institutions. i am glad the heads of state and government all agreed to take this up and deepen their involvement in the union’s foreign policy. they want more ownership by the european council. they want to assume their responsibilities as members of this union institution. what did we discuss? well, it seemed urgent to me to address our strategic partnerships first. the issue was to link general objectives to concrete means, to make progress on the ground. we therefore briefly talked about how to make the best use of the lisbon treaty, with the new external action service. i would like to take this opportunity to thank parliament for its work in securing agreement on this. how can we make sure that what is done in brussels and in the capitals is going in the same direction? how can we coordinate better between the different actors in brussels? how can we bring together the different aspects of our relationship with partners – for instance during summits – in areas such as the economy, climate, values and security? the proof of the pudding is in the eating. how do we deal with our partners, one to one? we set priorities on a number of pressing matters. our key messages for summits with third countries have to be underpinned by some specific negotiations and trade-offs. i retain from the discussion in the european council the following other points: first, this is the beginning of a process. second, our key messages should be mandated by the european council, prepared and implemented by the foreign affairs council, the commission and the high representative, just as we are already preparing the g-20 meetings in the european council. my third point is that, with our partners, ‘reciprocity’ is a key word. we can also speak about ‘identifying mutual interests’. the general feeling is that this is not the case yet. we all insist on deliverables and leverage. we must turn objectives into concrete results. we have strategic partners but we need more strategy. we have developed ideas on how to position ourselves vis-à-vis china and where to fine-tune them further. thanks to the european council discussion, when other upcoming meetings as well: the g-20 summit in seoul and the eu-us summit, both to take place in november, both crucial for global economic prospects. we will further prepare these meetings at the european council of 28 and 29 october. the french president, as incoming chair, outlined some of his ideas for the g-20 in 2011. he received our full support for creating a new dynamic for the g-8/g-20, underlining that they should become a process, not just an event. on the middle east: the success of the middle east peace negotiations is of strategic interest for the european union. we adopted a specific declaration on this issue in line with our common position of december 2009. we are involved in the process via the quartet. our neighbourhood, for instance the western balkans and their european perspective and the eastern partnership are of the highest importance. our reputation in the world starts with stability on our own continent. if we want to be a global player we have to be a regional player. from now on we will discuss foreign policy in the european council in this spirit. we can only be credible and strong if we are united. we showed our unity in the position of the 27 on additional sanctions on iran, which was not self-evident, and in the very important un resolution on the dialogue between serbia and kosovo, extremely important for the western balkans. floods. more aid and more trade; we want pakistan to recover now and to develop economically. we will grant significantly-increased market access. catherine ashton helped us to reach agreement on this important declaration. second point, the task force. during the european council lunch we talked about the economy, the basis to gain political clout. in the first half of the year the european council had to involve itself in pressing economic issues. our economies are in better shape now, but the work is not over yet. during the lunch, i briefed my colleagues on the progress in the task force on economic governance. i did it yesterday here in the parliament. all heads of state and government want to continue the work and to keep the momentum. we have a large consensus on some of the most important issues, like the macro-economic surveillance framework. this will monitor and correct imbalances, risks of bubbles, and divergences in competitiveness. there is also agreement on council we will discuss the issue of integration of the roma. the prohibition of all forms of discrimination based on nationality or ethnicity is the founding principle of the european union. respect g-20. it is embedded in the institutional framework of the union but it brings to the union inputs from the highest political level in the member states and it gives the member states a sense of ownership and participation in the union and reinforces their commitment to its success. it comprises not only the heads of state or government but also the president of the european commission and bank, the euro group, and of course yourself, mr president, along with leaders of the political groups and chairs of the parliamentary committees, well beyond what is provided for in the treaty. we do indeed work in the general european interest. the efforts made by all european institutions over the last months have started to produce results. our economies are recovering at an unexpected pace. engaged in reform programmes. i pay tribute to those national governments who are taking courageous measures in very difficult political circumstances. in most of our member states the crisis is not in writing. i voted in favour of this report because i think it is unacceptable to want to make ridiculous savings on patient safety and product quality. the initial proposals of the european commission were to weaken the current system by giving companies a central role in collecting, alerting, analysing and reporting on the adverse effects of their medicines. but the foundation of efficacy and safety for patients is the independence of pharmacovigilance networks and committees. the compromise with the council includes improvements in transparency and, above all, prevents the placing on the market of medicines that have not been sufficiently tested, as originally proposed by the european commission.
in writing. today in the european union too many patients are still suffering from the side effects of medicines. that is why i voted for the adoption of this report which seeks to address this problem. the aim of the text is to set up national and european websites on which patients can report adverse reactions to medicines and thus create a database. in the interests of transparency, a black symbol will be placed on the package insert of all medicines requiring additional checks. in sum, this text is a remarkable step forward in providing the conditions for better protection of patients, by providing them with practical information on the use of medicines and their adverse effects.
in writing. despite mandatory extensive clinical trials and marketing authorisation (maa), medicines have serious side effects that often require hospitalization, but also cause a very high number of deaths in the eu. i welcome the adoption of the pharmacovigilance legislation by the european parliament which strengthens the provisions on european legislation on medicinal products for human use. patients will now be able to report adverse drug reactions directly to the doctor. at the same time, the creation of a european internet portal will improve information on medicines: i note with satisfaction the provisions taken on the protection of personal data. these measures will improve the safety and quality of medicines and patients. however, there is still room for improvement in the funding of pharmacovigilance, which today remains dependent on laboratory fees (and thus on their goodwill), and for ensuring the independence of the risk assessment committee from the european medicines agency, which issues a large number of marketing authorisations for medicines in the eu. the ball is now in the commission's court, particularly as regards the improvement of the labelling of medicinal products.
in writing. i abstained on the mcavan report on pharmacovigilance because the basis for efficacy and safety for patients using medicines must be the independence of pharmacovigilance committees. this necessarily requires public funding, which is no longer guaranteed by this text, since these activities will now be financed mainly by laboratory fees, a system that is controversial and contested. even if the compromise reached with the council brings improvements in the field of drug testing and transparency of procedures, i could not support this text.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text. with this legislation, which was approved at first reading by the european parliament, biocides used to control pests and germs are on their way to becoming safer and more environmentally friendly. the general aim of the draft regulation is to update community rules governing products ranging from insect repellents to water treatment chemicals (agricultural pesticides are covered by separate legislation). for the first time, materials treated with biocides will also be regulated. we have also adopted a ban on the most toxic substances, in particular those which are carcinogenic, harmful to fertility or interfere with genes or hormones, while strengthening the requirement to gradually replace other dangerous substances with less harmful alternatives. the future centralised authorisation system for biocidal products at eu level, which will be implemented gradually, will also ensure greater uniformity across the 27 member states, and thus greater safety.
in writing. this proposal for a regulation establishing a european insurance and occupational pensions authority is part of the financial supervision package. the latter creates three european authorities to supervise specific sectors of financial activity: banks, insurance and financial markets. i fully supported this report and the financial supervision package as a whole because i believe it represents a major and above all necessary step forward. we have learned the lessons of the crisis and its dramatic effects on the economy and on employment, caused by the failures of the present financial system. with this new supervisory architecture, the objective is to clean up the financial system and ensure its stability.
in writing. insurance and occupational pension schemes should be guaranteed by the member states. the europe of reducing public revenue and expenditure is obviously not going in this direction. the green paper on pensions which the commission released on 7 july is a reminder of this. in this context, it is unthinkable that a european supervisory authority could supervise such a sector. i am voting against this text.
in writing. i am pleased to see the commitments made by my political family during the financial crisis widely adopted by the european parliament. we had to revise the european financial surveillance system. the lack of coordination between national supervisory bodies ultimately increased the risk of failure of financial institutions. by establishing three new european authorities responsible for supervising the functioning of banks, financial markets and insurance and pension institutions, we have put in place a complete architecture for financial supervision. the banks will thus be supervised in an equal and coordinated manner by the european banking authority. the commission will have the final say in any dispute with national bank supervisors. ensuring the solvency of financial institutions, allowing greater transparency of financial markets and products, also means ensuring better protection for investors, businesses, savers and consumers. this new tool will not be the preserve of a few financial experts but will be of use to everyone.
in writing. the creation of a european financial supervisor was proposed in september 2009 by the european commission, building on the work of the group chaired by jacques de larosière. from 1 january 2011, the union will therefore have a control tower to identify financial risks and tools to act if necessary. this role will be entrusted to three new supervisory authorities for banking, financial markets and insurance and to a european systemic risk board. i therefore voted in favour of this report because i believe that the european union needs a body specifically responsible for the macroprudential supervision of its financial system, which would be able to detect risks to financial stability and, where appropriate, to issue warnings and make recommendations to respond to such risks. preserving public service missions, encouraging innovation, improving financing for smes: these are the three objectives to ultimately create sustainable and equitable growth.

in writing. the powers conferred on the three european supervisory authorities (esas) are not limited to what their title suggests. they should be addressed to the council of the member states. they should not be able to put in place any measure without the prior agreement of the council except to change their roadmap which obliges them to protect investors, savers and the proper functioning of the internal market while cooperating with international institutions. i am voting against this text. the competences of the esas and their objectives need to be reviewed.

in writing. i voted in favour of this report despite the fact that progress has not lived up to the promises made in 2009 at the g20 summits, where european leaders committed to work towards effective and rigorous regulation of financial products and players. however, this legislative package does not replace the absence of economic governance. without fiscal harmonization, without a common industrial policy, without strong proposals for growth and employment, we will not be able to resist the attacks of the markets, nor to ensure that the wealth produced in europe is equitably distributed among all citizens.
in writing. i voted for the giegold report on the european financial markets authority because it is very urgent that the european union should have the tools to monitor financial markets in order to avoid new financial and economic crises. the creation of this authority, and all those established in the rest of the supervisory package, make it possible to move from the simple coordination of national authorities, with sometimes very divergent interests, to genuine european authorities. the activities of credit rating agencies, which had a major role in triggering the financial crisis, will now be subject to direct european supervision. this is undeniable progress, although there is still a long way to go.
in writing. the final vote on the 'financial package' marked the end of negotiations with parliament on a minimum of european financial regulation. i voted against this financial package because the proposed responses are not up to the current crisis and would be even less able to prevent new ones. it is not enough to create new bodies to regulate the financial sector, especially when these bodies have serious shortcomings. the composition of the general council of the european systemic risk board (esrb) speaks for itself, with only representatives of the ecb, the commission and the national central banks. the measures adopted by the european parliament are at best a first step towards the establishment of a real system of supervision of financial institutions. it is time to face up to reality and to see the very real social damage of so-called economic and financial realism. the responses are not up to the crisis, they are just a "cautery on a wooden leg".
in writing. the report highlights the negative impact of counterfeiting and infringements of intellectual property rights (ipr) online, across all creative sectors, on employment and the european economy as a whole. i am convinced that in order to strengthen the protection of intellectual property, it is necessary to improve an attractive legal offer online. i am also a member of the committee on the internal market and consumer protection and i believe that it is essential to make consumers aware of the risks posed by counterfeit products, both for health and safety. that is why i voted in favour of this report and i still believe that efforts must be made in campaigns to raise awareness, particularly among young people, of the fight against counterfeiting.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by marielle gallo on the application of intellectual property rights in the internal market. this is an own-initiative report, i.e. it is not a legislative report, and i think that the approach is balanced. the challenge for me is this: we need to protect intellectual property rights because they are the guarantee of living and thriving creativity and innovation, but we also need to develop legal services that make creative content online easy and accessible to the greatest number. i now expect the european commission to propose models combining these two imperatives, i.e. protecting copyright while guaranteeing wide access to creative content. like the rapporteur, i believe that studies should be carried out to assess the developments and possible improvements in the digital market in europe, through consultation of the stakeholders and the constant involvement of the european parliament.
in writing. i voted against this report because by equating file sharing for non-commercial purposes with counterfeiting and theft, marielle gallo and the european right are pushing for the criminalisation of millions of internet users who are also consumers of music and films. in doing so, they pit the artists against their own audience without giving them a penny more. contrary to what they want us to believe, the european right does not defend artists but industries and their obsolete model. this report is nothing but the continuation of the policy of the french government which is more concerned with the interests of the majors of the record and the world of show business than with the fundamental freedoms of citizens. this attitude is incapable of meeting the challenges of creation in the digital age.
in writing. in france, as in europe, creativity, research and innovation are suffering. it is a question of restoring readability and confidence to all the actors. to this end, the issue of intellectual property rights is legitimate. we therefore voted to give our voice to the fight against counterfeiting (especially medicines), to raising awareness among young people of the issues of intellectual property and to support smes. however, in the end we voted against the gallo report, in order to reaffirm the difference between file sharing between internet users for private purposes and counterfeiting by structured networks for profit. we regret that the report adopted does not reflect our strongly held positions in parliament and in france (the telecom package and the hadopi law), calling for a judicial decision before any sanctions are imposed on internet users. on this last, extremely sensitive point, the actors must look for proposals which are non-partisan, without a technological a priori, and, in the end, capable of guaranteeing fundamental freedoms, clarifying respect for property rights and multiplying creation.
in writing. of course intellectual property rights must be respected. of course, violations of these rights must be punished, because they harm the interests of our creators, our economies and our companies. but we could not approve mrs gallo's report because, under the few remarks on counterfeiting of tangible goods, which the commission is fighting lightly, the real target is downloading from the internet, which unfortunately affects millions of people. mrs gallo was elected by the party which introduced the hadopi law in france. nothing in the report actually says that the measures it is calling for will include the guarantee of judicial proceedings and remedies against possible infringements. nor is there any guarantee of the right to private copying. we cannot criminalize, monitor and blame millions of european internet users because the cultural industry is struggling to adapt to new technologies and to offer citizens a commercial offer worthy of the name.
in writing. the own-initiative report on the application of intellectual property rights in the internal market was adopted by 328 votes to 245 with 81 abstentions: mrs gallo (epp) did indeed obtain a majority but the debate was confused; it has failed to transcend the divisions, nor has it paved the way for legislation. i therefore voted against: this text does not strike the right balance between respect for fundamental freedoms and the protection of intellectual property rights; it's out of step with the technological reality. it is true that the alternative resolutions tabled by the adle and the s&d were not entirely satisfactory either, but they had the merit of eliminating false and inappropriate solutions. however, in a constructive spirit, i supported certain measures to combat counterfeiting (particularly in the pharmaceutical sector), to raise awareness among young people of the problems of intellectual property and to support small and medium-sized enterprises. it is time for non-partisan and technologically unprejudiced substantive work to finally reconcile fundamental freedoms, creativity and respect for the intellectual property rights of authors and artists.
in writing. i voted in favour of the amendments on the fight against counterfeiting, raising awareness among young people of intellectual property issues and supporting innovation in small and medium-sized enterprises, but i voted against the own-initiative report on the application of intellectual property rights in the internal market. the report combined the issues of file sharing between internet users for private purposes with counterfeiting on the part of networks structured for profit. i also deeply regret that this report makes no reference to the need for a judicial decision before any sanction is imposed on internet users. in voting against this report, i wanted to express my disagreement with a text which has failed to strike a balance between the protection of fundamental freedoms and the respect of intellectual property rights.
in writing. i voted against the gallo report, which in my view does indeed favour a real 'pirate hunt', which unfortunately is not unlike the french-french debate on the so-called hadopi law. the text voted in strasbourg is purely repressive in nature and creates a dangerous confusion by failing to distinguish between the counterfeiting of tangible goods - particularly medicines - and the sharing of digital files for non-commercial purposes. the millions of peer-to-peer internet users who also consume music and movies seem to be becoming potential criminals. with my socialist colleagues we had advocated an alternative position which, on the contrary, supports an approach adapted to the present realities, and in doing so protects the fundamental freedoms of consumers. and our strategy would not have "sniffed" copyright at all, because we were proposing the creation of new business models that would compensate authors for the use of their works online. we french and european socialists must be particularly vigilant to ensure that fundamental freedoms are not further restricted.
in writing. this text validates the intellectual property rights invented by the french revolution of 1789. but it does open up rights to private justice delivered to operators, a practice of the old regime. i am voting against, in line with my opposition to the hadopi act in france.
in writing. beyond the substance, i supported this report for its balanced aspect, and this despite the pressure from some internet actors relayed by the socialists, because the demagogy must one day stop. although this report is not legally binding, it lays the foundations for a european reflection on intellectual property in the digital age and emphasises various aspects which i would like to reiterate. piracy and file sharing, on a scale of millions of users, are having a negative impact on the cultural economy, the creative industries and employment. the problem remains, although the figures available to us are subject to debate. the report therefore asks the european commission to provide us with reliable figures. some argue that there is a market failure between the prices of cultural works in the legal circuit and their availability - "free" - on the internet. however, responsibility is necessary. illegal downloading cannot become legal through a "right-fundamentalist" pass-through of protecting individual freedoms. the cultural industries must also make an effort, offering really attractive prices, adapted to the new demand created by the digital era and respecting the fair remuneration of authors.

acting president of the council. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, first of all i would like to thank you for giving me the opportunity to speak here today on this very important subject, namely biodiversity. in its conclusions of 15 march 2010, entitled 'biodiversity: after 2010. the council stressed the need to preserve biodiversity and to avoid irreversible damage to ecosystems and their functions, including to protect social and economic stability and to achieve the millennium development goals. the council recalled that biodiversity plays a central role in the global fight against hunger and food security and is an essential contributor to wealth creation and poverty reduction. much more than in the eu, in most developing countries, the protection of ecosystems is closely linked to employment, income and livelihoods. with a view to the 10th conference of the parties to the convention on biological diversity, the eu is committed to making an active and constructive contribution to a global consensus on the post-2010 biodiversity action. this includes measures that need to be able to develop a vision beyond 2010 at the strategic level, which could for example have a time horizon to 2020, a vision that could have a time horizon to 2050, a vision of the secondary objectives and the key milestones, linked to measurable indicators, and finally a vision of the establishment of appropriate arrangements, for monitoring, evaluation and follow-up. the high-level meeting of the united nations general assembly two weeks ago, on 22 september, in new york, was a good opportunity to call on the international community to face the critical state of biodiversity worldwide and also to stress the need to safeguard the basis of life on earth for the benefit of humanity and future generations and to take appropriate initiatives at all levels. as regards technical assistance to the least developed countries, the council considers that the development and transfer of best practices and technologies are essential in the fight against biodiversity loss, climate change and desertification. it is important to achieve a coordinated approach and to use the resources in a satisfactory, cost-effective way. as regards financing, the council considers that the establishment of an effective policy framework for the period after 2010 and the introduction of a new strategic plan for biodiversity will require an appropriate use of resources from all possible sources, both public and private, including new forms of financing and financing of measures to combat climate change. the council also considered that consideration should be given to the possibility of also providing financial resources for biodiversity by modifying, abolishing or redirecting subsidies which are harmful to biodiversity. the integration of biodiversity into business activities and other sectoral policies remains a necessity and a priority objective. in its conclusions of 5 december 2006, the council already noted, in response to the paris message on biodiversity, that biodiversity and the maintenance of ecosystem services should be included in the policy dialogue with partner countries and partner regions. in doing so, they should be encouraged to further identify needs and to give them priority consideration in national and regional development strategies and plans. the council remains convinced that the integration of ecosystem services and biodiversity into development cooperation programmes and subsequent financial support is the only way to achieve sustainable results. although there is a clear link between the aarhus convention on access to information, participation in decision-making and access to justice on environmental matters on the one hand, and biodiversity on the other, it should be borne in mind that this convention was drawn up in the framework of the united nations economic commission for europe. although that convention is open to accession by countries which are not members of that committee, our development partners are not parties to that convention at the present time. i thank you for your interest and i look forward to your debate, which i am sure will provide a lot of new elements.
member of the commission. − madam president, the european union’s strategic objectives for nagoya are set out in the council conclusions of 22 december 2009 and 15 march 2010 and will be further elaborated and refined by the environmental council on 14 october 2010. three issues stand out in particular as priorities for the european union. the first is the adoption of the new strategic plan for the convention for the period 2011-2020. it should reflect the best available scientific knowledge about the state of biodiversity and provide an effective framework of implementation that is sufficiently ambitious to trigger step-up action by all the parties to the convention. this is vital if we are to prevent further species extinctions and enable biodiversity to continue providing the essential goods and services that we all depend on, and especially the poor. the second strategic priority for the european union is to conclude negotiations on the protocol on access and benefit-sharing, as a key contribution to the conservation and sustainable use of biodiversity beyond 2010 and in line with the commitment taken by all the parties at cop 8 in 2006. this is an expectation widely shared by developing country parties to the convention, many of which see it as their top priority. the third is to ensure that adequate resources are mobilised to enable the implementation of the post-2010 biodiversity policy framework, including the new strategy plan. the eu as a whole is committed, as part of its 2020 biodiversity target adopted earlier this year, to step up its contribution to averting global biodiversity loss, but i think we can also be pretty proud of what we are actually doing. over the period 2002-2008, the european union provided over usd 1 billion, approximately eur 740 million, for global biodiversity annually, largely through the thematic programme on environment and natural resources under the development cooperation instrument, but also the edf, both of which include adequate provisions for biodiversity. member states have also contributed significantly to the recent replenishment of the global environmental facility, for which usd 1.2 billion is earmarked for biodiversity. this represents a 28% increase compared to the last replenishment, and the new eur 1 billion mdg initiative announced by president barroso at the un general assembly in new york last month can clearly also benefit biodiversity. the commission is currently updating its own biodiversity-related development cooperation figures, using the same methodology as it has used to account for climate-related funding, and we are of course encouraging member states to do the same so that we can present a consolidated figure in nagoya. we also need to look at other ways of how we can contribute to enhancing implementation of the convention on biodiversity and help developing country parties deliver on their commitments under the convention, in particular the new post-2010 strategic plan that will be adopted in nagoya. we intend to explore ways and means to do this, together with our partners in nagoya. biodiversity loss is not a new challenge to poverty alleviation, as already mentioned. the 2010 biodiversity target was incorporated into mdg 7 already in 2002 and the eu itself has explicitly underscored the important linkages between biodiversity and development on many occasions. just last month in his statement during the high-level event on biodiversity at the united nations general assembly, president barroso remarked that our ability to end poverty and hunger and improve child and maternal health depends on the long-term availability of fresh water, food, medicine and raw materials that nature provides. this is also recalled in the 2010 mdg report, in the eu policy framework to assist developing countries in addressing food security challenges, and in the commission’s policy coherence for development work programme 2010-2013, which includes a specific target for biodiversity and accompanying indicators as part of the operational framework to enhance the coherence of eu policies with development objectives. what is perhaps new is the increasing knowledge and awareness about economics of biodiversity loss and the extent to which this undermines prospects for alleviating poverty in the long term. the international study of the economics of ecosystems and biodiversity (teeb) shows how costly biodiversity loss and ecosystem degradation is to our economies, including the economies in developing countries. so it is not any more a moral question, it is actually a question of our quality of life, and yet the conservation of biodiversity and ecosystems is not seen as a development priority. it is hoped that teeb will go some way towards changing this situation so that more of our developing country partners give higher priority to biodiversity conservation and sustainable use in their development strategies but, even where it is not a focus of action in country and regional support strategies, european development policy nevertheless requires that environment and sustainable management of natural resources be treated as a cross-cutting issue to be integrated into all development activities. both the development cooperation instrument and the european development fund include provisions for addressing biodiversity. to conclude, with regard to mechanisms for ensuring the right of access to information and public participation in decision-making related to biodiversity, the eu fully supports the draft cop 10 decision on the strategic plan, which urges parties and other governments to enable broad and effective participation in the full implementation of the objectives of the convention and strategic plan. we also believe that the protocol on access and benefit-sharing should oblige contracting parties to establish domestic frameworks that allow indigenous and local communities to take prior and informed decisions on whether or not to give access to their traditional knowledge. i would endorse everything said by the authors of the questions and i am truly grateful for their valuable contributions.

mr president, i would like to draw your attention, ladies and gentlemen, to one aspect of this resolution, one which is not secondary to me, but is central, a point from which regional cohesion policies can take their full meaning. the question is which instrument will best enable us to measure the development of european regions most appropriately and which will provide the best decision support, particularly on the eligibility choices for european funds. it is a question of a political compass, a guide to move, i quote the proposed resolution, towards this targeted approach to territorial development, towards this integrated approach. what is this guide on which to base our policies of regional cohesion? today we have only one indicator, gross domestic product, which is a great indicator, a great measuring instrument for economic growth and wealth creation. but regional development issues are not limited to increasing gross domestic product. the well-being of populations is not just an index or a curve. otherwise, we may end up with only a distorted, partial, and therefore partial, indicator. in order to carry out regional cohesion policies which are relevant to the objective of sustainable development of the territories, which, i remind you, is our common objective, the gross domestic product index must be supplemented by other measurement instruments, other indicators, particularly in the social and environmental fields. it is necessary to be able to assess the level of unemployment, precariousness, education, health, environmental quality, air and water quality, protection of resources, access to basic services, etc. therefore, and i will end with this, every effort must be made to create, alongside gross domestic product, a set of social and environmental indicators which will enable regional cohesion policies to move towards development based on the three pillars of sustainable development, economic, social and environmental.
(starting from micro) ...has more than 250 regions with its 27 member states. these regions are not all homogeneous, there are significant differences between them in terms of wealth, development and living standards. and it is to reduce these disparities and make the regions more competitive that the european union has implemented a policy of regional cohesion and convergence based on solidarity and endowed with the appropriate financial means: the erdf, the esf, the cohesion funds. however, despite the progress made, it would be an illusion to think that these differences will disappear in 2013, even in 2020. it is therefore appropriate to maintain the principles of cohesion policy and the accompanying financial means beyond 2013. this regional cohesion and convergence policy must of course be carried out in conjunction with other strategies, such as the eu 2020 strategy. but it must be carried out independently of this strategy and it should not, under the pretext of regionalising a particular objective of the eu 2020 strategy, appropriate or monopolise part of the cohesion policy appropriations. parliament must be very vigilant on this issue, which is essential for all regions, but particularly for regions whose development is lagging behind, particularly the outermost regions.
