in writing. a note by europol, eurojust and frontex estimated the number of irregular migrants entering the european union at 900 000. the document describes illegal immigrants from the balkans as having a high potential for drug, arms and human trafficking. while many of these countries remain highly unstable for geopolitical, religious and even ethnic reasons, the report by the socialist tanja fajon proposes nothing less than the abolition of the visa regime for all the countries of the western balkans. apart from the fact that this right of passage would be contrary to the schengen agreements and the very principles of the functioning and mechanism of accession to the european union, i do not think that there is any question of allowing free movement to countries such as bosnia and herzegovina or albania. the invocation of this "fundamental right" is in reality a "catch-all" utopia. the european union is already facing a massive and uncontrolled immigration which is seriously damaging the identity and the economic and social level of the nations which make up the union. let us instead advocate a fundamental right of peoples to retain control of their borders and to decide sovereignly who may or may not enter their territories.
in writing. if this is about extending visa exemptions to citizens of albania and bosnia and herzegovina, we could discuss the assessment that albania has made progress in eradicating the influence of organised crime. it's not. but the rapporteur's explanatory statement and the afet opinion, both of which advocate the liberalization of visa facilitation with kosovo, are an unacceptable provocation. i therefore vote against.
in writing. considering that the human rights situation in the democratic republic of congo is not improving, but is worsening, and that systematic human rights violations are being committed on a daily basis, including extrajudicial executions, abductions, sexual violence and acts of torture, i believe it was essential for me to vote in favour of this resolution by the european parliament. profits, the economy, mining and land resources are under the control of armed groups, and conflicts have been going on for years, despite the presence of un monuc forces. it is therefore essential to ask the government of the drc to restore stability and security to the country and thus to initiate peace processes.
in writing. we adopted today in plenary by a very large majority a resolution condemning the failures in the protection of human rights in the democratic republic of congo. we have condemned the violence and particularly the mass rapes that took place in the country during the summer. it is urgent to step up the fight against impunity and, above all, to put an end to all violations of human rights, whatever they may be! independent investigations must be carried out to bring the perpetrators to justice. we also deplore the fact that the un peacekeeping forces present in the country have not been able to prevent the violence. their presence is nonetheless essential but they must be allowed to carry out their mandate in the drc to the full.
in writing. a political solution to the armed conflict in the democratic republic of congo (drc) is urgently needed to bring security and stability to the people of eastern congo. this is the subject of the resolution adopted by the european parliament today following the publication of the report by the office of the high commissioner for human rights on 1 october, which lists 617 of the most serious violations of human rights and international humanitarian law committed over a period of ten years by state and non-state actors in the drc. tens of thousands of people were killed and many more were raped, mutilated or subjected to other forms of violence during the decade in question. the european union stands ready to support all efforts by the government of the drc and the countries of the great lakes region to jointly promote peace and stability in the region, with a focus on reconciliation, the security of persons, the reform and strengthening of justice, and the return and integration of refugees and internally displaced persons.
in writing. on the occasion of the world day against the death penalty, which will take place on 10 october for the eighth consecutive year, we as european parliamentarians wanted to adopt a resolution to recall our commitment to the death penalty and our wish to see this principle of opposition to the death penalty universally adopted. while 43 countries worldwide retain the death penalty, the resolution calls on those member states which still apply it to declare a moratorium on executions; the objective of achieving total abolition worldwide is one of the priorities of the union's human rights policy.
in writing. the 8th world day against the death penalty, 10 october 2010, is an opportunity for the european parliament to recall that the abolition of the death penalty worldwide remains a priority for the european union, even though it is still practised in 18 countries. in 2009, more than 700 people were executed, not counting the thousands of executions in china. the executions or death sentences have never improved the crime rate, and the european union must therefore promote alternative sentences available to criminal justice systems in its relations with countries still applying this punishment, which is contrary to the universal declaration of human rights. parliament also expressed its deep concern at the application of the death penalty to minors and persons with mental or intellectual disabilities and called for it to be brought to a swift and definitive end.
in writing. the oil spill caused by the deepwater horizon oil rig in the gulf of mexico last spring is the reason for this resolution by the european parliament's environment committee, which aims to draw attention to the urgency of preventing oil spills. i therefore voted for this resolution because it is essential that we succeed in establishing strict european rules for the prevention of accidents on oil platforms and that the union strengthens legislation on environmental liability. i regret, however, that the mention of a moratorium on any new oil drilling until new standards are in place throughout the union was dropped by a majority of members in today's vote. the introduction of a moratorium was in line with the policy of preventing and strengthening security measures for oil platforms and was in line with the policy of barack obama who put in place a similar moratorium in the united states until december 2010.
in writing. the eu must learn from the deepwater horizon disaster and ensure that high safety standards are respected in all offshore oil exploration areas. given the risks of offshore drilling and the uncertainties about the management and possible consequences of such an incident in europe, the resolution we supported calls for 'a moratorium on all new offshore oil drilling in eu waters'. we also ask the commission to take a detailed inventory of the sites and to work on an action plan, in liaison with the member states, to improve safety standards on existing platforms. finally, we want to be sure that the polluters are held legally responsible and that the victims, like the fishermen, can be properly compensated.
in writing. the highest levels of precaution, environmental protection, safety and security are essential principles for oil activities in europe, on which we cannot compromise. the lessons to be drawn from the disaster in the gulf of mexico will be essential to prevent similar events from happening again in the maritime and coastal waters of the european union. nevertheless, parliament was right today in rejecting the maximalist position of a moratorium on any new deepwater oil drilling in european waters. it is not only the survival and future of our european oil industry in times of crisis, but also our energy independence.
in writing. i abstain in the face of a document which does not contain a single reference to the transition to post-oil.
in writing. nearly 5 million barrels of oil spilled into the waters of the gulf of mexico between april and september 2010 following the explosion of the deepwater horizon oil platform, causing extensive damage to both the region's economy and ecosystem. in all, more than 400 species - whales, dolphins, manatees, herons, egrets, and others - are threatened. while the eu has many oil platforms - more than 500 in the north sea - everything must be done at european level to prevent such a disaster from happening on our territory. in voting in favour of this resolution, i am calling for strict european rules on accident prevention for oil platforms to be defined, and for legislation to ensure that high and uniform safety standards apply to all oil platforms and to all drilling activities in the eu, from the atlantic to the black sea. i also welcome the commission's decision to put oil drilling in eu waters through a 'stress test'.
in writing. i supported this balanced resolution which does not prohibit deepwater oil exploration in the future but makes it conditional on compliance with european safety standards, which are among the strictest in the world. in my view, these standards must guarantee both the sustainability of europe's energy supply and the safety and sustainability of offshore activities. we all have in our minds the terrible images of the oil spill in the gulf of mexico, the painful loss of life, the distress of the affected people and the enormous damage caused by the explosion of the deepwater horizon oil platform. that is why i renew my call for the creation of a genuine european civil protection force capable of rapid and effective deployment after such catastrophes. the scarcity of oil makes offshore deepwater exploration and extraction essential. but their impact on the environment must be controlled, and we must ensure that they do not pose a threat to marine and coastal areas and biodiversity in the future. this is a major challenge for the international and environmental image of the european union, which is recording very positive results in this area.
in writing. i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on the eu biodiversity goals. in the face of the gradual disappearance of species and thus of the earth's biological wealth, it is important to set ambitious objectives for the protection of fauna and flora while ensuring that man can continue to exploit their wealth. to this end, parliament has advocated targets for resource conservation based on strict regulation and the promotion of new technologies.
in writing. it is regrettable that despite the commitments made by the eu at the european summit in gothenburg in 2001, the loss of biodiversity has still not been halted. this resolution recalls that biodiversity plays a key role in the fight against world hunger and food security; and that it is a prerequisite for any efforts to mitigate and adapt to climate change. it is time for all member states to fully implement natura 2000 legislation and the habitats and birds directives and take initiatives to preserve marine biodiversity. this policy for biodiversity must be pursued at both european and international level in order to integrate these concerns, in particular in the union's development cooperation policy and external actions and in any future agreement concluded within the wto.
in writing. the conference of the parties to the cbd will be held in japan from 18 to 29 october. the objective of halting biodiversity loss by 2010 has not been met, either at global or european level. as the parliament's resolution points out, the depletion of biodiversity, if nothing is done quickly to reverse it, will be considerable and uncontrollable in the medium and long term. parliament called for the non-patentability of living organisms and for an end to the plundering of genetic resources by industry and companies, particularly in the southern countries. the protection of biodiversity is an essential element in achieving the millennium development goals. i therefore supported the resolution, which incorporated the amendments proposed by the gue/ngl and the greens. with the cancún climate change conference just a few weeks away, it is therefore high time that the international community, and the european union in particular, in view of its commitment to environmental protection, took up the report 'the economics of ecosystems and biodiversity' (teeb) and its recommendations at the nagoya conference. it is urgent to reiterate that the struggles for biodiversity, against climate change and against poverty are closely linked, as are the responses to address them.
in writing. the basel ii agreements regulate the activities of banks, in particular the capital they must maintain to ensure their solvency. in this resolution, the european parliament advocates long-term risk and profit management, rules that are adapted to the size of banks (so that the largest banks do not feel exempted) and that the costs of adapting to new legislation are not passed on to individuals. parliament also expressed concern that basel ii is not being respected in a uniform way across the world. it urged the european commission to take action to achieve greater harmonisation. i think these recommendations are in the right direction: reducing the risk of a future crisis and protecting individuals. i therefore voted in favour of this text.
in writing. the attempts to improve the international financial system at the level of the basel committee, the g20 and the european union seem to me to be a caucus on a wooden leg. the september agreement on the volume and quality of bank capital requirements was hailed as a major step forward and a major victory over a banking sector that opposed these measures and threatened to cut off credit. it seems to be a pyrrhic victory: the share prices of companies in the sector have barely risen since the agreement was reached, which is not a good sign. banks have until 2019 to comply with the new regulations and anything can happen between now and then. risk analysis, which is known to be totally ineffective, remains at the heart of the system. the liquidity and leverage ratios were not resolved, nor were off-balance sheet assets and securitisation. financial institutions that do not receive money from the public sector, such as hedge funds, are not affected, despite their dangerousness and the perversity of their operation. in short, nothing is solved, and nothing will be solved until we change the system in its entirety instead of trying to patch it up.
in writing. this text does not meet the challenge of the current crisis and its economic and social consequences. the urgent need is to radically change the rules of the banking system, not to take half measures to preserve it. the basel accord sets a ridiculously low level of equity and does not prohibit any of the tools of speculation. i vote against this appearance of speculation.
in writing. africa is exhausted by the consequences of the crisis, natural disasters, extreme poverty, wars, epidemics, so it is urgent to help it to implement a sustainable health policy. that is why i supported this report, which envisages health systems financed in a mixed way by state resources, international solidarity and citizen participation. this requires that european countries keep their promise to spend at least 0.7% of gdp on cooperation in 2010. the eu must support the many existing mutual initiatives aimed at improving access to health care. member states are called upon to provide their expertise and greater technical and financial support to the governments of the developing countries in order to establish and extend social protection systems. finally, the eib also has a role to play in guaranteeing loans, co-financing investments in clinics and covering part of the remuneration of health professionals. only through these combined efforts will africa be able to have a sustainable health system that is accessible to all.
in writing. strengthening health systems in sub-saharan africa is a crucial aspect of development policies. addressing the shortcomings of health care systems will also have an impact on global public health, through improved training of carers, tailored prevention campaigns, and lower treatment costs. this will help to reduce serious epidemics such as hiv, tuberculosis and dysentery. it is unacceptable that private companies, in the name of profit, impede access to health care, much less that conservative religious movements reject sexual and reproductive health policies and question the right to abortion, thus endangering the health of millions of women. improving health systems in sub-saharan africa and globally requires the european union to coordinate better with the rest of the international community. in particular, it has a role to play in fostering the emergence of mutualist, non-profit-making and supportive health structures, which promote access to quality health care. that is why i support the adoption of the veronique de keyser report.
in writing. how can we accept that the life expectancy of an african and a european can differ by 30 or 40 years? several factors, such as poor governance, natural disasters and extreme poverty, contribute to a worrying situation, where african health indicators are among the most worrying in the world. as the report points out, the world bank believes that it is unlikely that developing countries will be able to finance their own national health systems with tax revenues in the near future. in this context, non-profit systems funded in a mixed way, both through state resources, international solidarity and citizen participation, can help to address the huge health challenge in sub-saharan africa. certainly, some african countries have already embarked on promising initiatives with the help of the international community. but the european union has a specific role to play in building health structures of solidarity - by guiding and financing basic health systems or access to medicines, and by supporting programmes to raise awareness of prevention and early diagnosis of diseases.
in writing. my colleagues and i believe that we must build on the successes of the european union's regional policy. this means that it will have to undergo an evolution, not a revolution. it must remain a strong policy, well funded and a real lever for economic development for all our regions. we want simplified rules, not just in words but in deeds. we believe that the cities or the outermost regions should be given special attention. having worked on this resolution both in the working group and in the parliamentary committee on regional development, i have made two important advances: that the needs of potential beneficiaries are better taken into account and that the concept of gdp is not unnecessarily sacralized. i think that gdp should remain the main criterion for allocating funds, but we must also consider other criteria. i am satisfied with the compromise reached and have voted in favour of this text. by adopting this resolution by a very large majority, we have come together and sent a very clear message to the european commission and the european ministers.
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution on the european union's regional and cohesion policy after 2013. this text contains key statements such as the need to maintain, after 2013, a cohesion policy which is a necessary condition for the union of the member states. i think that we have to be very cautious about asking that, under the second pillar of the common agricultural policy (cap), rural development be coordinated with the cohesion development objectives and managed at regional level to ensure that it is appropriate to the needs. regional adequacy can be achieved by contracting without a mandatory instrument. we are in complete agreement that cohesion policy should not be renationalised. cohesion policy must not be national or regional: it must be european. we must move from a cohesion policy based on the reunification of the continent to a cohesion policy based on the planning and development of the european territory: to make the union the most competitive territory in the world in economic and social terms and the most sustainable in environmental terms: this is an ambition linked to the europe of results that citizens expect.
in writing. the european parliament has just adopted the resolution on the european union's cohesion and regional policy after 2013 in support of the demands made by the regions currently meeting in brussels for the open days. parliament wants to send a strong political signal ahead of the fifth cohesion report due in november, which will set out the broad guidelines for eu regional policy after 2013. the social crisis we are currently experiencing gives a special dimension to regional development policy. in order to continue to cope with this period of economic restructuring, the regions need an appropriate budget. to ensure the success of the eu 2020 strategy, the regions also need to be better involved and to be able to take action. the european commission must continue to simplify the procedures for accessing funds. finally, cohesion policy must also be better communicated so that european citizens understand the importance of the structural funds in major projects for territorial and social cohesion. this is one of the actions of proximity which europe must promote.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of this resolution setting out the guidelines for the erdf for the 2014-2020 budgetary period. i think that by recalling the regional nature of the erdf we are reaffirming the need to take account of the specific features of the territories in the implementation of regional policy. nevertheless, it is essential that the managing authorities take account of the realities on the ground and determine areas of erdf intervention which genuinely meet the needs of local authorities and economic operators. it is true that the management of the erdf in our regions is marked by profound disparities, which is why i am calling for the management standards to be harmonized at european level. it is also important to provide for greater opportunities to adjust the lines of intervention midway through the programme in line with the economic and social context and the evolution of the territories, so that the erdf can bring real added value throughout the programming period. the erdf is, in my view, a formidable lever for growth, employment and territorial cohesion, and it must become a relevant tool for effectively supporting structural development projects at the service of our citizens and our territories.
in writing. article 9 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union provides that: in defining and implementing its policies and actions, the union shall take into account requirements relating to the promotion of a high level of employment, the guarantee of adequate social protection, the fight against social exclusion and a high level of education, training and protection of human health. other it seems to me therefore essential to increase the effectiveness and visibility of the european social fund (esf), the social component of the european union's regional policy. the €10 billion invested each year in a social europe (lifelong learning, social inclusion, adaptation of workers, etc.) must be used in a way that is consistent with the objectives of the eu2020 strategy and be fully exploited. however, the esf must remain an integral part of the eu's regional policy to avoid that a sharp differentiation of funds leads to increased complexity. i voted for this text because it clearly sets out these challenges and makes a strong appeal to the european commission: the esf must become a central instrument of european policies.
in writing. the european social fund plays a key role in promoting social cohesion by helping to integrate workers in european regions. its action in favour of small and medium-sized enterprises, education and vocational training is essential for the success of the eu 2020 strategy. the role of the european social fund could, however, be further strengthened. the future architecture of the structural funds for 2014-2020 will have to take into account the specificities of the fund. adjustments may be considered. but it is important to keep the european social fund within the framework of the general regulation on the structural funds, as is the case today. the creation of a legal framework of its own will inevitably lead to a fragmentation of european policies and unnecessary complexity for the beneficiaries. the coherence of european policies must go hand in hand with an integrated vision of objectives and means, which requires greater synergies between instruments. the european social fund must therefore continue to operate under the general regulation, albeit with its own rules, but in no case with an independent budget.
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution on the future of the european social fund (esf). the esf is a key element of european social cohesion, supporting employment, the integration of workers into the labour market and vocational training. in this text we have clearly spoken out against the european commission's proposal to separate the european social fund from the other funds. on the contrary, it must be closely linked to other instruments, in particular regional policy instruments, in order to increase its effectiveness. we have voted for greater efficiency, simplification and transparency in this instrument, which must continue to be a powerful lever for the construction of social europe. the european social fund must also be able to be directed towards the fight against poverty and social exclusion as a whole and to help meet the union's objectives in this field.
in writing. this report claims to defend decent work and to fight against precarious work. pretending is one thing. we still have to find the means. the europe 2020 strategy goes in the opposite direction of such a claim. what is the real significance of this gossip? i don't know. why point out the problems of the poor and ignore the problems of the rich? this text is a hypocritical sermon.
in writing. the european parliament voted a resolution on the future of the european social fund. at a time when the esf is being challenged, in particular by the president of the commission, who wants to integrate it into a wider fund with diluted objectives, this support for the esf by the european parliament is important. the resolution supports the role of the esf in the context of european regional and social policy and calls for the simplification of the procedures for allocating funds. these overly restrictive procedures do not promote a distribution of funds that is really adapted to the needs of the population and, moreover, lead to a non-consumption of appropriations, especially in france, which is a scandal in itself. i regret, however, that the resolution in particular repeats the dogma of 'modernization of education systems' and calls for these to be adapted to the needs of enterprises alone in order to improve access to employment.
the commission has already submitted a proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos. - mr president, commissioner, we are finally coming to the end of these long months of work to lay the foundations for the future external action service of the european union, but i wanted, as some of my colleagues have done before, to thank the rapporteurs for the quality of their work. because we all want to see real european diplomacy, which is not just the sum of the 27 member states' diplomacies, the financial regulation and the regulation on the status of civil servants, which we are discussing today and will be voting on tomorrow, are of paramount importance. they must enable us to meet a double challenge: to speak with one voice on the international scene, but also to ensure the coherence of the union's external policies as a whole. as such, trade policy is not within the competence of the high representative, but as a former trade commissioner, i have no doubt that she will be able to create the dialogue necessary to ensure that trade policy properly respects the objectives of the union's external action, as set out in the treaty, in particular sustainable development, poverty eradication and the protection of human rights. finally, i would like to stress that our common political will will be measured by the budgetary resources devoted; our ability to exert political influence on the international stage depends on it.
president of the council. - madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, since 2010 is the european year for combating poverty and social exclusion, we are of course well aware that the challenge of poverty is not confined to the borders of the union, nor can it be solved exclusively within them. the recent series of global crises that have affected all countries, with the poorest being the hardest hit, has shown how interconnected the world is today. promoting development is therefore an integral part of europe's response to today's global challenges and the next five years will be crucial for european and therefore global development policy. it is enshrined in article 208 of the lisbon treaty, and we have stated in the european consensus on development, that the primary objective of the european union's development cooperation is the eradication of poverty in the context of sustainable development, in particular by striving to achieve the millennium development goals. however, the achievement of all the millennium development goals in the context of sustainable development is a collective responsibility, whereby all partners should respect the commitments they have made. the european union is convinced that developing countries are responsible and in control of their own development and that they bear the primary responsibility for achieving the millennium development goals. it is therefore important to stress that their achievement requires comprehensive strategies including democratic governance, protection of human rights and the rule of law, economic growth for the poor, private sector development, trade development, human and social development, and environmental sustainability. the european union encourages partner countries to rapidly step up their own efforts, including in the reduction of poverty and inequality and in the establishment of partnerships with civil society, the private sector and local authorities. the european union will strengthen its support for their efforts to mobilise national resources for development, in particular in the context of improving public financial management and the soundness and efficiency of their tax and customs systems. on 22 september, the member states of the united nations, in adopting the outcome document of the millennium development goals summit, reaffirmed their commitment to work together to improve the economic and social conditions of all peoples and to do all in their power to achieve the millennium development goals by 2015.
member of the commission. − madam president, let me first thank you for this opportunity to talk about the challenge of poverty and what the european union can do on the global level through its development cooperation policy. in the second part of this statement i will also turn to the report by mrs figueiredo. eradicating poverty is the most pressing global challenge of our time. it is a challenge that must be tackled, not only for obvious reasons of solidarity and duty, but also for the sake of worldwide prosperity and stability. and that is in everybody’s interests. in 2000, world leaders gathered at the un in new york and agreed on an international development agenda for the coming 15 years, the millennium development goals. among the different goals and targets set in the framework, the world committed to reduce extreme poverty by half. where are we now, five years before the 2015 deadline? encouraging progress has been achieved. overall, 120 million people moved out of poverty between 2000 and 2005, which corresponds to an annual drop of 2.4%, but there is no time for complacency. today, 1.4 billion people still live in extreme poverty, and there are huge disparities among regions, countries and population groups. besides, the recent and current global crisis – from food and fuel price shocks to economic instability and climate change – threatens both past achievements and future prospects. two weeks ago, the mdg summit confirmed the world’s ambition to fight against poverty. members of the european parliament, led by gay mitchell, made an important contribution to that summit and i thank them very much for their participation and support. i would also like to thank parliament for its support in the whole preparation process ending with adoption of the cashman report. this house’s continuing attention to the mdgs made the eu’s position strong and ambitious in new york. i think the meps who took part in the summit were reassured by the outcome. there was no blame game; rather, the gathering gave new energy, impetus and hope with regard to attaining the goals. it demonstrated that the mdgs are still high on the political agenda, with some 110 heads of state and government attending the summit. the european union was instrumental in making this event a success by shaping and voicing a strong common approach among our 27 member states. the fight against poverty is also high on our agenda in the european union. this is part of our european project. it is a central objective of the european union development policy, as stated in the lisbon treaty, and it is also something that european citizens firmly support, which is equally important. as the world’s leading donor, the european union has made a major contribution to the achievement of the mdgs so far. to give you just two examples, the european commission alone has helped put 9 million more girls and boys in schools since 2004, and we have connected 31 million households to clean drinking water. i believe this is something to be proud of, but we need to do more and we can do more. in june, europe’s leaders helped make the mdgs stronger by agreeing on an ambitious plan and a set of actions. the plan prioritises action on the goals on which we have made the least progress, and in those regions and countries that are lagging furthest behind, including those experiencing conflict and fragility. the plan also confirms our commitment to meeting the 0.7% gni target by 2050, despite the difficult economic and financial context. to achieve this we need to assess progress on this every year. turning the millennium development goals – in particular the goal relating to poverty eradication – into millennium development realities by 2015 will also remain the overarching priority of my action. we all know that aid alone will not be sufficient to attain the mdgs. to meet the goals it is also of paramount importance that we are more creative in enhancing the impact of our aid, in promoting more sustainable and more inclusive growth, and in mobilising other and additional sources of finance for development. equally important are the quality and effectiveness of aid, including through more transparency and accountability, as well as ensuring that non-aid policies are more supportive of the mdgs. development aid must be conceived as a catalyst, not as a cure. no country has ever been transformed by aid alone. sustainable progress depends primarily on developing a country’s capacity to generate inclusive and sustainable growth. development can only come from within developing countries, not from outside, and so it is on this ‘within’ that we must focus our development efforts. in the end, this is what the principle of ‘ownership’ means. in november, i plan to launch a green paper and public consultation to gather views on how to improve our policies and instruments to better act on the enabling factors for sustainable and inclusive growth in partner countries, thereby tackling the root causes of poverty, bringing strong added value to our development cooperation. i believe, as usual, that your contribution to this debate will be essential. i would like to thank ms figueiredo for her report on minimum income schemes. at the very heart of her report is the basic right of people to have sufficient resources to allow them to live in dignity. this is enshrined in the charter of fundamental rights of the european union. it has inspired several recent commission initiatives in the area of active inclusion, in particular the 2008 commission recommendation on active inclusion which was endorsed by parliament and the council. the recommendation sets out integrated active inclusion strategies based on three pillars – namely inclusive labour markets, access to quality services and adequate income support. the commission therefore welcomes this report. at the same time, we fully respect member state competences as regards the design and functioning of social protection schemes in general and minimum income schemes in particular. adequate income is a fundamental component in the fight against poverty for people who cannot work. it constitutes a necessary complement to inclusive labour markets, to combat poverty for people who can work. the report rightly reaffirms the basic principle of income support, which has to be both adequate and incentive-compatible. member states are currently taking fiscal consolidation measures to ensure the long-term sustainability of public finances. the commission shares the view that these measures have to take account of the need to protect the most vulnerable members of society. the european commission will present a european platform against poverty by the end of this year, setting out concrete measures to support member states in reaching the target of lifting at least 20 million european citizens out of poverty by 2020.
for the greens/efa group madam president, ladies and gentlemen, 80 million poor people in europe, more than 5 million homeless, millions of poorly housed people, one in five children living in poverty, and at the other end of the scale, what do we have? the number of billionaires is increasing. we have just celebrated the world day for the abolition of poverty on 17 october, and the european year for the eradication of poverty and social exclusion is coming to an end. what concrete solutions will europe have brought to those who are the first victims of a crisis for which they are not responsible? what hope do we offer to my generation, the european generation which is suffering the full brunt of unemployment, precariousness and exclusion, these young people who distrust europe, who expect a great deal from it and therefore from you? we have a duty to respond to their daily anxiety and their anxiety about the future. the lisbon strategy has failed in its mission to eradicate poverty. we no longer have the right to watch and let it happen. this is no longer the time for fine words, for empty words. it is time to show boldness, political courage. all the associations that work with people in poverty, atd quart monde, eapn, feansa, emmaüs europe, have been calling for this for 20 years! that is why we are asking the european commission to draw up a framework directive to define an adequate minimum income. this framework directive will ensure eligibility for and access to a minimum income sufficient to lift every child, adult and elderly person living in poverty out of it and thus guarantee their inalienable right to live in dignity. we have no time left, ladies and gentlemen, and we must act now. let us put an end to this unbearable scandal of enduring poverty together! poverty, the end of poverty, should not be a slogan, it is a reality and i hope that together we will fight this fight.

madam president, we have been celebrating this international day for the eradication of poverty for many years now, without much concrete results, it must be admitted, and we risk celebrating it for many decades to come if the same policies continue to be pursued. from this point of view, europe and the west in general cannot shirk their responsibilities. the fight against poverty is the fight for a fair distribution of wealth within states and internationally. it also means respecting the environment and upholding the principle of equality between human beings everywhere. if the speeches we are making today are not followed by concrete actions in the sense of what we have heard here, i fear that the statements we are making will remain statements of good intentions, without any real impact on the misery and poverty in the world and in europe.
in writing. first, the inclusion of the fight against poverty in the 2020 strategy is a significant step forward for me. the economic crisis has increased poverty in recent years. the european union must be able to encourage the member states to tackle this problem. secondly, the european social fund (esf) is the essential european tool for fighting poverty. i am a rapporteur for the european social fund and i support its use to bring back into employment those who are furthest from the labour market. the esf has had this vocation since its creation with the treaty of rome and must keep this primary objective: employment. thirdly, i am against a minimum income without compensation except for those unable to find work. to reduce poverty, employment is the norm. it's the only way to restore dignity to any person. fourthly, the governments of the member states have a responsibility to actively combat poverty. europe is there to accompany them, to complete their action but is not meant to replace them. europe cannot solve all the problems. states must take their responsibilities first.
in writing. the current directive 2009/42/ec provides for data collection for maritime transport statistics on a voluntary basis. the amendment to this directive will make it compulsory to collect data by type of goods. i welcome this amendment, which will not impose any additional burden, since member states must be able to compile data using existing sources. it is logical that these rules should be binding on maritime transport, whereas they are already binding on road, rail and inland waterway transport. i also welcome the rapporteur's amendments on the implementation of the regulation under the delegated act procedure. parliament must take advantage of this new prerogative provided for by the treaty of lisbon.
in writing. parliament was again asked to approve the payment of aid from the globalisation adjustment fund (gf) to employees made unemployed by the crisis or relocations. again, this aid will be allocated from budget lines originally allocated to other european programmes, as the egf does not have its own funding under the current financial framework. in order to put an end to this situation, i worked, as part of the preparation of the 2011 budget, on the creation of a payment line specific to the egf. eur 50 000 000 was thus adopted by parliament in its vote on the budget reading on 20 october 2010. this amount, which remains symbolic in the light of annual needs, has yet to be confirmed, the european council having initially rejected the proposal to allocate funds from the egf. i shall therefore continue to monitor this matter with a view to achieving the budgetary and legislative consolidation of this system.
in writing. on the day after the world day against poverty and social exclusion, i voted resolutely in favour of this report on women workers in precarious employment. because it is a fact: despite positive developments in gender parity, gender equality, women remain more vulnerable than men in terms of employment. women are much more likely than men to be in precarious employment. and there are still many disparities between men and women in terms of employment opportunities, quality of work, income and pay. it is therefore essential that the commission acts to actively promote equal opportunities for women and men in employment policies, through a future gender equality strategy, through a gradual shift from the status of a precarious worker to that of a regular worker, and that it supports national initiatives in this direction.
in writing. in the context of the work of the parliamentary committee on women's rights, the report by the socialist britta thomsen is generous in terms of social progress. but as usual, this type of report is full of rather vague and even unacceptable "all-in-one" proposals, with a strong leftist, environmentalist and immigrationist connotation at the bottom. it is not possible to consider, for example, that it should be possible to support the settlement of 'migrant women' when it is not really clear whether they are legal or illegal. while it is true that these women, or men, are the first victims of globalization and ultra-liberal neo-slavery, the solution to prevent them from falling into many horrible traps (misconduct, violence or sexual abuse) lies first in allowing them to stay in their country of origin. to this end, immigration policy must be reversed to enable these populations tempted by economic exile to remain in their home countries, by redefining binding international aid to enable political and economic stabilization of these countries.
in writing. low, undeclared or unclear wage earners, workers with no right to social protection or employment-related benefits, workers with no prospect of advancement on the labour market, etc. the number of so-called 'precarious' workers is increasing, as a consequence of the economic crisis we are experiencing. among these workers, there is a high gender disparity: women are overrepresented. i am aware of the need to increase their protection and have therefore supported the european parliament's resolution on women in precarious employment. i call on the member states to ensure that employers who subject their female employees to abusive or harmful treatment are brought to justice swiftly. measures must also be taken to ensure that precarious workers have access to union-based protection of rights such as decent pay, maternity leave and fair and regular working hours. i also hope that the barcelona targets on childcare will be implemented as soon as possible and that the obstacles to women working the number of hours they want - whether part-time or full-time - will be removed.

on behalf of the s&d group. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i would first like to congratulate our rapporteur, barbara weiler, on her work and the remarkable compromise reached with the council, whereas the commission's original proposal had major shortcomings. i would like to return to four important points made in this directive. firstly, i welcome the fact that equal treatment is guaranteed between the public and private sectors. the commission envisaged more severe sanctions for the public sector, even though the latter was acting in the public interest. this reflected a lack of knowledge of the reality of the public accounts situation in the member states and could result in a competitive disadvantage for public undertakings in a competitive situation. another step forward is the extension of the payment period to 60 days instead of 30 for public health services. the latter have complex budgetary procedures which impose on them longer payment periods for which they cannot be held responsible. as regards payment deadlines, it was also essential to prohibit unfair terms to the detriment of creditors in contracts between companies, as is often the case between a large group and an sme. finally, and this concerns mainly smes which are victims of late payment, the introduction of an interest rate of 8% in the event of late payment and of compensation to cover the costs of recovery may encourage these companies to seek redress. they have so far tended to avoid doing so at the risk of putting themselves in danger. i am therefore delighted to be able to vote for this text, which i hope will be a real step forward for the viability and health of european businesses, a step forward which is necessary for a more efficient but also fairer internal market.
in writing. i would like to thank mrs weiler for the quality of her report and the outcome of her negotiations with the council, since the first reading agreement takes up all the key points that the socialists and democrats defended and obtained in the vote in the imco committee. i am particularly pleased that private enterprise and public authorities are now on an equal footing. the commission's original proposal provided for much heavier penalties for public authorities - a difference in treatment which is totally unacceptable to our group since, unlike private companies, public authorities do not act in the interests of profit but in the general interest. the right of the creditor to obtain compensation for the costs of recovery is also a significant step forward, as many companies, especially smes, have so far refrained from claiming interest on arrears from their debtors simply because the cost of the necessary steps was greater than the financial benefits to be derived. finally, the maximum payment period of 30 days in the text seems to me to be a reasonable principle, given that a certain flexibility is allowed, particularly for public health establishments, which was a point particularly important to our group.
member of the commission. − madam president, i would like first to express my deepest sympathy to the families of the victims and to all those who are affected by the industrial accident that occurred on 4 october in ajka, hungary. i also would like to recognise the decisive and effective actions of the hungarian authorities to contain the impact of the spill and its spread from the rivers torna and marcal downstream into the danube and into neighbouring countries, and also to prevent the risks of new spills by building additional protection walls. i had the opportunity to thank minister sándor pintér, the hungarian minister of the interior in charge of civil protection, for all the efforts of the various services involved and for the bravery and dedication of the first responders. i have just come back from the site of the accident where i witnessed both the catastrophic impact of the red sludge on people, homes, land and the ecology of the region, and the significant efforts of the hungarian response teams. while the causes of the disaster and its full impact are still under investigation, it is clear that the most severe damage is in the immediate vicinity of the accident and the directly affected human settlements, agricultural land and ecological systems. 7 000 inhabitants, mainly from the villages of koluntár and devecser, have been affected. nine people died and 130 have been injured, about 35 of them first responders. around 1 000 hectares of agricultural land and four natura 2000 sites have been affected, and there has been substantial damage to flora and fauna in the area. according to the information provided by the hungarian authorities, the red mud does not contain high concentrations of heavy metals and is therefore not considered as hazardous waste. nonetheless, dust from the sludge presents a health risk and therefore precautionary measures are necessary for the population and the emergency personnel in the area. the hungarian authorities have deployed massive human resources and equipment. the day i was there, yesterday, there were around 1 200 rescuers from the civil protection, environment, health and police departments working tirelessly on the ground. it is very important to stress that the emergency phase is broadly over now, because the damage downstream to the danube is stopped and the risk of a second spill contained. steps are now being taken towards the next phase of decontamination and rehabilitation. machinery and staff continue to work on the removal of the red sludge and its disposal in appropriate sites. houses and structures beyond repair are being demolished; protection dikes have been built to prevent the risk of a second spill and are being reinforced. monitoring is being carried out and information on precautionary and sanitary measures is being provided to the population. let me now turn to the eu response. on 7 october, the hungarian authorities triggered the civil protection mechanism requesting an eu expert team. it was deployed immediately for a week in the affected area. this team delivered a number of suggestions for measures to further enhance the hungarian government’s comprehensive remedial and recovery plan. these include: minimising the further spread of red mud via air and water; steps to assess the risk to human health and mitigate them; steps to assess the risk of further damage and mitigate them; environmental monitoring; and remediation and revitalisation measures. beyond this initial emergency response, the commission stands ready to deploy the civil protection mechanism to assist further with expertise, as well as equipment, if the hungarian authorities so require. secondly, the structural funds could be mobilised to address the consequences of the disaster, and that was made clear. the government was informed of that. if they were to decide they wanted to redirect funds, the commission would look favourably on such requests. thirdly, the mobilisation of the eu solidarity fund is very unlikely to be possible in this case due to the strict conditions of the current regulation, under which only natural disasters can be considered; these conditions also include a 0.6% threshold of damage to gdp, and that is unlikely to be met. once again, the commission is very clearly concerned about the need to make the solidarity fund faster and expand its scope. it is very difficult to explain to citizens in member states why we can help people in pakistan immediately, but we cannot help the people living in the ajka area. the commission is also looking into the question of environmental legislation. at a first analysis, the existing eu waste legislation, the directive on waste from extractive industries, the upcoming industrial emissions directive replacing the integrated pollution prevention and control directive, the directive on the control of major accident hazards, the so-called seveso directive, and the waste framework directive provide a sufficient framework for regulating potentially dangerous industrial activities and managing waste in a way that does not pose risks to human health and the environment. the commission is of the view that the focus must not be on new legislation but on ensuring the proper implementation and enforcement of existing legislation by all member states. we also have environmental legislation that deals with post-accident damage, namely the environmental liability directive. it applies to the installation, and consequently the necessary remedial measures that have to be undertaken, by the liable operator who should bear the full cost of remediation. our report on the implementation of the environmental liability directive shows a rather slow take-up of the financial security instruments to cover for liabilities, and this is the case in ajka. we are considering how to strengthen this in the future and if necessary make this mandatory. following the ajka sludge accident, the commission will take stock of the lessons learnt at european level, and in particular the appropriateness and the correct implementation and enforcement of european environmental legislation; the measures needed to make sure that the affected population and industry at risk are covered by appropriate insurance schemes; and the way forward to strengthen european disaster monitoring and response capacity and enhance our instruments to express solidarity with our members and our citizens in moments of need. concerning this last point, i would like to mention that next week the commission will adopt the communication on the reinforcement of eu disaster response capacity which will address the response to various types of disasters, including industrial accidents, and will strengthen our capacity to respond collectively. i would like to take this opportunity to thank parliament for its strong support in this area of strengthening eu disaster response capacity. i look forward to hearing your questions on the specific case in hungary as well as any comments you might want to make on the broader issue.

the history of our european union, a court case started because of rights. we have started court cases because of commerce, because of the economy, because of finance, but this is the first time, on the basis of the treaty of lisbon and on the basis of the charter of fundamental rights which is included in this treaty of lisbon, that the commission has said enough is enough. the commission decided – all 27 commissioners – on 29 september to start infringement proceedings against france on the basis of non-implementation of those rights of the human being, the rights of the individual citizen. i do not need to tell you all the pressures which have occurred since that moment, but the commission said unanimously that it will start court procedures and will put an ultimatum to france. if france has not answered in a positive, acceptable way before 15 october, this court procedure is going to be implemented. that is the normal way we proceed with all member states. now, what has happened? well, france has given an answer. and this was the first time, it was unique in terms of the way questions are handled, and i believe personally that it was the first moment of the european of the citizens. let historians one day look at that. we are in the middle of the proceedings, we are in the middle of the fight, so we might see it from a different point of view. now objectively, what has france done? france has done exactly what the commission has asked it to do. under the 2004 directive, there are material rights, we also call them procedural rights, which exist for the sake of protecting citizens against an unacceptable action by the authorities when they are imprisoned. and these procedural rights have not been implemented in french law. so we said to france: by 15 october we need to know the ways in which you intend to change french law implementing the 2004 procedural rights and showing us a credible timetable of how you are going to introduce that into french law. well, we got it. we got it one hour before the end of the deadline, but we got it. since 08.00 on saturday morning my experts have been looking at the papers and i have come to the conclusion today that all the points on the basis of law which the commission asked for from france have been answered – though of course not yet applied in national french law, because first they have to go to the senate and then be introduced de facto into french law and applied in real terms. we decided we are happy with what the french authorities gave us, but we cannot close the case, because these promises, these elements of law, these proposed laws are not yet implemented. so we have said that we are freezing the case, but are leaving it open. we are leaving it open until the moment the french government has really applied this legislation de facto in day-to-day proceedings. that is one thing that i think is some kind of a victory. think about everything which has happened. now the french will say there is no problem, there never has been any problem. well, there was a problem and they are bringing us the law which they are going to change. let us see if they do it. i believe they are going to do it. there was a second question and that is how the individuals were treated during the summer period, and whether they had procedural guarantees as individuals, as european citizens, or were discriminated against. why did i not start infringement proceedings like those we started on the basis of the laws? simply because if we want to act, we can only act on the basis of legal evidence. we cannot act just because we have a feeling, because we are persuaded something is wrong. we have to have the legal proof and that is why we have asked the french government to supply us with the dossiers on the individuals. now we have got dossiers on individuals, several piles of them. my experts are analysing those and they have told me they will certainly have supplementary questions to the french government, and they think they will finish this analysis with answers from the government in four weeks’ time. so, as of today, we have these two cases. this is, i think, a very important fact because i would also like to tell members very frankly that the implementation of the 2004 directive on free movement is not brilliant. what we are seeing now, because the commission has been strong, is that all the countries who are not perfect either – not imperfect to the extent of france, but not perfect – are starting to say that they are now going to implement it perfectly. so something has happened. i think that all europe has understood that we are not joking any more and that the rights of the individual, of our citizens, and the values of our society must be handled seriously. that is enough about the french question, because a decision has been taken by the commission on that matter, but it is not finished and is still an open procedure. now to the question on the database allegedly held by the french gendarmerie and possibly containing ethnic elements. first, the commission is closely following developments in these matters. we have again been given assurances by the french authorities that everything is all right, but a different system applies here, because there is a french law here on data protection and the handling of data which is checked in accordance with our rules by the french data protection authority cnil. it is in line with the rules that cnil has carried out an inspection and made a preliminary public report last week. you have seen cnil’s results. i have read them too. the way it is reported sometimes in the press is not complete, because cnil has also said, very seriously, that there might not be ethnic elements, but there are certainly databases which have not been authorised by the authorities. as regards compliance with eu legislation, the information provided has to make sure that the situation is covered by the data protection directive. this might be the case only for immigration-related purposes. for immigration, there are a series of guarantees and safeguards which apply to what we call ‘sensitive data’. sensitive data can only be processed in exceptional cases, in cases of public interest; they are subject to suitable safeguards, and those suitable safeguards have to be provided by the country concerned. should the data processing not come under the data protection directive, then the 2008 framework decision on the protection of personal data processed in the framework of police and judicial cooperation in criminal matters could apply. there we still have a problem because this framework directive applies only as from 27 november this year. so, on the basis of this directive, the powers of the commission are rather limited. i will answer the very concrete questions which have been asked in addition to the french case. are there other member states where we could verify the possible existence of databases containing data on ethnic or racial origins? under the data protection directive, the processing of such sensitive data is authorised by way of exception and has to be notified to the national data protection authorities. the data protection authority in france is cnil. and these exceptions for reasons of substantial public interest also need to be notified to the commission. when such notification is made, the national data protection authority and the commission are in a position to assess if the measures are in line with data protection rules, and here we have the result of the preliminary analysis by cnil which clearly says that such authorisations have not been asked for. so, we should allow the judicial work in france to be done by the judicial authorities which are not just authorised, but also responsible, for doing this kind of work. what about the netherlands? there were several databases where the processing of sensitive data was provided for and was notified by the netherlands to the commission in 2005 and 2006. the most controversial database related to criminal activities of youngsters of caribbean origin. this database has since been deleted. recently, one municipality in the netherlands planned to create an ethnic file, but it cancelled its project in response to the recommendation of the dutch data protection authority. this shows that the system under the directive – whereby the data protection authorities, the national data protection authorities, are responsible – works. by the way, i would like to tell parliament that i am working on the reform of the data protection directive, partly with the aim of reinforcing the independence and the intervention opportunities of the national data protection authorities within a european framework. that will have to be that for the time being: i have to shorten my speech because there is no interpretation after 24.00, so let us cut it off there.

in writing. last wednesday we approved the revision of the framework agreement on relations between the european parliament and the european commission; the european parliament has been asked to make a statement on the situation in the middle east. these new powers of the european parliament are essential and mark a radical change in the european institutional procedure. the strengthening of parliamentary control over the commission, parliament's power to approve international agreements, parliament's participation in the commission's work programme and parliament's participation in the election of the president of the european commission are all major developments in the construction of a more democratic european area. what i also think is fundamental is the additional guarantees we get in terms of the obligation to inform parliament: we will have better access to confidential documents relating to international agreements and negotiations. the european parliament should and must be involved in these 'international procedures', both upstream and downstream. this agreement thus establishes a new balance for a more democratic european area and it is good that all this is laid down in a formal agreement.
in writing. the revision of the framework agreement, approved by a large majority, marks an undeniable step forward in relations between the european parliament and the commission. it is time to reflect rigorously the institutional balance established by the lisbon treaty. among the key elements of this revision, equal treatment between parliament and the council, particularly as regards the exchange of information and access to meetings, should be welcomed. in this respect, i can only welcome the provisions introduced concerning the negotiation of international agreements. how can parliament give its informed consent if it is not informed throughout the negotiation procedure? and meps are indeed determined to make full use of the increased powers they have since the entry into force of the lisbon treaty: i want to see this as evidenced by the rejection of the swift agreement last february. one thing is certain, and that is that we must remain vigilant in order to maintain this new institutional dynamic.

in writing. the european external action service (eeas) is now on track to become a functioning diplomatic corps. parliament has obtained 60% of its staff from the other european institutions, which will ensure a certain degree of independence from the member states. the principle of geographical balance was introduced to ensure an appropriate and significant presence of nationals from all member states. this vote has strengthened the role of the parliament: the heads of the european union delegations appointed in strategically important regions will be heard by the parliament's foreign affairs committee. in addition, parliament will have a say in the use of the eeas budget and its officials will have to undergo specific training on budget management.

in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, we are firmly opposed to the creation of a european external action service. foreign affairs, diplomacy, are matters of national sovereignty. and that is why we voted against all the reports on this subject. a common foreign policy pursued in the sole interest of the european union will inevitably come to conflict with the fundamental interests of one, several or all the member states. on the occasion of a conflict in which countries are drawn against the will of their citizens. the promotion of a policy which is particularly hostile or particularly favourable to a country or group of countries, against the age-old traditions of certain diplomacies or the vital interests of certain members. but worse still, the treaties already provide that all this will be subject to other commitments and constraints, even wider and even global: nato, the un, who knows? so it is not even strong and independent diplomacy that is being offered to us, it is an instrument of submission to foreign leadership on our continent.

in writing. the vote on the estrela report on the rights of pregnant women and young mothers at work will make it possible to harmonise the duration of maternity leave and its remuneration to a minimum. the european parliament has chosen to have a strong negotiating position with the council and has therefore supported the principle of 20 weeks of leave with 100% pay (i would remind you that in sweden maternity leave can be up to 75 weeks, of which 14 weeks are reserved for the mother, the rest being shared with the father). this is a strong gesture for european parents, women and men, who will be helped to find a better balance between family and professional life. it is now up to european governments to examine the budgetary feasibility of such a change and to accept it. in the end, it is likely that the minimum leave will be the one proposed by the european commission and supported by the modem delegation, namely a leave of 18 weeks, which would correspond to the recommendations of the international labour organization (ilo).
in writing. the extension of maternity leave with full pay to 20 weeks is a false good idea. such legislation will undermine the employability of women in companies, who will see it as too much of a burden to bear in the event of maternity. it will also jeopardise the woman's reintegration into the exact position she held before she left. finally, opting for compensation at 100% of the salary over a long period of time is a cost for social security schemes (in a context where the european institutions are strongly calling on states to reduce their public deficits). for these reasons i cannot support this report and i think that we should remain realistic and allow some flexibility for the member states in this respect.
in writing. parliament has just voted in first reading to extend maternity leave to a minimum of 20 weeks across europe, paid at 100% of salary, except for high-wage workers, and the possibility for fathers to take at least 2 weeks of leave when a child is born. it is a victory for the supporters of social europe and a step towards greater equality between men and women in europe. some on the right have used the future costs of these measures as a pretext for rejecting these advances. but helping parents to reconcile family and work life will make it easier for parents to return to work, encourage european births, and protect the health of mothers and infants. the left in parliament, with the portuguese socialist rapporteur edite estrela, held firm, the european right split and the road to progress won. the battle must now be won in the council, where several governments are threatening to block this directive. national parliamentarians should take this up and intervene with their governments so that they do not undo what the european parliament is proposing for a europe that protects the rights of its citizens.

in writing. the maternity leave directive was finally adopted by the european parliament on 20 october. i voted for this text, which represents a real advance for women. the directive still needs to be accepted by the council. the text voted today aims to grant women in the european union a right to 20 weeks of maternity leave, 4 weeks more than in france, where women are currently entitled to 16 weeks of maternity leave. the text also provides for a right to 20 days of paternity leave (more than the 11 days currently granted in france). the directive also provides that women are to receive full pay during their leave. this is a reminder of the importance of the crisis. in addition, the text has a social non-regression clause, which means that if the law of the member states is more protective on certain points, it will continue to apply. so this is progress and i welcome it.
in writing. i am also pleased with the solution found on payment deadlines and welcome the inclusion in the text of the socialist and democratic group's proposal to allow an additional deadline for public health services, whose complex budgetary procedures lead to longer payment deadlines. moreover, while respecting contractual freedom between private enterprises, an important safeguard is provided by prohibiting excessive payment delays for creditors, who are often smes.
in writing. late payment can lead to financial difficulties and even bankruptcy for some companies, especially smes: according to the european commission, late payment costs the european economy around €180 billion annually. other estimates put the cost at $300 billion a year - the equivalent of greece's national debt! in the current economic climate, i am pleased that the council and parliament were able to agree quickly on an ambitious revision of european legislation in this area. the european parliament has had a major impact on this issue. we have made sure that the final text is based on many of the improvements voted for in the committee on the internal market and consumer protection, including: higher statutory interest rates payable in the event of delay; for business-to-business transactions, a default 30-day rule and an extension to 60 days, extendable under certain conditions; for public institutions, a maximum of 60 days; greater flexibility for public health and public medical and social care institutions; and finally, simplification of the compensation for recovery costs (a flat rate of eur 40).
