in writing. the crisis exposed the failings of the economic and monetary union, nearly wiped out the euro, and led to the loss of millions of jobs across the continent. with the report by mrs berès, the european parliament has just adopted a coherent proposal for a strategy to bring europe out of the crisis and to respond to the financial, economic and social shocks it has caused. the establishment of a real financial supervision, which we have begun to adopt but which will have to be considerably strengthened; a financial transaction tax to regulate markets and finance public goods, and reduce government deficits; the coordination of member states' economic policies and budgets for sustainable growth; appointment of a mr or mrs euro, to put a pilot in the euro area and unify its representation in the g20, the imf; the commission has also proposed the creation of a european energy community. it is time for europe to get moving again. that is what the citizens expect. in a world of movement, immobility is decline. that is why we must now move from reporting to action.
in writing. as usual when it comes to the economic, social and financial crisis in this house, mrs berès' report misses the point and focuses on saving the system rather than on challenging it. this report even adds to the profession of faith in the self-regulating virtues of the market, which is pretended to believe that it can be "moralised". it is the belief in the benefits of global competition and the unrestricted free movement of capital and goods. monitoring a system that is not working will not prevent the worst of it. the banking system has shown its cynicism by repaying in advance, in order to avoid having to change its behaviour, including the most scandalous ones, the state aids which had saved it from going under. the whole global financial system, as it stands today, is detrimental to the real economy. it encourages speculation and the creation of complex products, often opaque and potentially toxic. it produces wind-based wealth. it conditions the very short-term strategies of companies, favours shareholders at the expense of other economic actors... you can't just pretend to be watching him. we need to change it.
in writing. beyond the loss of millions of jobs across the european continent and the threats to the euro, the crisis has highlighted the lack of strong and harmonised economic governance within the european union and the failures of financial supervision. i have spoken in favour of this resolution because it seeks to address these problems and calls for the introduction of a financial transaction tax which would have the benefit of limiting speculation in financial transactions, regulating markets, financing public goods and also reducing public deficits. this is a strong measure that i have long called my wishes and i am glad of it.
in writing. i supported the report by my french socialist colleague pervenche bérès on the economic and social financial crisis. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances. with this vote, the european parliament is proving that political responsibility and ambition can go hand in hand. the priority is on employment, because economic recovery is likely to be achieved without a fall in unemployment. the text calls for the establishment of a genuine european energy community. the appointment of a mr/mrs euro responsible for the economic and monetary choices of the union will also be a major step forward. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competition' in the context of the directive.
in writing. the european parliament adopted on wednesday, 20 october, the report of its special committee on the financial, economic and social crisis. we voted against this report with the gue/ngl group because the proposals it contains are quite surreal and do not take into account the social mobilizations that have been taking place for months in the member states of the european union against the austerity plans and the anti-social measures that are destroying social systems and public services, the only measures envisaged to limit the budget deficits of the eu states. it is part of the counter-reform of pensions proposed by nicolas sarkozy and his government which the french social movement has been fighting and denouncing for weeks now. the report therefore continues to praise the stability pact and the measures and policies which we have been denouncing for years and which our fellow citizens increasingly see as failing. the very large majority (501 votes in favour) who voted for this report clearly do not understand the messages of the citizens who have been mobilizing all over europe for weeks against the austerity plans and the counter-reforms that accompany them.
in writing. in adopting the resolution on economic governance, the european parliament recalls its main objectives in the negotiations on the six commission legislative proposals. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament on the subject of the financial perspective. we continue to argue that the introduction of a financial transaction tax would reduce speculation and improve the functioning of the internal market. in addition, the revenue generated by this tax could help finance global public goods and reduce government deficits. this tax should be set on the broadest possible basis, and certainly initially at the level of the european union.
in writing. this is not about improving economic governance at the level of the union, but about putting the economic, budgetary and fiscal policies of the member states under the absolute imperative not of their economic prosperity, but of the interests of the single market and brussels. it is also about the reactivation and worsening of the stability pact, which has been continuously harmful. this is not acceptable, any more than the creation of a common public treasury to administer a european tax, the institutionalisation of a european economic government (for what purpose) is acceptable. it is true that the level of public deficits and public debt, the majority of which is held abroad, is dangerous, both in financial and sovereign terms. but they would probably be less important without your policies, without the obligation for states to borrow from the markets. almost one sixth of the french government's budget is spent on paying interest on its debt. as long as we pay for that, we don't do anything else.

the international maritime organisation. on the second question of overweight and incorrectly stowed containers, there are no eu rules governing the weighing of containers before loading them on ships or procedures covering stowage or lashing. this matter is regulated at national level or through international agreements. the commission does not plan at this stage to take a legislative initiative concerning this issue. however, this could change if international discussions are not successful and there are increased problems with the stability of ships, the strength of ships or losses of containers. before presenting any new proposal, the commission would need to fully assess the impact such a measure would have on shipping operators. today the commission does not have sufficient information concerning this specific matter. concerning the third issue of tracking systems to locate containers at sea, this possibility could be further explored. however, equipping millions of containers with tracking devices would be costly and a proper assessment of the benefits must be carried out before taking a final decision to make such tracking systems mandatory. the commission could also assess the feasibility of clarifying the provisions of directive 2002/59/ec that established the community vessel traffic monitoring system and which obliges the member states to ensure that the master of a ship reports to responsible coastal stations any sight of containers drifting at sea. if the option to ensure the traceability of the containers is to be explored, the cost of such measures should be taken into account. however, such an option could be considered in the framework of the potential development of the traceability of the containers for logistics and security purposes. finally, concerning compensation for the damage caused by lost containers; this can be addressed under directive 2009/20/ec concerning maritime insurance, and directive 2005/35/ec concerning maritime pollution and sanctions in the event of offences covers cases when oil-polluting substances have been dumped into the sea. directive 2004/35/ec concerning environmental liability also establishes strict liability for operators who cause damage to the environment through the transportation by sea of dangerous goods or polluting goods. such operators are obliged to remedy the damage caused to protected species and natural habitats. additional measures to put in place a compensation regime for damages caused by lost containers would need to be closely assessed against the proportionality principle justifying eu action. the commission believes that at this stage the work of the imo to improve standards should be the priority.

in writing. parliament voted in favour of extending the geographical scope of the financial instrument for cooperation with industrialised and other high-income countries and territories. it is an instrument for establishing economic, commercial, academic, scientific and diplomatic relations with major partners in the world economy such as india, china and brazil. we have chosen to give this instrument a wider geographical scope so that it can benefit new countries whose development is accelerating significantly and which will soon be important trading partners for the european economy, such as the countries of asia, central asia, latin america and south africa.
in writing. i abstained on the report on the creation of a financial instrument for the restructuring of the banana sector in the acp countries. firstly, i regret that this financial instrument has a budget of eur 190 million, whereas the acp countries have estimated the minimum needs at eur 500 million to enable them to restructure the sector in order to become competitive. finally, i regret that this report, under the guise of agricultural diversification (an objective which is not much supported by the eu in the economic partnership agreements negotiated with the acp), seeks to frame by means of a financial instrument the rapid disappearance (in three years) of the banana sector in the acp; this will benefit latin american producers who are already leading the world market with over 70% of the export market share. i also did not want to vote against this report because the acp countries and the european banana-producing regions urgently need help to deal with the consequences that have already been felt as a result of the geneva and other bilateral agreements which have reduced the customs duties on latin american bananas from eur 185 per tonne to eur 74 per tonne.

the rapporteur. - mr president, mr minister and president of ecofin, mr commissioner, the text we are debating tonight and which will be put to the vote of parliament tomorrow is the result of a long process. on 30 april 2009, the european commission published its proposal for a directive on alternative fund managers. it aims to establish a secure and harmonised framework at union level for controlling and monitoring the risks posed by money managers to their investors, counterparties, other financial market participants and financial stability and to enable money managers, subject to strict requirements, to provide services and market their funds throughout the internal market. i would like to interrupt, mr president, just to ask if, given the length of our work, i have unlimited time, because i see that the clock has not started, which is fine by me, but i wanted to be honest and tell you that. the text was tabled in parliament almost 14 months ago. it has attracted considerable interest from meps, with a record 1 690 amendments tabled. the trade unions have been very vocal, and the rapporteur has had almost 200 interviews on this text, not to mention interviews with the national authorities. the compromise text under discussion today was a particularly laborious one. half a dozen informal trilogues were held under the spanish presidency during the first half of 2010 to facilitate the exchange of information on the progress of work. no agreement was reached in the council during this period. on 17 may 2010, the economic affairs committee voted by a large majority on the report, which was the result of collective reflection by the members of parliament. parliament introduced proportionality, differentiated rules for the different categories of funds, capital rules protecting target enterprises and employment, and a passport regime for funds and alternative fund managers established outside the european union. a dozen trilogies followed. a specific working group was also set up between the three institutions to deal with the technical aspects of the proposal in several meetings with the belgian presidency and the commission. on 26 october 2010, at the trilogue, which became the final one, held in the active presence of ecofin president didier reynders and commissioner michel barnier, agreement was reached on a compromise text which the rapporteur considered could be put to the vote of parliament. without going into the details of this long technical text, i will highlight the main points: the directive will require alternative fund managers located in the european union to be authorised or registered, to comply with operational and organisational requirements, conduct of business and transparency rules and will subject them to the supervisory and sanctioning power of the competent authorities of the member states and esma. it will give them access to the eu's internal market through an intra-european passport to manage and market their products. in the future, managers located outside the european union will be able to obtain a passport provided they comply with the same obligations as managers based in the european union. the number of meetings and the intensity of the exchanges and negotiations between the rapporteur, the fictitious rapporteurs, the presidency of the day and the commission have enriched the original proposal in many respects. it should be noted that the progress parliament wanted was achieved as the negotiations progressed and, of course, not only at the last trilogue, which was accompanied by adjustments but was decisive from a political point of view. i would like to emphasize here the areas in which parliament's intervention has been decisive. firstly, on two highly political subjects, concerning relations with third countries, the existence and implementation of a passport - which i no longer understand because i have four minutes normally allocated to managers resident outside the european union. specific conditions have been defined for the granting of the passport. as regards private equity, parliament obtained that provisions be inserted in the directive to avoid the potential unbundling of the assets of the target company, as well as specific rules on the information obligations vis-à-vis target companies, their employees or their representatives. i shall not go into a number of provisions which have been obtained in accordance with parliament's wishes, given the lapse of time. i will simply say that parliament would have liked to go further, but it has been able to weigh in on the negotiations so that the role of esma is more asserted. the solutions adopted are nevertheless a significant step forward in improving the european level of control. parliament ensured that the powers of the council and parliament were strengthened in the process of adopting delegated acts by the commission. a majority in parliament would have wanted a very strict framework for passive marketing, or even a ban on it. the inclusion in a recital of the principle that professional investors must exercise due diligence when investing in funds domiciled outside the european union is a significant first step. that is what i wanted to say at the beginning of the debate, mr president, mr minister, mr commissioner. i would like to take this opportunity to thank all those who have contributed to this success. president of the court of auditors. − madam president, honourable members, thank you for all the kind comments that you have addressed to the court on this occasion, as a tribute also to those who whole budget are decreasing. we have also provided you, in particular in the area of cohesion, with more information than last year, because last year we said that at least 11% of the funds should not have been paid; this year we are able to say that the most likely error estimated is indeed over 5%, which we could not say last year, and that at least 3% of the funds should not have been reimbursed. this is the measure of the progress we have found. these are facts. why? what are the reasons behind this? what progress have we achieved? we are not inventing facts; we are not being kind to the commission or kind to the member states. the court is an independent audit institution governed by the treaty. we base our findings on the evidence and it is what we report to this institution, which we have the obligation to assist in this discharge procedure. we are willing to assist you in this work and the main reason for this, as we said in our report, is that on the one hand the systems put in place to manage the funds for this programme period 2007-2013 are performing better. the other reason is that the disbursement of funds for the programming period is only 25% so the financial execution for the period is in our evidence lower than what should be expected. so the combination of these two factors – better performance of the systems on the one hand and lower execution, so fewer payments effectively made, on the other – has given us the situation where we now are. this is where we have this word of caution. we have to see how things evolve now with the systems behaving so well across all the 27 member states and with all the funds to be disbursed in the future. so a word of caution. but i said that we are willing to assist this house, and particularly the committee on budgetary control, in its discharge. our members will assist you with that and provide you with all the information you need. but we are also assisting you through our special reports. you can find audits and other elements which look at the impact of the funding in real life, at how effectively they have been used, and i think that this is very valuable information the rapporteur. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the vote you are about to take concerns one of the key elements of europe's response to the financial crisis, namely the regulation of alternative funds, including hedge funds and private equity. this compromise document, this compromise text, has been drawn up at great length. we have managed to reach a broad agreement and i would like to congratulate the belgian presidency, which has been directly and strongly involved in this matter, in particular through the active presence of the minister at the crucial trilogues, and i would also like to thank commissioner michel barnier, whose action has been particularly useful. i would also like to thank my colleagues, the fictitious rapporteurs, the staff of the secretariat and the experts who have assisted us. it took more than 14 months to complete, and there were 1690 amendments. it was a lot of work, but i believe that we are now arriving at a text which, thanks to the belgian presidency, represents a significant step forward in european financial regulation.

in writing. the financial crisis that has hit the european union hard is the result of the unbridled activity of many investment funds, especially those from the united states. among these, alternative funds, hedge funds , are characterized by aggressive speculation. this seems to be one of the major causes of the disaster, the consequences of which we are still suffering today. in order to protect the european market from the excesses of these alternative funds in the future, i voted in favour of the report by my colleague, mr jean-paul gauzès. this text is a major step forward in financial regulation. with this vote, we are strengthening esma's powers. this european financial market authority will be established on 1 january 2011 and will issue under strict conditions a passport allowing the activity of alternative fund managers located in the european union. the directive requires them to be authorised or registered, to comply with operational and organisational requirements, rules of conduct and transparency. it will submit them to the supervisory and sanctioning powers of the competent authorities of the member states and esma. fund managers located outside the european union will henceforth be subject to the same rules as european funds.
in writing. as growth in the european union is still suffering from the consequences of the 2008 economic crisis, i voted in favour of the jean-paul gauzès report because it helps to streamline the financial system by better regulating investment funds. indeed, hedge funds have been denounced as having contributed to the worsening of the crisis. by creating a system of 'european passport', the european union is imposing a sort of 'code of conduct' on these financial institutions, which will now have to comply with certain conditions within the european area. the single market thus becomes more transparent and more efficient.
in writing. after the parliament's vote, the eu will finally regulate the activity of the most speculative investment funds! how late since poul rasmussen's own-initiative report, which as early as 2008 proposed to impose strict limits on these "black holes of finance". it took the financial crisis for the member states and the majority of parliament to agree to adopt binding legislation on alternative funds. for the first time, these funds, whether or not they are based in europe, will be subject to controls, activity restrictions and greater transparency; the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the draft directive on the protection of the environment. much remains to be done to effectively manage finance in europe; the european authority should be the only competent authority, rather than the national authorities, and companies should be even better protected against speculation. without the conservatives' reluctance, the union could have adopted more stringent and effective legislation. it's just a first step. the text we have adopted will be revised in four years. it will be an opportunity, on the basis of an assessment, to go further to protect the economy and jobs from the damage of speculation.
in writing. new rules for better economic governance continue to be put in place but still not enough the report also calls for the commission to take a more active role in the fight against fraud and for the member states to be given the opportunity to present their own case. alternative investment fund managers, representing nearly usd 1 trillion in assets, play an important role in financing the european economy. even if these funds are not directly at the origin of the financial crisis, their management must not escape the imperative of regulation of all financial services actors. parliament has obtained the inclusion of new chapters on asset allocation and remuneration. , has significantly influenced the rules on the passport system, depositary liability, capital requirements and the use of leverage.
in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of the compromise reached after months of negotiations on the regulation of hedge fund managers. i voted for it because, even if it is insufficient, it would be unacceptable that certain investment funds could still act with impunity, given the role they have played in amplifying and spreading the crisis. i particularly regret the weakness of the provisions on leverage, the weakness of the guarantees for offshore funds that will be able to obtain a passport, the weakness of the obligations incumbent on private equity funds, which often specialise in the dismantling of unlisted companies. i regret that we have to accept that these predators can operate throughout the union with minimal registration and controls. but should we have waited any longer for a text which is not intended to regulate hedge funds but only their managers, and to manage risk rather than prevent speculation?
in writing. i voted for the text on alternative investment fund managers because it is essential to legislate on this part of the financial markets, which implements extremely risky strategies that are harmful to employment and the real economy. many advances are welcome, such as the setting of the remuneration of fund managers so that it does not encourage and reward excessive risk-taking, to name just one example. the directive is clearly a step in the right direction, even if it has some major shortcomings. it is particularly regrettable that the framework is left to national authorities and not to the recently created european authority esma when voting on the financial supervision package. we must remain vigilant and prepare now for the next steps to put markets back at the service of the economy and prevent further financial crises.
in writing. the gauzès report is unfortunately a missed opportunity to effectively regulate the hedge funds which are at the root of the crisis. despite their destructive role and the risk they pose to the current financial architecture, the council and parliament have bowed to the intense lobbying of the financial sector to keep these highly profitable tools for the benefit of a minority. i therefore voted against this report which maintains the possibility for alternative funds based outside the eu to be marketed there without having to comply with the new european rules. it's a gaping hole that's destroying all the progress of this new legislation.
in writing. i would like to welcome the excellent report by jean-paul gauzès on the alternative investment fund managers directive. this report will make it possible to introduce more transparency, supervision and rules of conduct in the regulation of financial markets. this is a successful first step which i hope will be followed by other initiatives aimed at a thorough and comprehensive reform of the financial architecture.
in writing. i vote against this text and the amendments of the european parliament contained therein. this text does not regulate anything, contrary to what it claims. voting for this text would be a victory for the financial lobbies over the general interest of the people.
in writing. the gue/ngl voted against this report on hedge funds. despite the number of pages and the apparent energy of the rapporteur, this report is frighteningly weak. the content of it is simply not up to the challenges we face. the proposals announced are often the opposite of what should be done to avoid a new financial crisis like the one of the subprime mortgages in autumn 2008. it will therefore not allow the european parliament to exert pressure on the commission and the council to stop this policy of budgetary austerity which is gradually destroying all the instruments of social policy. this is a bad sign on the eve of the g20 meeting chaired by nicolas sarkozy.
in writing. regulation (ec) no 539/2001 establishes the list of third countries whose nationals are subject to the visa requirement for entry into the european union. until recently, taiwan and the northern mariana islands were listed in annex i to the regulation and were therefore subject to this visa requirement. since taiwan does not pose any illegal immigration risk or threat to public policy for the union and the northern mariana islands nationals are, as holders of a us passport, citizens of the united states, it has become necessary to move these territories from the restrictive regime in annex i to the more flexible regime in annex ii. i therefore supported the rapporteur's position allowing this transfer.
in writing. on 11 november the european parliament voted in favour of taiwan being added to the list of third countries whose nationals are exempt from the visa requirement for crossing the external borders of the member states, and i am very pleased that this resolution has been adopted. firstly, many other countries in the same geographical area (hong kong, macao, japan, south korea, etc.) have already enjoyed the same visa exemption for some time. secondly and most importantly, visa liberalization is a great way to encourage links and rapprochement between people, between citizens: students, researchers, simple travellers, etc., and i am convinced that it will promote closer cooperation in the fields of education, culture, research, and tourism between the european union and taiwan.
in writing. regulation (ec) no 663/2009 of the european parliament and of the council established the european energy recovery programme (eerp) to contribute to economic recovery by providing a financial envelope of eur 3.98 billion for the years 2009 and 2010. aid for sustainable energy investment is most effective and profitable when concentrated at the local level. that is why i voted in favour of this text. it provides for the creation of a financial instrument to support energy efficiency and renewable energy initiatives that have a rapid, measurable and substantial impact on economic recovery in the union, enhancing energy security and reducing greenhouse gas emissions. the beneficiaries of the instrument are public authorities, preferably at local and regional level, and public or private bodies acting on behalf of those public authorities.
in writing. in the current difficult economic environment, this financial instrument, by allowing €146 million of uncommitted appropriations to be devoted to energy saving, energy efficiency and renewable energy projects by 2014, will help to support growth and stimulate the recovery of economic activity in the eu, while fighting climate change and promoting environmental protection. i support this and i shall vote in favour of the report by my colleague kathleen van brempt.
in writing. the unique relationship between the european union and the united states is one of the strategic pillars of the european union. together representing half the world economy and united by the common values of democracy and human rights, the transatlantic partnership is also a guarantor of global stability. the forthcoming eu/us summit is an important moment in this cooperation. i voted for this text because it emphasises the challenges and obligations of this cooperation. the resumption of dialogue between our two great powers and the promotion of multilateral negotiations, which is the policy of the new administration, will be a major factor in the success of the negotiations. obama also stresses the importance of this text. in this context, it set out guidelines for the next summit, notably on the israeli-palestinian conflict, the iranian nuclear issue, nuclear disarmament and the transatlantic security pact. it also called for the strengthening of the transatlantic economic council and stressed the need to reform the international financial system, develop cooperation in the fields of energy, the environment, intellectual property and consumer protection, and judicial and police cooperation.
in writing. the relationship between the united states and europe is unique and historic. the resolution voted by parliament today, which i supported, underlines the importance of ever greater cooperation between our countries and of a permanent intensification of our relations, particularly in the context of the economic crisis and the terrorist threat to the west. i also welcome the inclusion of the monetary issue in the resolution, which shows our desire to rebuild the international monetary system at a time when currency wars are undermining the growth of the european union. this is a friendly but firm signal to our transatlantic allies on the eve of the opening of the g20 summit.
in writing. the european union and the united states are two areas that have been hit very hard by the economic and financial crisis; the european parliament has been trying to reassert our resolve to find a common response to this crisis and the need to strengthen economic cooperation in order to get out of this difficult period once and for all. i believe that to this end, the completion of a transatlantic market by 2015 is a good way to further develop the economic relationship between our two areas and to be stronger in the face of the upheavals in the global economy. in addition, because the us and the eu are longstanding partners who share many values (democracy, respect for human rights), we want a transatlantic inquiry to be set up to shed light on the allegations of torture in iraq. finally, as the terrorist threat seems to be growing, i would like the eu and the us to cooperate fully in this area, without however adopting measures which might be too intrusive to people's privacy. we wanted to remind you of this in the run-up to the next eu-us summit.
in writing. i supported the resolution in which the european parliament gave its recommendations to the council on how to address transatlantic issues at the next eu/us summit. given the weight of the european union and the united states in the world economy and the current economic situation, it is essential that the two partners intensify their cooperation in order to promote growth and employment. that is why i particularly supported the two oral amendments tabled by my colleague, mr elmar brok, which stressed the need for better coordination of monetary policies in the transatlantic relationship. these two amendments are to be linked to the debate which is opening up in the g20 on the risks to all the economies of our planet posed by 'currency wars' and any national monetary initiative which could destabilise the exchange rate balance. any 'competitive devaluation' or 'competitive undervaluation' must be avoided, since they undermine the necessary international economic and monetary cooperation.
in writing. the resolution on transatlantic relations as adopted is a plea for a special relationship with the united states. the european union is also committed to the creation of a transatlantic market by 2015 and to the political objective of 'defending a common cause'. this common cause, which involves increased cooperation in afghanistan, closer integration with nato missions and compliance with us demands for the sharing of european citizens' banking data via the swift agreement, is why i voted against this text.
in writing. the only merit of this resolution is that it advocates the universal abolition of the death penalty and calls on the united states to join the international criminal court. other than that, it's unacceptable. how can parliament support the creation of the transatlantic single market, this gigantic project which has been set up behind the backs of the citizens of europe? how can it welcome the swift agreement, the transfer of pnr data, the 'open skies' agreement between europe and the united states, the greenhouse gas emission allowance exchange and the anti-democratic institutions preparing for gmt? i vote against perjury in the public interest and democracy.
in writing. transatlantic relations are of paramount importance to europe, and i supported this resolution on the priorities for the next eu-us summit. in particular, efforts to implement the un reform agenda in the field of global governance must be intensified. in addition, it is essential to achieve an ambitious and binding post-2012 greenhouse gas emissions regime. in addition, in the area of financial stability, the comparability of accounting standards at global level is crucial and progress must be made in this direction. on the other hand, regulatory standards established in one area should serve as a reference for others, thus leading to an ever-increasing density of international financial regulation.
in writing. the european union has signed agreements with various states on the exchange of passenger name record (pnr) data in order to meet air safety requirements. the lisbon treaty also gives the charter of fundamental rights a binding force, which protects the personal information of european citizens. when these trade agreements are renewed, parliament is called upon to give its approval to the new agreements negotiated. two needs clash on this issue. on the one hand, the fight against organised crime and terrorism, which is being multiplied by the new means of communication, and on the other hand, the protection of privacy and fundamental freedoms, which are being jeopardised by these same means of communication. i felt it was important to support this text, which continues transatlantic cooperation against organised crime and terrorism while leaving ample room for the necessary guarantees of the freedoms of european citizens.
in writing. the transmission of passenger name record (pnr) data is an important element in the fight against terrorism and transnational crime. however, the number of countries requiring airlines to provide pnr data is constantly increasing, and it is therefore necessary to closely monitor the misuse of personal information of european citizens for other purposes in the light of european data protection rules. i therefore fully support the resolution adopted today by the european parliament, which aims to provide a strict framework for the transfer of passenger data to third countries. these countries will have to provide guarantees on the use, storage and collection of this data, which should prevent misuse and respect the rights of our citizens.
in writing. to safeguard the security of international transport, especially in the face of the risk of terrorism, it is essential that states can exchange passenger information - pnr data, collected by air carriers. but it is equally crucial that these provisions do not infringe the fundamental freedoms of citizens and do not lead to discrimination against certain people on the grounds of their origin or religion. the protection of personal data must therefore be better guaranteed. the european parliament, before the commission starts negotiating the terms of exchange of pnr data with the usa, canada and australia, has a clear requirement: the protection of personal data is too sensitive a subject for these negotiations to take place at the level of the member states alone and in opacity. they must be conducted in a transparent manner at eu level. the data transmitted should be used only within a strictly defined framework and should not be transmitted to a third country. many information will have to be excluded from the collectable data, especially those related to ethnic origin and religious beliefs.
in writing. the protection of personal data is a sensitive area in eu-us relations, as in the case of the agreement on bank data transfers (swift report). a general eu-us agreement on data protection is currently under discussion, as is a new agreement on the sharing of air passenger name records (pnr). in voting today's joint resolution, parliament has just reiterated its demand that pnr data collected should not be used for data mining or profiling purposes under any circumstances. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of personal data. if parliament is not heard, it will have the opportunity to exercise its right of veto.
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution on the global strategy for the transfer of passenger data to third countries, as there is a need to establish a binding legal framework for these transfers, which are increasingly being used in the fight against terrorism. in preparing for these negotiations with the usa, canada and australia, parliament set out its conditions. we are asking in particular that the data cannot be used for profiling purposes and that the negotiation be conducted in the greatest transparency vis-à-vis parliament. parliament's role in the process of european integration is to be strengthened. the protection of privacy is a sensitive issue which must not be sacrificed to the other necessity of the fight against terrorism. as in the negotiation of the swift agreement, parliament will be able to ensure that citizens' privacy is respected.
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution on the eu's external strategy on passenger name record (pnr) data, as i believe that the conclusion of agreements allowing the exchange of information on pnr data between the european union on the one hand and canada, the united states and australia on the other hand is of paramount importance for international security. i therefore welcome the commission's recommendation to authorise the opening of negotiations for the conclusion of these agreements. the usefulness of the exchange of such data in the fight against terrorism and international crime has been established for several years. these international transfers of pnr data provide law enforcement agencies in our states with valuable tools in the fight against the terrorist threat. it is also necessary to emphasize that the new overall approach to pnr data presented by the commission last october, which aims to set general criteria specific to all pnr agreements, is in my view very positive. it will provide a more structured and coherent framework for these agreements and provides for significant guarantees in terms of the protection of personal data.
in writing. this resolution is in total contradiction to the one this house adopted last may. it 'welcomes' (sic) the commission's proposal of last september. the commission shall be empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with article 26 to supplement this regulation by laying down detailed rules for the exchange of pnr data between member states. worse, their unlimited storage for profiling purposes is considered legitimate! what are the thoughtful remarks in this resolution against a practice that is at the heart of a project it endorses? i am voting against this resolution which infringes the right of every human being to have his personal data respected.
in writing. according to the commission's estimates, demographic changes are likely to profoundly alter the structure of the population and the age pyramid. the number of young people aged 0 to 14 will rise from 100 million to 66 million by 2050. the working age population is expected to peak at 331 million by 2010 and then decline steadily (to around 268 million by 2050). faced with this situation, the european union must respond adequately to safeguard employment for both older and younger people. i voted in favour of this own-initiative report by the european parliament which calls on the member states to consider the possibility of abolishing the mandatory retirement age but also outlines a policy to combat discrimination, to set as an objective lifelong learning, to develop a reflection on new forms of work organisation in enterprises, particularly to reduce stress. the resolution also contains a number of initiatives, such as the fight against youth unemployment and for a decent retirement, and a european pact for people over 50.
in writing. there was a lot of good in thomas mann's own-initiative report on the demographic challenge and solidarity between generations, including the importance of the generational pact in our present societies, youth unemployment and the need to tackle the challenges facing older people and young people in parallel. i voted against the resolution, however, because some of its paragraphs were unacceptable, particularly on the subject of pensions. fortunately, the one explicitly mentioning the need to replace the systems of financing pensions by distribution with systems of financing by capitalisation was rejected by a large majority in parliament, but another, which called on 'the member states to reconsider the possibility of abolishing the compulsory retirement age', was adopted. that is completely unthinkable! if greater flexibility is to be ensured in the pension system, the retirement age must remain a fundamental pillar! the commission's consultation on the future of pensions in europe is coming to an end, and the message from parliament is particularly important. that is why i have decided to vote against the resolution.
in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, it is a pity that the mann report, which also contains good things about promoting policies in favour of families, reconciling work and family life, access to employment for young people and the elderly, etc., still fails to promote immigration as a solution, even a partial one, to the ageing of our countries, or even to financing pensions. in all countries, including france, studies show that this is not the case. not just demographically, but financially. even mrs tribalat, a french demographer who can hardly be accused of sympathy for the front national, comes to these conclusions. i know that in this chamber we like to believe, according to the slogan of the sos racisme association, that "mohamed will pay for maurice's pension" .... for karl, for matthew or for juan! but that's not true. all over the place. mr mann should also be careful when he advocates replacing our allocation systems with capitalisation systems. given the current context of global financial crisis, this is the kind of proposal that can lead our elders to ruin, to the benefit of a few madoffs.
in writing. solidarity between generations is one of the main social challenges of european and national policies for the coming years, and in the face of the ageing of the european population. this report rightly stresses this value of solidarity, the need for solidarity between generations, the importance of the pact between generations, and it contains very positive elements, for example on reconciling work and family life and the organization of working time, particularly for women, on access to employment for young people and the elderly, on the fight against discrimination... on the other hand, there are many points in the report with which i do not agree: paragraph 24 which calls for the abolition of the compulsory retirement age, several passages on flexibility in the organization of work and the simplification of social law, and a passage on the abolition of early retirement schemes. i therefore preferred to abstain from voting on this report. i am also pleased that the proposal to replace the system of financing pensions by distribution with a system of financing by capitalisation has nevertheless been rejected by the european parliament.
in writing. i voted against the report on the demographic challenge and solidarity between generations because it contained unacceptable positions. there are some particularly interesting points in this text, such as the need not to oppose the employment of young people and the retention of older people in the labour market, and the emphasis on lifelong learning and the fight against age and gender discrimination in the labour market. but the text also contains many recommendations concerning pension systems which i cannot endorse: the text calls on the member states to abolish the legal retirement age and stresses the need to reduce the burden of public debt, which is tantamount to encouraging private pension funding systems, which are particularly unfair. the report also calls on the member states to increase the employment rate by developing parttime work, which only increases the level of precariousness. these are some of the reasons why i voted against this text.
in writing. i voted against the mann report because it is imbued with a liberal logic which takes the pretext of the ageing of the european population to advocate reforms of public social protection systems in europe, particularly by attacking the health and pension systems by way of distribution, encouraging their privatisation and a reduction in the age of retirement, which i reject.
in writing. the report argues that the extension of life expectancy should not result in a decrease in workers' rights. yet, that is what he is advocating all along. the european parliament will be committed to the following measures if it votes in favour of this report: raising the retirement age to the latest possible date beyond the 64 years promised by the europe 2020 strategy, promoting precarious employment, replacing the distribution pension with funded pension systems. i vote against this nameless social regression.
in writing. i voted against this report which once again shows the inability of the majorities governing europe to listen to the demands of the european citizens. although the european union has no competence in these matters, which are the exclusive competence of the member states, mr mann is undermining both the social acquis and the principle of subsidiarity. the report also calls on the member states to encourage people over 60 to stay longer at work by adapting workplaces to their health. the elderly must first and foremost have the right to a decent pension, which allows them to live with dignity. in addition, adaptation to the needs of end-of-career workers is mainly achieved through early retirement schemes, which mr mann purely and simply wanted to dismantle. i am, however, pleased that a passage explicitly calling for the replacement of the system of distribution by capitalisation has been rejected by the european parliament. under the guise of intergenerational solidarity, mr mann even felt the need to stress that older people must be treated equally as human beings with fundamental rights. in writing. it is essential to encourage researchers and investors to stay in europe. the fight against brain drain must remain a priority for the european union. to do this, we will have to reorient and simplify the administrative and financial aspects of the research framework programmes. the financial resources must be allocated more directly to our companies, universities and research laboratories. the research funding system, too focused on control, leads to a waste of resources. as the report points out, the general trend should be towards a reduction in average time to commit and pay in order to stimulate participation in these research programmes. we must fight against the administrative blockade which hinders the proper functioning of these programmes.

member of the commission. − mr president, the commission is deeply concerned by the deterioration of the cholera situation in haiti. the number of casualties among the hospitalised cases is increasing sharply day by day. the number of people admitted to hospitals comes to more than 20 000. at the end of last week more than 1 100 people had already lost their lives. but it is feared that these figures are severely underestimated. the fatality rate is very high and shows that people arrive too late at health centres. cholera treatment is simple, but early access to treatment is key to limiting fatalities. treating cholera patients also requires considerable human resources. the haitian public health system is now seriously overstretched, despite substantial support from the international community. médecins sans frontières, as one of the front-line medical actors, is calling on all groups and agencies present in haiti to step up the size and speed of their efforts. the whole country is now affected. the epidemic is spreading at an alarming rate in the capital, port-au-prince. slums such as cité soleil are especially prone to contagion due to very bad hygiene conditions and poor access to clean water. we are focusing on saving lives through prompt treatment of those affected, increasing access to clean water, promoting better hygiene behaviour and supporting epidemiological surveillance in order to know where and how the epidemic is evolving. the commission has reinforced its humanitarian presence with relevant medical expertise and mobilised funds – eur 12 million – to support partners in haiti. the european mechanism for civil protection has also been activated through the monitoring and information centre of the european commission and has already co-financed the transport of in-kind assistance provided by france. another offer from austria has just entered the pipeline. an eu civil protection and technical support team with member states’ experts is to be deployed early this week. experts from the european centre for disease prevention and control have been deployed by dg sanco to assess the best way to reinforce epidemiological surveillance in haiti, and further cooperation is under consideration. after the recent incidents related to civil unrest in cap haitien and port-au-prince, we are following closely the security situation with our partners and the relevant un agencies, particularly ahead of the presidential elections of 28 november. the commission was in touch with the un under-secretary general for humanitarian affairs and emergency relief coordination, baroness amos. we fully support her in stressing the importance of allowing national and international aid workers to continue lifesaving activities without disruption. considering the serious and rapid deterioration of the cholera situation, further contributions are urgently required to fill gaps in health, water, sanitation, hygiene and logistics. priorities include medical personnel and other personnel specialised in water, sanitation and hygiene, as well as medical supplies, beds, water purification units and tablets. the commission is therefore in contact with the belgian presidency and the member states to encourage further eu support to help haiti at this very critical and difficult time. eu support can be channelled through the eu civil protection mechanism. the endless efforts of haitian and international aid workers to meet the current challenges on the ground are commendable, but it is clear that mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to thank the european commission and the belgian presidency for their open, cooperative and, in short, european spirit. in these times of crisis, let us not forget the preservation of the future. last year, the virtue contest between governments was about who would spend the most. everybody was standing on the gas. this year, it's the opposite. everybody's standing on the brakes. that's good! parliament accepts the figure imposed on the council by the most thrifty or stingy member state, but on the condition that there is agreement on preserving the future. the union no longer has the resources to finance its budget. instead of being the primary instrument of solidarity between europeans, the community budget has become the place where conflicting national interests clash. the treaty of lisbon has now been in force for one year. it gives the union the new powers it has long been waiting for. however, no additional resources were able to be entered in the 2010 budget, nor will any be entered in 2011. the same applies to the europe 2020 action programme. at a time when all member states are engaged in policies of massive public expenditure cuts, there is a huge interest for them to identify and exploit the potential savings that can be made by the pooling of certain expenditure, either between several states or at the level of the 27 member states. europe, the european vision, european benchmarking can help us to spend less. that is why the european parliament is proposing an agreement between our three institutions on a method of working together on all these proposals for the future. i would add, on my own behalf, that we will save time by involving the national parliaments, which have fiscal and budgetary sovereignty.

madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, a great deal has been said, because the bee is indeed a symbolic species, a sentinel species of our nature. many research programmes are now devoted to the bee, with sometimes contradictory results. a few days ago, a scientist came to me and explained that the swarms of planes that we see in the sky have an effect on the diffraction of the sun's rays and lead to over-fatigue and therefore to over-mortality of the bee, for example. i believe that, contrary to what was said earlier by a member of the right of this house, we have here an example of a sector in which the pooling of our knowledge and the coordination of research programmes can provide a solution to the problems of each of our countries. yes, europe can be useful. perhaps this example of bees is a symbol of our common construction.
in writing. the text proposed by the committee on agriculture and rural development on support for the beekeeping sector is particularly relevant in the context of the post-2013 cap reform. as bee mortality is increasing and the number of beekeepers in europe is decreasing, it is urgent to take stock of the difficulties faced by the sector and put in place the appropriate measures. this is crucial to combat the very likely negative consequences on our food production, since we know that 84% of plant species depend on bee pollination. so the first step in tackling the decline of bees is to get a better understanding of the phenomenon through increased research on bee mortality. secondly and additionally, we call on the commission to expand its support for the beekeeping sector and to renew existing support programmes before their scheduled completion in 2012.

in writing. the european council in october took a further step in the subjugation of nations and the dispossession of their sovereignty. first, with pseudo-economic governance, which is really economic supervision: the obligation for the states to have their budgets approved in advance by officials in brussels; the monitoring of their economic policies as a whole; automatic preventive sanctions, even before the authorized debt and deficit ceilings have been exceeded; the possible suspension of the voting rights of the failing state... all in compensation to germany for keeping the financial stabilization fund afloat. but this mechanism is only a right of the states and the brussels commission to go into debt, or to guarantee loans, on the markets, in favour of states in difficulty because they are victims of... market speculation against their sovereign debts! and what's more, because of their membership of the eurozone. we are dreaming! the european council also decided on a reform of the treaties to set up a crisis management mechanism. for the first time, the simplified revision procedure will be used, this anti-democratic method which does not provide for any parliamentary debate. this is not governance, this is totalitarianism.
president of the council. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the presidency of the council and the european parliament had already had the opportunity to discuss the g20 on 20 october last, and we were at that time on the eve of the g20 ministerial meeting and waiting for what was going to happen in seoul. as europeans, we have prepared well for these meetings, both at ministerial level and at the level of heads of state and government. we have understood that the lack of cohesion among europeans would very quickly lead to the european union's credibility being exhausted on the international scene. the comments from around the world were mixed, admittedly, about the seoul summit. i think we must continue to be optimistic, even if the results are not as spectacular as we would have liked. we were convinced, before seoul, that the hardest, most important test was not to lose our momentum. we should not make the mistake of thinking that we no longer need to coordinate globally because we are not in the critical situation we were in a year and a half ago, or even six months ago. we still believe that political leaders have the responsibility to make decisions. that's right, that's the essence of politics. but i think they also have another, even more important, responsibility: to ensure that these decisions do not remain on paper but produce tangible effects and are carried out. the seoul summit has shown that the real challenge for the g20, and therefore for all of us, is now to understand how to pursue and even accelerate implementation. it is necessary to move from good intentions to concrete results, and all this is important for at least two reasons. the first is that markets do not just make statements. they are watching the developments that are happening in the concrete two, ten, thirty days after the summit, when the media have taken their cameras off the stage. the state of health of the european economy must be seen in a global context and not just as a result of the progress achieved in two summit days. the progress we are aiming for can only be achieved through daily and constant work, and as members of the european parliament you know this better than anyone. the second reason is just as important and directly affects you. i believe that the european parliament and national parliaments can play a role both of control and of political impetus on the european and international economic agenda by ensuring that this implementation work, between one summit and the next, is carried out successfully and that the g20 becomes more and more a process rather than a series of meetings. in substance, the union's contribution to strong, sustainable and balanced growth is now clear and is based on a number of principles: fiscal consolidation plans aimed at sustainable and differentiated growth, the europe 2020 strategy for the structural reforms needed to support in particular job creation, the financial sector and market reform agenda and, finally, the strengthening of the union's economic governance. i would add that the union is very interested in the peer review process within the g20. as europeans we are used to this and we know how useful this kind of exercise can be. clearly, everyone must play their part and show a renewed willingness to contribute to the framework for action for growth. i would like to say again, in the spirit of my previous remarks, that the battle against protectionism cannot be won once and for all but by maintaining a certain level of global alertness day after day. the commission has already made a number of proposals in this area. the first is the reform of the international monetary fund, since the europeans have made it clear that they are ready to do their part to make the new imf more representative of the new international economic reality and thus to make the emerging economies' voices heard and play a greater role. we have agreed to reduce our presence on the imf's executive board and have made substantial concessions in terms of quotas. i think we also kept what we held most dear, and in general, the international community won. the second development concerns the so-called basel iii agreement. i think that on the capital requirements for banks we are moving in the right direction, and it is of course essential that this commitment to implement basel iii is actually being fulfilled by all the states concerned. it is clear in this respect that the issue of implementation will remain on the political agenda of the union and also of the g20. finally, if i look at what has happened in recent weeks with regard to the so-called currency war, i think that the european union has done a good job and has been able to defend a balanced position which is to say that exchange rates must reflect economic fundamentals and that competitive devaluations should not be used. finally, france now has the responsibility of the g20 presidency from seoul and i think this is a unique opportunity for europeans and for the european union as such. it will be very important to work together in a coordinated way to ensure that throughout the next year, and in the run-up to the cannes summit in november 2011 and beyond, the g20 remains true to the expectations it has created. the real challenge before us is to demonstrate that a forum created to deal with the crisis is also capable of providing the contribution and impetus needed to achieve medium-term objectives such as new, more sustained, strong and balanced global growth, clear and fair rules for the international financial market, and international organisations that are more representative of today's world and better able to assist national governments and european institutions in managing globalisation. i believe that it is up to the g20 to demonstrate in the coming years that this globalisation is not only economic but also, and above all, political.
president of the commission. − mr president, before this month’s seoul summit there was concern that once the pressure of the crisis which brought g20 countries together was receding, the g20 would find it impossible to fulfil its role as the primary forum for global economic coordination. after this month’s seoul summit i can reassure you that that negative scenario was not confirmed. we have seen the g20 move from crisis mode to a more stable approach to global governance. despite difficult issues under discussion and the fact that some other issues like the taxation of the financial sector were not agreed, the g20 once again delivered an important message of global determination; it made real and steady progress on addressing global economic challenges. i know the results were received with some scepticism because there was no spectacular, last-minute breakthrough perfectly timed for the evening news. but what the sceptics fail to understand is that the g20 process itself is spectacular news; it is not like our european, more integrated process where everyone round the table shares a common culture of negotiation and compromise. apart from the european union and some of its member states, the g20 includes countries as diverse as the us and china, russia, brazil and japan, argentina, saudi arabia, korea, south africa. the very fact that they are engaged in a joint process of addressing global imbalance and agreeing, for example, on financial regulation, should be recognised for what it is: enormous progress that would simply have not been possible some years ago, and the seoul summit was an important further step in that process and the launching of a new agenda, not a one-off spectacular event. so, yes, it was a success and i think the european union, represented by myself and the president of the european council, can be satisfied with the summit conclusions. in fact, we made a very important contribution also at finance minister level where the european union was represented by olli rehn, the commissioner responsible for that area. on the whole, the conclusions reflect the priorities the european union set out ahead of seoul and the european union should be proud of the very important contribution it is making to this process. let me highlight some of the key achievements: first and foremost, the european union wanted this summit to make progress on joint action to boost global growth and jobs and to give answers on how to address global imbalances and currency tensions. we all knew it would be an uphill struggle to find a commonly agreed way to tackle global imbalances, but the g20 after long, hard negotiations opted for a cooperative solution setting in place a mechanism and a timeline which brings our economies together to address this issue. the g20 partners committed to reducing excessive imbalances and to maintaining current account imbalances at sustainable levels. do not underestimate the significance of this. the g20 discussion on how to address imbalances showed that the eu is ahead of the curve. the results of our own thinking on european union internal imbalances inspired g20 leaders as the best way to tackle global imbalances. our method of using indicators to trigger an assessment of macroeconomic imbalances and their root causes is at the basis of the new g20 mechanism. it will be set up by mid-2011, with the first assessment before the next summit in november 2011. our focus now will be on strengthening this mechanism as much as possible and ensuring it is properly applied during the french g20 presidency in 2011. so, the conclusions were important but i agree that now we have to see how they will be implemented. the second achievement relates to currency rates. there will be no success in rebalancing growth without addressing currency tensions. once again the european union helped to build a g20 consensus on cooperative solutions. we have agreed to move towards more market-determined exchange rate systems that reflect underlying economic fundamentals. we also agreed to refrain from comparing the evaluations and to be vigilant against excess volatility and disorderly movements in exchange rates. this resolve provides political momentum for the french g20 presidency that will take up a comprehensive reform of the international monetary system. i am also happy to see that the g20 summit endorsed the historic reform of the imf. indeed, we have exceeded the pittsburgh expectations on the quota shift and on the representation of emerging economies. thanks to the open and cooperative approach of eu member states, our significant concessions and our ability to share responsibility means that the fund now has the legitimacy it needs to take on the challenging tasks ahead, particularly addressing imbalances and currency tensions. emerging economies now have to prove that in return for increased representation, they are willing to shoulder increased responsibility for global economic governance. a fourth achievement at the summit was keeping up the momentum for global financial regulatory reform, with a clear focus on implementation. we welcome the endorsement of the basel iii reform and the fact that the g20 will continue to work on systemically important financial institutions. the g20’s financial reform efforts will continue in areas like macro-prudential policy frameworks, shadow banking, commodity derivative markets and market integrity and efficiency. the european union is in the lead on many of these points and our internal work will feed into the g20 process. it is now important to ensure strict and consistent implementation of all these commitments according to the agreed timetable, to ensure a global level playing field. we have received strong assurances from the united states that they share our determination on this. the seoul summit also created new momentum to conclude the doha round and reiterated the g20 commitment to fight protectionism in all its forms. an achievement which gives me personal satisfaction is that with the seoul development consensus interlocking development, trade and investment, we have firmly placed development on the g20 agenda. this new growth-oriented approach will complement existing donor focus activities and the united nations system. it will boost our efforts to achieve the millennium development goals and it is perfectly in line with the commission’s recent proposals in its green paper on the future of development policy. this green paper is now open for consultation and i look forward to input from this house. finally, i strongly welcome the g20’s commitment to the g20 anti-corruption action plan, to future work on energy-related issues and
