for the greens/efa group mr president, i should like to concentrate my remarks on mr luhan's report. we agree with mr luhan on at least one point: regional cohesion policies have a key role to play in europe for a balanced economic development, socially harmonious and ecologically efficient, that is, ultimately globally competitive. i would also like to thank mr luhan for having incorporated some of our amendments which are aimed at the establishment of a sustainable low-carbon economy which respects biodiversity. however, we will not be able to vote on its resolution because the vision it develops of cohesion policy as an instrument of global competitiveness remains too narrow, too limited, too insufficient in our view. we have two obstacles: firstly, the rapporteur relies almost exclusively on quantitative schemes translated into infrastructure as a growth engine, plus is his fundamental criterion. we do not think that is appropriate for the present situation. for example, it identifies 246 operational programmes in research and development and welcomes them, without asking about their content. it's good to look, but you have to know what you're looking for. second obstacle: the rapporteur does not make clear enough the projects; we would like a strong choice to face the challenges that his report lists, the choice of a green economy, the choice of a green new deal that would be the only one that would be able to pull europe and its regions upwards.
in writing. there is now a very strong threshold effect between the regions eligible for the convergence objective and the others. this is extremely damaging for a number of regions which, although not poor, are not rich. it would be particularly appropriate to mitigate this threshold effect by creating an intermediate category of regions, between the 'convergence' and 'regional competitiveness and employment' objectives. i am glad that this proposal is included in the conclusions of the fifth cohesion report. this intermediate category could be targeted at regions with a gdp per capita between 75% and 90% of the community average. i also hope that this system will replace the transition mechanism and also take into account regions which are not affected by an exit from the convergence objective. in the context of the negotiations on the next multiannual financial framework, this new architecture of cohesion policy will have to be done on a constant budget. i would remind you, however, that just over 20 regions are expected to be excluded from the convergence objective, which will lead to savings of eur 10 billion per year. these amounts could very well be reallocated to a new intermediate category of regions.
in writing. the luhan and manescu reports rightly recall the principles which must guide our cohesion policy. however, i would like to stress three areas where we need to be more ambitious. firstly, territorial cohesion, which is a very important aspect of the community's development. the concept is often cited but rarely translated into concrete actions. we must, for example, pay particular attention to the border areas. the handicaps and difficulties faced by these regions reflect the limits of european integration. we need to turn these fracture territories into seam territories. secondly, the unequal treatment of regions which are between objective 1 and objective 2. some regions, with the same gdp, have aid intensities ranging from 1 to 10. it is time to put in place a transitional mechanism that treats fairly all regions whose gdp is between 75% and 90% of the community average. finally, work is needed on new performance indicators. the development challenges of regions depend on their territorial constraints. we need to refine our criteria at all levels of governance to truly measure regional development needs and objectives.
the rapporteur. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, why a report on advertising? because advertising, it can be the worst as it can be the best. the worst is if it is lying, if it is intrusive, if it is misleading, if it does not play its part, if, in the end, it does not provide what the consumer expects from it, that is to say, information. the best, because advertising is also a great tool for economic development. advertising is a kind of lubricant for the economy, as some have said, advertising is also an element that provides the consumer, when done well, with comparison points, and it stimulates, in a certain way, competition. so advertising is not something new, and why a new text, when there are already texts? for a number of reasons. first, because today's advertising is not yesterday's advertising. i recently read a report from the united states, but in europe the situation is quite similar: on 29 november last, in one day, online commerce accounted for more than one billion dollars in turnover. so that's a huge increase in online commerce and online advertising tools. and one of the reasons for this report is that the texts which regulate advertising are sometimes totally unsuitable for the tools which have emerged in recent years. advertising can be intrusive, and it is increasingly so, invading privacy. advertising is another very new element which is not dealt with in the texts. advertising can be hidden. the ad may not say his name. there is this famous example on facebook, on social networks a new tool that is not addressed by legislation , we see groups of people appearing who denounce this or that supposed defect of this or that product. all of this is capable of literally destroying a brand in a matter of days or weeks. so, you can see that yesterday's advertising is not today's advertising at all, that this one uses tools that did not exist - i think about behavioral advertising, targeted advertising, reading your private emails. who here wants, who here wants their private e-mails read? well, that's the way it is today for advertising purposes. i think that we should think about some very simple values: respect for privacy, protection of the most vulnerable, because we know very well that children are among the most vulnerable to receive what is called behavioural advertising, that is to say, targeted advertising. these children do not understand that this is not just a simple advertisement that comes to their home by chance. it's an ad targeted to their particular desires. as much as an adult could understand it, a child cannot. well, new technology, new challenges - and considerable economic challenges. we are in the midst of a real political debate. the question is solved, if we listen to some professionals who do not want to touch the world of advertising. and it's true that we hear some professionals tell us that basically, consumers are warned by broad and extremely detailed privacy policies on websites. in fact, it is well known that these long, incomprehensible privacy policies are not read, and when they are read, they are not understood, they are even illegible. it is clear that the bottom line is always the same: advertising must be fair, respectful of others, respectful of privacy. the consumer must not be spied on, must not be targeted without his knowledge. the consumer, the citizen, must be respected. mr president, and i will end here, we must therefore have two objectives. first, fairer, more fair, more respectful, more effective advertising, more respectful of privacy, but also of citizens, that is to say, of consumers, better informed, not manipulated, better informed, with a sharper critical mind. that's the whole point of this report. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i hope that you will accept this report and vote in favour of it in general in this house.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, madam rapporteur, this text is of course very complex, but what is it really about? it is a question of drawing the lessons of the crisis once again: no, we must not do things as before, yes, we must change the rules of the game, we must put the system in order. those who today in the various countries of the union are taking advantage of the crisis and the anxiety of the citizens to blame everything on europe, we hear everywhere: 'if europe is not working, it is because of the euro, and besides, i have the solution, we must leave europe, we must put an end to the euro ...'. we must tell all these people again and again that we need common rules, that if the countries of europe were not united, if they were isolated, they would be dead today. yes, we need regulation, common policy, common rules, a flattening of our rules and a better functioning of the system. my dear colleagues, the matter is quite simple at bottom, together we are strong, alone we are dead!

for the gue/ngl group mr president, i would like to thank our rapporteur for his attention and his work, as well as all the fictitious rapporteurs who have contributed to the quality of this report. we consider this report to be important because it draws the consequences of one of the few positive aspects of the implementation of the lisbon treaty, if it is actually implemented. the effective implementation of fundamental rights in the european union is an important, even fundamental, issue for the future of the european union. but we must not just talk to ourselves. the treaty, the charter of fundamental rights and, soon, accession to the european convention on human rights, can provide us with new tools in this field and enable the european union and its members to take a new step. many say that human rights are among the essential values of the european union, but few have a truly universal and indivisible conception of them. indivisible, that is to say that all the human rights recognized in the charter, but also in the european convention, and in all the european and international conventions which follow from the universal declaration of human rights, have the same value whatever they may be. there is no primacy of civil and political rights over economic and social rights. the right to live with dignity is as important as religious freedom, for example. universal means that human rights are the same for all, regardless of nationality, regardless of legal status. we know that the right to education, the right to family life, for example, are also constantly being violated in almost all the member states. the situation with regard to the roma is unfortunately emblematic of this. so yes, the commission must decide to launch infringement name many others. so yes, there is a fundamental issue here, it is the credibility of the european union and the future of its foreign policy.

in writing. on the basis of the report by my german colleague, reimer böge, i voted in favour of the proposal for a decision of the european parliament and of the council on the mobilisation of the european union solidarity fund to the amount of eur 67 million to provide assistance to madeira (portugal), which was affected by landslides and floods, and to france, which was affected by floods following the storm xynthia in february 2010. i note that the amount represents 2.7% of the total direct damage estimated at eur 2.5 billion. naturally, this is a significant amount of funding, but i cannot help but wonder whether, in view of the relatively small amount (2.7% of the total damage), the european union should not, with this fund, finance a european civil protection force that could immediately act in support of affected citizens to deal with situations of extreme brutality that exceed national intervention capacities. this force would not cost very much money, as it would initially involve the coordination of existing national civil protection forces. it could also be used for operations abroad (such as haiti).

in writing. in my view, the european union solidarity fund, like the globalisation adjustment fund, is one of the budgetary tools that most concretely embodies the value of 'solidarity' that we, the socialist meps, strive to promote in the formulation of community policies. on 27 and 28 february 2010, the storm xynthia caused the death of 53 people and injured nearly 80 in the vendée and charente-maritime. a real regional and national trauma, its psychological and economic impacts are still felt 10 months later. as early as its march 2010 plenary session, parliament had been mobilized and called, by a very large majority vote, for the use of the fund to help victims. today's vote, which releases 35.6 million for these departments and 31.2 million for portugal, which was hit by floods in madeira as a result of the storm, reflects this common desire to show genuine solidarity between european citizens. this is the europe we want to develop, a europe close to the citizens, listening to their problems and able to respond to them collectively.

in writing. whether in haiti during the earthquake in january, or in pakistan with the floods this summer, during disasters, europe does a lot but in a dispersed order. each member state sends its own personnel, its own sniffer dogs, its own aircraft, etc. however, the sum of individual responses organised in an emergency will never be equivalent to a planned and organised european response. the european union, together with the 27 member states, is the world's largest donor of humanitarian and development aid. we have a wide range of civilian and military instruments to meet emergency and reconstruction needs. but as long as national reflexes persist, we will unfortunately not be able to derive any practical benefit from this virtual status of collective strength. what we need is a real 'rapid response capacity'. and improving efficiency and speed in emergencies requires strong political will on the part of the various parties involved.
in writing. work is continuing on financial regulation. i voted in favour of this own-initiative report by the european parliament which aims to subject all financial products to the control of the market authorities. the lack of transparency undermines the efficiency of markets and has contributed to the deepening of the financial crisis. the 'market in financial instruments' directive facilitated the transfer of market activities to more regulated and transparent trading spaces. in line with the conclusions of the g20 in pittsburgh on 20 september 2009, the objective of this report is to ensure that 'all standardised otc derivative contracts are traded on exchanges or via electronic trading platforms'.
in writing. it is clear that there is a need to guard against the misuse of chemical, biological, radiological and nuclear products, materials and organisms. but it is mainly the everyday use of these that must be guarded against. the text never expresses a view on the necessary abandonment of nuclear power. this is a serious threat to our fellow citizens at the moment. as for the terrorism at the heart of this report, why call on the largest threat to peace in the world, nato, to deal with it? so many inconsistencies that i cannot vote for this text.
in writing. regional policy is one of the most important policies of the union for me. the funds it distributes throughout europe contribute to cohesion between the different regions and promote their competitiveness. however, there are areas where improvements can be made, particularly in the area of multilevel governance, i.e. coordinated action by the union, the member states, regional and local authorities. regional policy suffers from the complexity of its procedures, which often discourage local actors from using it. however, these do not prevent a still too high level of irregularities. i voted in favour of this initiative by the european parliament which stresses the essential role of local authorities in the implementation of regional policy, but at the same time calls for improved multi-level governance. it also called for better monitoring by the commission, both in supporting regional actors and in monitoring the proper use of funds.
in writing. i voted in favour of the own-initiative report by my romanian colleague ramona nicole mănescu on good governance in the field of eu regional policy, in particular as regards the procedures for assistance and control by the commission. i welcome the request for simplification, as this is the condition for a better understanding and use of european funds by local officials. like the vast majority of my colleagues, i am in favour of a strong cohesion policy with financial resources remaining after 2013 while rejecting any attempt at renationalisation. i would add, in my own personal capacity, that the best way to prevent cohesion policy from being renationalised is to make it european. i regret that too often the funds from cohesion policy are used for projects of a regional, sometimes national and rarely european dimension.
in writing. the report by mrs mănescu aims to bring the european union closer to its citizens: it calls for better commission control over the inclusion of local authorities in the development of cohesion policy. this document is part of a plan to simplify very complex administrative procedures in favour of the development of our regions and of increased collaboration between local authorities in the various member states. its adoption by a large majority confirms the importance attached to improving the use of european funds.
in writing. this text is a testament to the establishment of the european macroregions. in order to better impose these competitiveness poles in the interests of the sacred single market, this house proposes that they be headed by the european commission to the detriment of elected governments. the eu's regional policy should focus on reducing the inequalities in income and living conditions of the citizens who inhabit europe's regions. we're not even close.
in writing. council regulation (ec) no 377/2004 of 19 february 2004 established a network of immigration liaison officers. these officers are representatives of the member states seconded to a third country and are responsible for facilitating the european union's (eu) action in the fight against illegal immigration, in particular by collecting information for the european agency frontex. but coordination in this young policy can be improved. meetings between those liaison officers, commission representatives and the frontex agency should be possible. in addition, better cooperation with other bodies such as the european asylum support office and the united nations high commissioner for refugees should be encouraged. it has therefore become necessary to amend regulation (ec) no 377/2004. i have supported this text which, while recalling the requirements that fundamental rights impose on this policy, provides the management of the union's external borders with the means to carry out effective controls.
in writing. as a fictitious rapporteur on this dossier, i supported the report by mr diaz de mera, which went beyond the technical amendments proposed by the commission, in particular by better understanding the complexity and opacity of the work of the immigration liaison officers (oli). in a context of mixed migration flows, it is essential to include in their activities a more human rights-sensitive and respectful approach. the tasks carried out by the oils must also be made more transparent and subject to greater democratic supervision; this is done by strengthening the exchange of information between the european parliament and organisations such as the united nations refugee agency (unhcr) and the european asylum support office (easo). in view of the council's objections, the compromise finally reached to settle the terminological controversy (illegal immigration versus irregular immigration) seems satisfactory, but it can only be a first step; the european institutions will have to make their commitment a reality.
in writing. the exchange of best practice between police services in different countries is sometimes necessary and its objectives are praiseworthy. it should be remembered, however, that international police cooperation already existed in the 19th century, long before the construction of europe. this report proposes that we, in the framework of frontex (the european external borders agency of the member states), improve the exchange of information on illegal migration flows, illegal immigration and the return of irregularly staying persons, including the establishment of networks of immigration liaison officers. this new initiative, which is desired by the majority of europe's citizens, could be welcomed if the objectives were really to curb immigration dramatically. the reality is quite different, and the fruit of the work of this agency, as well as the measures taken at the level of the governments of the nations, is a failure. france and europe are overwhelmed by immigration. according to an "official" figure from the european union, nearly 900 000 illegal immigrants enter europe each year. while illegal immigrants are not sent back to their country of origin, nor even criminal aliens, one is entitled to wonder how these various measures could reverse migration flows without real political courage following the facts.
in writing. we were due to vote on wednesday on my colleague véronique mathieu's draft directive to create a 'single permit' for residence and work for migrant workers. i voted for this text. unfortunately, he was not adopted. this text allowed the alignment of the arrangements applicable to foreign workers and thus fought against social dumping. by better regulating legal immigration, it enabled the union to combat undeclared work and illegal channels. the socialists opposed this directive on the grounds that it excluded certain categories from its scope. the liberal group, on the other hand, took a very unpredictable stance and rejected the text. having seen one of their positions on an amendment rejected, they voted against the whole text without giving any advance notice of the importance they attached to this point. that's how you waste a year's worth of work.
in writing. let us remember that the european parliament is not subject to the council! now even on immigration, member states must take meps seriously! co-decision is a reality! the proposal for a directive on the single permit for third country nationals was rejected in plenary - a strong gesture by parliament because the issue was crucial! the creation of a single permit for third-country nationals wishing to reside and work in a member state has been discussed for years! it was a laudable initiative at the outset but today's epp amendments deny the very essence of a single permit - they are also against equal treatment for all and create different categories of workers, which is simply unacceptable! we cannot compromise on equal treatment! in response to these epp amendments, we therefore voted by a majority against the final proposal: by 350 votes to 306, the proposal is rejected and must be referred back to the european commission. we must do better: yes to a responsible common immigration policy but no to a policy which is restrictive and discriminatory!
in writing. the creation of a single permit for third-country nationals wishing to reside and work in a member state has been discussed for years. this is a commendable initiative whose initial objective is to simplify the administrative requirements for third country nationals by allowing them to obtain a work and a residence permit in a single procedure at a 'one-stop shop'. the original legislative proposal provided that third-country workers should enjoy the same treatment as nationals in terms of employment-related rights (such as access to social security, education and training). but according to the text as amended by its rapporteur, member states would have been allowed to restrict some of these rights. this is contrary to equal treatment and is unacceptable. we therefore voted in the majority against the final proposal, which was rejected. the construction of a humane and reasonable immigration policy is a key societal challenge for the coming years, but it can only be met at european level to avoid electoral motives and national reflexes.
in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, at a time when europe has almost 25 million officially unemployed, a directive to facilitate labour immigration is being put back on the table! there's something indecent about that! the text also proposed to guarantee certain economic and social rights to these immigrant workers, allegedly to avoid social dumping or unfair competition with native workers or those already present in europe. a hollow admission that immigration is weighing down on european wages and does not offset any shortages of labour, but on the contrary competes directly with our workers. some amendments, which seek to strengthen equality of rights - and costs - between residents and immigrants, actually only proposed to allow access to our social benefits for all kinds of immigrants, whether working or not. a choice between social dumping and automatic social assistance which is no longer politically or financially sustainable. it is time to decide, at the level of our states, to reverse the migratory flows which have become an unbearable economic, social and even cultural burden and to practice national and community preference in all areas.
in writing. this report and the proposal for a directive it amends are a disgrace! they introduced the introduction of a selective immigration system based on the needs of the markets. they strip all immigrants of their rights if they can't serve those markets or no longer serve them. and even when they grant limited rights to those who work, they give the possibility of restricting them further down the line. immigrants are not second-class human beings! this directive is simply inhuman. i vote against and denounce it.
in writing. victims of violence can benefit from protection measures against their aggressor in their respective member states. however, this protection stops at the borders of their state and there has been no way to extend this protection beyond the borders. i voted in favour of this new directive, which allows the judicial authorities of a member state which has put in place protection measures under its national law to issue a 'european protection decision', which protects victims in the territory of the other member states of the union. the directive is of course primarily aimed at women who are victims of violence, but it could also concern anyone, regardless of gender or age, potential victims and their families.
in writing. the european protection order is the realisation of the priority given by the spanish presidency to combat violence against women. victims who benefit from a measure to remove an aggressor will be able to be protected across national borders, thus allowing them to start a new life wherever they want. the european protection order issued shall have the same legal force throughout the union. the scope of the text has been extended to include the protection of life, physical or psychological integrity, and dignity, personal freedom and sexual integrity. this broad definition allows the notions of forced marriage, paedophilia, human trafficking, sexual mutilation, etc. to be included. this measure meets the primary objective of the area of freedom, security and justice, namely to build a protective europe. i therefore voted in favour of this text.
in writing. human trafficking is an abomination which the european union cannot unfortunately ignore. whatever the reasons, sexual or labour exploitation, it is inadmissible by the union authorities. this is why europe has for some time now been equipping itself with a wide range of legislation to combat this phenomenon. this new directive, which i voted for, replaces the old framework decision, by virtue of the new powers in this area. by bringing together the community acquis in this field and concentrating it in a single text, this directive is to become a major instrument in the fight against trafficking in human beings. it lays down the principles on which the legislation of the member states must be based, provides for the applicable sanctions, establishes the liability of legal persons, protects victims from any prosecution which their status might have occasioned, sets up measures to assist and protect victims and contains certain specific provisions for women and children.
in writing. human trafficking affects several hundred people every day in europe. mostly women and little girls. it was therefore urgent to fill the legal vacuum in some european countries, such as spain, where the largest brothel has just opened a few kilometres from the french border. the european union has therefore finally acquired an instrument to create a deterrent environment for traffickers and to provide assistance and protection for victims of trafficking. common rules now define the offences and penalties applicable to traffickers. this is a further step towards protecting human dignity and reducing the commodification of human beings.
in writing. we adopted a report last week on the proposal for a directive on preventing and combating trafficking in human beings and protecting victims, and i welcome this vote. first, the definition of 'trafficking in human beings' will now be understood much more broadly, including trafficking in the sex industry, exploitation at work, especially in agriculture or domestic services, exploitation for begging purposes... secondly, our text sets out sanctions, minimum sentences for traffickers. thirdly, our text provides for a whole range of measures to help and assist the victims, not to mention the hundreds of thousands of people in the european union every year. time has shown that the existing framework is not sufficiently effective. the text we adopted last week shows a willingness to step up our action to protect citizens and prosecute traffickers throughout europe.
in writing. human trafficking is a form of modern slavery. it is also a highly lucrative business for criminal organisations, which can take many forms, including sexual exploitation, forced labour, human organ trafficking, begging, illegal adoption and domestic work. this is the first binding european legislation on the subject. the text strengthens the protection of victims and sanctions against perpetrators. the gender approach underpinning the text is welcome, as it is often women who are victims of human trafficking. it should also be noted that victims will not be prosecuted for crimes committed as a result of trafficking, such as cases of violation of immigration laws. i have supported this text.
in writing. facilitating the issuing of visas for georgian citizens and approving an agreement on the readmission of irregular immigrants: both issues were voted on in the european parliament's plenary session on tuesday 14 december. my colleague n. griesbeck was the rapporteur on these two agreements on the movement of persons between the union and georgia. the objectives of this agreement with georgia are to reduce the time taken to obtain a visa, simplify the documents required and even exempt certain categories of persons such as students, journalists and pensioners from the visa requirement. in parallel, we also voted in favour of the readmission agreement, which provides that the eu and georgia mutually undertake to readmit their nationals who are staying illegally. these two agreements mark the willingness of the eu and georgia to cooperate in the fields of freedom, justice and security.
in writing. i voted in favour of the very good own-initiative report by my excellent romanian colleague, petru constantin luhan, on the achievement of territorial, social and economic cohesion in the european union. i fully agree with the statement in the report that achieving economic, social and territorial cohesion is a necessary but not sufficient condition for ensuring global economic competitiveness, which requires significant investment in key areas such as energy, the environment, infrastructure, education, research and development, creative industries and services, logistics and transport. this is the sum of the grand investment plan of one trillion euros which i have been calling for since the beginning of this mandate and which is the necessary condition for the development, through competitiveness, of our continent and for equal opportunities for european citizens wherever they are in the territory of the union.
in writing. while territorial disparities between the different regions of the european union are tending to widen, one of the best tools for meeting the ambitious objectives of the 2020 strategy is a smarter european cohesion policy, with a strong focus on innovation, research and development, taking into account regional specificities. the report by mr luhan goes in this direction and establishes european cohesion policy as one of the key elements of the economic vitality of our regions. it brings us closer to a more 'sustainable' european economy.
in writing. this report is concerned primarily with regional competitiveness, european competition and high productivity. it is a key element of the europe 2020 strategy. the only relevant reference in the report, namely 'quality public services for all citizens, wherever they live and work', is therefore rendered meaningless. i am voting against this text.

the rapporteur. - mr president, mr minister, mr commissioner, we are now in the third act of the financial legislation for 2010. after the supervision, after the directive on alternative fund managers, we are now dealing once again with the rating agencies. once again, because europe has not been late in bringing in a regulation in this area which was designed in 2009 and which is now coming into effect. credit rating agencies generally issue opinions on the creditworthiness of companies, governments and complex financial products in the form of literal ratings. the rating reflects the assessment of the risk that issuers of financial instruments may not be able to meet their debts. these agencies have gradually become a major force in the financial world for a number of reasons. first, the notes are taken into account in the banking regulations for the determination of the amount of capital to be set aside for investments. secondly, because the rating contributes to the success of the issues since these ratings have become a major indicator for investors. the credit rating agencies, though not the main cause, played a harmful role in the recent financial crisis. indeed, they underestimated the probability of default of the issuers of certain complex financial instruments. in 2009, the european commission proposed a framework for the supervision and regulation of credit rating agencies in order to restore confidence in the markets and to strengthen investor protection. in the same year, regulation 1060/2009 on credit rating agencies was adopted. in the debate in the european parliament before the adoption of this regulation, the rapporteur had stressed the need for integrated supervision of credit rating agencies and common control of their products at eu level. at that time, such european supervision was not legally possible. however, the commission had undertaken to make a legislative proposal to that effect and you, commissioner, have kept that promise. the agreement between the council and the european parliament on the architecture of european supervision, which will enter into force on 1 january 2011, has now made it possible to effectively implement such european supervision of credit rating agencies. the regulation establishing the european securities and markets authority expressly provides that the authority shall exercise specific supervisory powers over credit rating agencies. that was the subject of the supplementary and amending regulation on which we reached agreement and which will be voted on tomorrow. i had wished, and my colleagues followed this request, that the other issues relating to rating agencies, sovereign debt allocation, remuneration scheme, competition, be deferred in a reflection which will take the form of an own-initiative report which will precede the legislative proposal that you will make in the first half of 2011 and for which you have launched a consultation. i believe that by this european supervision of credit rating agencies we are taking a big step in the same direction as the supervision that has been put in place. i should like to thank the belgian presidency for its tireless efforts on the financial issues, the commissioner, you and your teams and, of course, my colleagues in the european parliament who have taken part in this debate and have supported our positions.
the rapporteur. - mr president, mr minister, mr commissioner, after what you have heard, you can draw two conclusions. the first is that parliament will give its massive support to this text tomorrow, which will show once again that parliament, by its large majority, appreciates the regulatory and supervisory action undertaken by the commission and to which the belgian presidency has given its strong support. the second conclusion is that i am not drawing a conclusion today, but that a new debate will be opened, starting with the consultation of the wolf klinz own-initiative report, to examine all these difficult questions. so, we must not hide it, in 2009, when we made the first regulation, these questions were already asked. and the reason we haven't addressed these questions is because we haven't found a relevant answer. so i hope that, thanks to the reflection that has begun with the presentation of the wolf klinz report, the discussion that will begin around the consultation will make it possible to provide answers this time to complete the regulation of rating agencies. but if you will allow me, i will end by quoting the chairman of the financial markets authority who says that, all the same, the right thing would be for the financial markets to detoxify themselves from the rating agencies to allow investors a greater personal appreciation of situations and risks. i think that would also be a guarantee.
acting president of the council. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i am very pleased to be here in the european parliament again today, after the debate we had before cancún and now after the outcome of the climate conference. i am also pleased to see here some familiar faces who were also present as delegation in cancún and who, on behalf of the european parliament, made a very useful and active contribution to the success of the conference. i think that this is something that should be emphasized and underlined. the cancún climate conference has finally turned out to be a success. until the last day, we were waiting for a result, but in the end the result was positive. this was necessary both for climate policy and to save the multilateral process. we have reached a decision at the climate conference, a decision which actually consists of two parts, a first part which you could consider as a set of concrete measures that can be implemented very quickly, and a second part which lays down a set of foundations for reaching a global agreement in the long term for the period after 2012. this is of course in the context of the two degrees celsius target which is also included in the outcome of the climate conference as a starting point. when i speak of immediate implementation or of a number of actions which can be put into effect immediately, i am talking about adaptation, technology, the fight against deforestation and financing. and i might mention a few things very briefly. first and foremost, the adaptation. a framework has been adopted and a committee is also being set up. this will help to provide support to the most vulnerable areas. second, the technology. support will be provided for both mitigation and adaptation. two new structures are being set up. the executive technology committee and the climate technology centre and network. the aim is to promote knowledge through research, dissemination and transfer of technology. thirdly, the fight against deforestation. national strategies and action plans of developing countries will form the basis for financing actions to combat deforestation. finally , the green climate fund is to ensure that $100 billion is made available to developing countries by 2020. these are the concrete achievements of cancún. so if we look at the longer term and the foundations that have been laid, we will obviously have to continue working next year on the establishment of an international agreement after 2012. the mitigation measures of both developed and developing countries are now incorporated and anchored in the text, which is very important, as the results of copenhagen are now officially incorporated in it. it also provides for greater transparency. the longer-term legal form beyond 2012 is to be defined next year. that's going to be a whole discussion; we are moving towards a second commitment period under the kyoto protocol and what are the greenland and the united states doing? so this is not the end, but the beginning, an important new step in the climate debate. i think that all of us together, the european parliament, the council and the commission, will have to continue to work hard to ensure that we get a next important step next year and hopefully also a binding international agreement. i would like to thank parliament again for the efforts it has made in cancún.

text. on all three points we made progress. for the first time, the 2°c objective is acknowledged in a un document, the pledges are anchored and the obvious has been stated, namely that countries need to do more for the world to stay below the 2°c rise. we also started a process to strengthen transparency and, as we said in cancún, it is not enough just to say that you are in favour of increased transparency. what does that mean? it is very important that the text now contains several pages spelling out exactly what the political guidance for mrv and ica would be. that is very important and i the rapporteur. - madam president, today the european union is opening up to participatory democracy. it is not yet direct democracy, citizens will not decide for themselves, but they are gaining the right to directly, publicly, massively, challenge those who make decisions in europe, above the heads of their governments and their elected representatives. the citizens now have the same right of political initiative as the council of ministers and the european parliament have here. we have benefited, as zita gurmai said, from the excellent preparatory work carried out by commissioner šefčovič and his teams and from the intelligent and effective cooperation of the belgian presidency. on the part of parliament, this text is the result of the work of four rapporteurs, a gang of four, including you, madam president. your presence has been an honor. we wanted to design the procedure as simple as possible for the citizens, as citizen friendly as possible. who can participate? citizens, that is to say natural persons, all citizens, including, why not, elected representatives, but only european citizens, the treaty leaving no doubt on this subject. the right to participate in the citizens' initiative is an additional privilege enjoyed by citizens in europe. who can take the initiative? it will take seven citizens in an organising committee, not 300,000 as proposed by the commission, not 100,000 as envisaged by the council, but seven citizens from seven different countries, i.e. a quarter of the member states. who should you contact if you want to start an initiative? the commission itself will publish a guide to the citizens' initiative and set up a specialised contact point. what procedure? the simplest one! one application to register the initiative and to have its admissibility assessed. what is the eligibility criteria? the treaty, the whole treaty, nothing but the treaty, including the charter of fundamental rights. how can an initiative be supported? it is not a question of the political, financial, local, national, european, international support, lobbying, ngos, churches, etc. the only condition is full transparency. those invited to sign must know who is behind the initiative. it is up to them, the citizens, to take responsibility. what are the formalities for collecting signatures? the simplest ones! signatures on paper and online. of course, the control can only be exercised by the member states, but we have ensured, as mrs gurmai said, that the forms are as harmonized as possible. in the end, a genuine single european regime will have to be established in the 27 countries, a third of the states are already ready for it. finally, what will be the political consequences? this is a subject on which parliament has placed great emphasis. in accordance with the treaty, the commission will be the sole judge of whether or not to give legislative follow-up to a successful initiative. the commission must then be protected against political pressure to multiply legislation when the union is already over-regulating. but at the same time, we must protect citizens from the risk of no policy follow-up in cases where the commission considers that additional legislation is inappropriate. this is why two new rights have been created for the authors of successful initiatives: the right to be received by the commission to present their motions and the right to a public debate, which may take place in front of the european parliament itself. in short, this is a simple, innovative and democratic procedure. the citizens have the floor. in writing. the budgetary practice of the european union is based on a number of principles, including that of specialisation. this means that an amount allocated to a policy can only be used within the policy. this principle, together with others, ensures sound financial management in the union. but it also results in a certain budgetary rigidity. the annual budget, or even more so the multiannual financial framework, cannot cover all the expenditure facing the union. for this reason, a 'flexibility instrument' has been introduced in recent years. it consists of a financial reserve, the amount of which is entered in the budget each year, and which makes it possible to finance policies or projects whose cost could not have been anticipated. the report by my colleague reimer böge calls for the use of this instrument to finance the lifelong learning programme, the competitiveness and innovation programme and aid to palestine. as i believe that the union can do something useful in these three areas, i voted for this text without hesitation.
in writing. it is unacceptable that the financing of aid to the palestinian people, european education and training programmes and programmes to promote competitiveness and free competition should be grouped together in a single text. the malicious intent is obvious. this mix of genres is forcing me to abstain. i reiterate my full support for the cause of the palestinian people.
in writing. the preparation of the 2011 annual budget has once again given rise to genuine political negotiation between meps and member state governments. in this context of budgetary constraints, the council of the european union, which represents the governments of the member states, has wished to involve the union in the efforts of rigour to which the european countries are striving. although the european parliament (and the commission) wanted the crisis to be tackled by voluntary policies, it aligned itself with the council's position, showing its solidarity with the member states. in return for this concession, parliament wanted a debate to be opened on the union's resources, and in particular the question of whether it could have its own funding, independent of the member states' contributions. the council, which was initially intransigent, has finally given in to our legitimate demands. that is why the other members and i were able to agree to this budget, which is limited in its short-term ambition but which opens up prospects for the future of the union's policies.
in writing. the european union must have a budget that is commensurate with its ambitions. it must not be carried away by the crisis but must rise to the challenges that lie ahead. with the lisbon treaty, parliament now plays an equal role with the council and has established itself as a force for proposals. i voted in favour of the 2011 budget because it is our responsibility as meps to give europe clear political direction. europe will maintain its priorities in 2011. it will be able to revise its financial needs upwards in order to put its new skills into action. despite the difficult economic situation, parliament succeeded in obtaining a firm commitment from the member states. on a proposal from parliament, the commission will in 2011 start to reflect on the different types of own resources needed for europe to ensure its financial autonomy in the future. i regret, however, that parliament has not reached a consensus on the additional funding that the iter project will need from 2012 onwards. a flagship project of international research and european scientific dynamism, the experimental thermonuclear reactor could have benefited from an unused surplus part of the 2011 budget.

in writing. when it comes to making the european marriage rules more coherent, an agreement among 27 is difficult to achieve. fortunately, since the amsterdam treaty of 1997, member states who wish to do so can join forces to make progress in a specific area, in 'enhanced cooperation', in order to form a core of driving states that can propel the union forward. the difficulties faced by spouses in obtaining recognition of their status throughout europe, particularly in the event of divorce or legal separation, have led some states to join forces to improve the coordination of national regulations. i have insisted that this enhanced cooperation, in which france wishes to participate, be implemented. in my view, this initiative is a step towards bringing europeans closer together in an area which concerns us all and in which legal certainty is paramount. i therefore voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation implementing this enhanced cooperation. in future, such enhanced cooperation should be used as often as necessary.

in writing. in principle, credit rating agencies issue independent opinions on the credit quality of an entity, debt, financial bond or financial instrument. however, the opinions of these agencies can sometimes have serious consequences for the economy of the countries whose financial regularity they note. in 2009, the eu adopted regulation 1060/2009 which aims to regulate the activities of agencies in order to protect investors and european financial markets from the risk of bad practices. it lays down the conditions for issuing credit ratings and the rules for the registration and supervision of credit rating agencies. at the same time, a report by an expert group concluded that the supervisory framework needed to be strengthened in order to reduce the risk and severity of future financial crises. the 'esma' regulation has established the european securities and markets authority. in order to ensure the proper functioning of this authority and its proper integration into the general framework of financial regulation, it has become necessary to amend regulation no 1060/2009. i voted for this report which improves the control of rating agencies.

in writing. metrology is the science of measurement. since antiquity, europeans have successively adopted kyrielles as measuring systems in all areas (length, volume, alcoholometry, etc.). the adoption of the metric system, for example, has enabled better collaboration between the various economic agents on the continent and then in the world. however, in many areas disparate measurements and measurement systems remain. the union has long pursued a policy of harmonising measurement systems in order to remove these barriers to cooperation between europeans. directive 2004/22 was an important step in this movement. as we prepare to revise this legislation, a number of instruments which are now obsolete and which should be eliminated in order to improve readability are emerging. i have supported this text, which brings a welcome change to the metrology legislation.
in writing. the citizens' initiative, promised by the lisbon treaty, is finally being implemented. this new form of participation in eu policy-making allows european citizens to call directly on the commission to submit a proposal on issues of interest to them and falling within the eu's fields of competence. all that was needed was a procedural regulation to make this new right of european citizens a reality. it is now done, with my support in the vote. a citizens' committee composed of people from at least seven different member states may register an initiative with the commission. after that, signatures can be collected, either on paper or online. the million signatures needed will have to come from at least a quarter of the eu member states and be collected in less than 12 months. member states shall verify the validity of the statements of support. all signatories will have to be citizens of the european union and of voting age in european elections. finally, the commission, as guardian of the treaties, will remain the ultimate judge of whether to initiate the suggested legislative procedure.
in writing. a compromise was reached on the rules governing the citizens' initiative and the report was adopted by a very large majority: 628 votes in favour, only 15 against and 24 abstentions. i welcome this vote which opens up the possibility for european citizens to make their voices heard more strongly from 2012. the idea is simple, it is a kind of european-wide petition: a citizens' committee from at least 7 member states will have 1 year to collect 1 million signatures on a subject of public interest that requires the attention of the commission. the commission will then have to decide within three months whether it considers a legislative proposal on the subject to be appropriate or not, and it will have to justify its decision. we can regret certain conditions obtained by the member states, such as the need to be a european citizen and not just a national to be able to sign the petition or the possibility for the states to ask for identity cards to check signatures. nevertheless, the citizens' initiative is still a good idea, a blueprint for participatory democracy that we must now make a reality!
in writing. by adopting the basic rules of the 'citizens' initiative' introduced by the treaty of lisbon, a further step towards european direct democracy is taken. in the future, the commission will have to consider drafting a new european law if the request comes from one million citizens from at least one quarter of all member states. this new instrument thus gives european citizens the opportunity to have a real say in the legislative process by bringing a demand or concern that is based on popular will to the european level. this is a victory for our movement, which has been calling for a rapprochement between the european union and its citizens by building a more concrete, more transparent and more accessible europe.

in writing. the european citizens' initiative is one of the most interesting new features of the lisbon treaty. this is a european petition which will enable one million european citizens, from a representative number of eu member states, to put a subject on the commission's agenda. in other words, it is the emergence of a real legislative power for the european citizens, because the commission will be obliged to respond to this citizens' initiative by commissioning a study or proposing a directive. in a context where citizens still feel far too little belonging to the european union and where the figures for abstention in european elections are particularly worrying, this new tool will enable european citizens to become full-fledged actors in european democracy. that is why it is rather regrettable to hear voices today about the risks that the citizens' initiative would entail. the compromise reached with the council is perfectly balanced, and the terms of the project's admissibility mean that abusive initiatives will not be allowed to take place. we must not be afraid of the debate that citizens will have when they take this tool into their own hands. i voted for this text.

in writing. while the construction of europe was for a long time confined to working towards the completion of the internal market, the last ten years have seen an unprecedented emulation of european legislators. at the outset of the european community, there was an implicit division of labour between the council of europe, which was responsible for matters relating to individual freedoms, and the community, which was the embryo of a single market. but fairly quickly, the courts of the member states had to deal with cases challenging community law on the basis of human rights. that is why, after a long gestation, the charter of fundamental rights was adopted in 2000 and entered into force last year with the treaty of lisbon. the charter now provides the court of justice of the union with a single legal basis for protecting the fundamental rights of european citizens. yet we are only at the beginning of this new system. that is why i have supported this text, which reminds all european actors, member states and institutions, of their duties under the charter and of the need to develop a real culture and effective cooperation in the field of civil liberties.

in writing. the energy issue is a major challenge for europe. it is important to remember that the development of the continent owes much to the relatively easy supply of energy which european countries have enjoyed for more than a century. the energy question is now being asked in new terms. the use of fossil fuels is increasingly seen as an archaic idea. the dual pressures of global warming and the inevitably increasing difficulty of supplying oil and, to a lesser extent, gas, are pushing us to look for new solutions. since 2006, there has been an energy efficiency action plan. it tackles two aspects of efficiency. to achieve savings that make the union less dependent on its international partners, it must tackle both efficiency in production and efficiency in consumption. cheaper buildings, more efficient appliances and more optimal production technologies will combine competitiveness, innovation and economies of scale. i have of course supported this basic text (including the binding target of 20% additional energy efficiency by 2020), which puts the union at the forefront of these areas.

in writing. buildings are responsible for about 40% of energy consumption and about 36% of greenhouse gas emissions in the european union. efficient buildings should therefore be a priority in the next review of the energy efficiency action plan. today, 30% of existing housing in europe is unhealthy and has a high energy bill. it is therefore important not only to promote new sustainable construction but also to renovate sustainably. this is why member states must launch without delay a programme of major renovation of existing buildings in order to achieve by 2050 a near-zero energy consumption in the building environment. there is also a link between energy efficiency and energy poverty. we therefore ask the commission to develop a new energy efficiency action plan which takes into account the needs of vulnerable consumers.
in writing. there is much to be done to improve energy efficiency in key sectors such as transport or buildings which offer untapped opportunities. however, it is unrealistic to set a binding target of improving energy efficiency by at least 20% by 2020 as there is no common evaluation methodology or indicators. instead, we should focus on concrete sectoral targets, such as the commitment to reduce energy consumption in existing buildings by 38%. the lack of financing is a major obstacle to the renovation of buildings in the residential and sme sectors. instead of fighting for unrealistic goals, the european commission should instead identify innovative solutions and stimulate public-private partnerships in this area, because this creative ecology is a source of jobs.

madam president, our group is calling for the first word of the last sentence of paragraph 30 to be changed, and for 'welcome' to be replaced by 'notes'.
in writing. in 2007, several european states joined forces to create a european heritage label . the aim of this initiative is to strengthen the sense of european citizens of belonging to a common european identity and to foster their sense of belonging to a common cultural space , by selecting a number of outstanding sites across the continent. in 2008, the council of the european union sent the commission conclusions inviting it to submit a legislative proposal which, like the european capitals, would make this intergovernmental initiative a true label of the european union. following the council's instructions, the commission then launched an impact assessment and a public consultation. at the end of this consultation, the commission issued a proposal for a decision establishing a european union action for the european heritage label. i supported this text.
in writing. the youth in action programme aims to develop and support cooperation in the field of youth in the european union. it aims to encourage the participation of young people in public life, particularly the most disadvantaged and disabled, and their spirit of initiative, enterprise and creativity. the lifelong learning programme contributes to the development of the union as a knowledge society in line with the objectives of the lisbon strategy. supporting and complementing the action of the member states, it aims to promote exchanges, cooperation and mobility between education and training systems within the community, so that they become a world-class reference. switzerland, which is not part of the european union, does not participate in these actions. on the contrary, i believe that our swiss neighbours should be involved in these policies, with a view to an open union. that is why i voted in favour of this legislative resolution which includes switzerland in these important actions.
in writing. traditionally, the december plenary session is partly devoted to human rights. the formal highlights of the session included the presentation of the sakharov prize and the adoption of the resolution on parliament's annual report on human rights in the world and the union's policy on the matter. one of the union's international commitments is to promote democracy and fundamental rights throughout the world. this year's report notes that serious violations in this area persist and are aggravated by the economic crisis, climate change, new technologies and the fight against terrorism. it recommends that the objectives of the lisbon treaty be implemented, in particular through the new european external action service. the rapporteur, my colleague laima andrikienė, said: 'the priority of a coherent european foreign policy must be the promotion of democracy and human rights'.
in writing. the situation in afghanistan remains a matter of concern. almost a decade after the western coalition ousted the taliban from power, peace and prosperity are still far from the everyday lives of afghans. the strategy applied for years in the country is wrong and it must be changed. the union must state its position on the subject and acknowledge the failure of us military policy in the region. our troops are sinking, and no hope of escape seems possible under these conditions. for these reasons, i supported the parliament's resolution calling for a new strategy for afghanistan. the system we have had up to now must be changed. corruption and waste must be tackled if international aid is to play its part. it is through action in the civil sphere that peace will return. the coalition needs to be more stringent in controlling these funds. but we must stop interfering in afghan affairs. the afghan government must be free to find its modus vivendi with all components of afghan society. the road to development is still long, and we must not rush into these fragile balances.
in writing. this report paints a disastrous picture of the consequences of a war waged by nato with the complicity and support of the eu in afghanistan. it is regrettable that he has not denounced this war itself and is hesitating between keeping ottoman military forces in place and their necessary withdrawal. however, in view of all the important criticisms contained in the text, i shall abstain.
in writing. in the architecture of the european union, the role of the commission is similar to that of a government in a classical state. the commission has the legislative initiative but also the power to implement regulations, directives and decisions. the commission can therefore be regarded as the executive branch of the union. it has a derived power which enables it to adopt acts implementing acts adopted under the ordinary legislative procedure. just as regulations and circulars in france must respect the laws which frame them, the commission's implementing acts are not autonomous in relation to european laws. however, it is possible that, in the exercise of that entirely natural implementing power, the commission may be led, most often without necessarily seeking to do so, to exceed its prerogatives. in a democratic spirit, it is for the other institutions of the union to monitor the commission's activities, so that the distribution of powers is respected. that is why i voted in favour of this proposal for a regulation which lays down the general principles for the control of the commission's implementing powers by the member states.
in writing. the commission's proposal is a legitimate attack on democracy. this report merely amends it without ever denouncing it. the commission is the only group of civil servants in the world which is not controlled by its government (the council). i object to this new authoritarian drift.
in writing. on thursday 16 december, the heads of state and government agreed to continue the financial solidarity mechanisms that have been set up over the last few months to deal with the crisis. the aim is to ensure the stability of the euro as a whole in the event of difficulties for one or more euro-area member states. however, the granting of financial assistance will remain subject to strict conditionality, which i believe is necessary. like parliament's resolution, i welcome this commitment by the states, which is a sign of genuine european solidarity. the best response to the markets today is unfailing solidarity.
in writing. this report endorses the establishment of the european financial stability mechanism and the social bloodletting it entails. it wants it to be in line with imf standards and to ensure that national budgets are controlled by the european commission. i am voting against and denouncing this text.
in writing. for many years, côte d'ivoire has been the archetype of successful decolonisation. the country, which has been a good student of its newfound independence, experienced considerable development in the 1970s and 1980s. unfortunately, a latent political crisis is gradually undermining the ivorian state. the last presidential elections brought the opposition alassane ouattara to power. the incumbent president, laurent gbagbo, refused to step down. the country has since descended into an incredible confusion. two governments are vying for power, and serious incidents have claimed the lives of supporters on both sides. i voted for the european parliament resolution calling on mr gbagbo to respect the choice of the ballot box and to immediately make way for his legitimate successor. the text also supports the action of the african union which is currently putting pressure on the country to return to democratic order.
in writing. just over a decade ago, the european union adopted a directive to protect laying hens from the disastrous farming conditions in which too many farms kept them. the commission has also proposed that the member states should be allowed to apply the provisions of the directive to the processing of agricultural products. it was to be implemented by 2012. with two years to go, many farms are far from meeting the new standards. this parliament resolution calls on the commission to be firm on this issue. it welcomed the consultation of industry professionals initiated by the commission but urged it to refuse the additional time requested by some operators. it is already ten years since the directive was adopted.
in writing. from 1 january 2012, eggs laid by hens reared in battery-raised hens of less than 550 cm2 shall no longer be marketed. but many factory farms still fall short of standards. a risk of egg shortages and consumer price increases could arise if some member states are not prepared to comply with the ban. this would also lead to an increase in imports of eggs from third countries, which do not always comply with european health standards. that is why parliament is sounding the alarm. producers and member states are reminded to act as quickly as possible. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the rules are applied. producers who have invested in compliance and free range poultry farmers must be able to enjoy fair competition within the european union.
author. - mr president, malaysia is one of those countries for which cooperation with the european union, although recent and relatively modest, appears to be rather positive. this is particularly true in economic matters, of course, but also in social matters, such as education, women's rights and the rights of the most vulnerable. however, the situation is far from idyllic when it comes to democracy and human rights. there are some worrying signs. the situation we are discussing today is a sad illustration of this. while malaysia has signed a number of international conventions, including the universal declaration of human rights, acedaw and cide, it continues to refuse to sign others, including the international convention against torture. malaysia is one of the countries that imposes the death penalty, and it is even mandatory for drug trafficking convictions. corporal punishment is common and is applied to all: men, women - especially those accused of illicit sex - and even children, for schoolchildren guilty of serious disobedience. worse, for those sentenced to such sentences, these sentences are carried out with the help of doctors, in defiance of their medical ethics, the latter being responsible for resuscitating the condemned before they serve the full sentence. worse still, in recent years the malaysian parliament has expanded the list of criminal offenses that can be punished with the use of the cane. there are now more than 60 of them, including illegal entry. and since 2002, when this offence was created, thousands of refugees have been subjected to this punishment, this torture. the malaysian government must stop this practice. as the eu's dialogue with malaysia seems to be bearing fruit, should the eu not use all the persuasive means it can to push malaysia forward in this area?
author. - mr president, uganda is indeed one of those african states where homosexuality is still severely repressed. it is one of the most striking and most severe in this respect, since uganda, under the leadership of the fundamentalist evangelicals of the united states, with whom the ugandan head of state is a close associate, has embarked on a veritable crusade against homosexuals. countless numbers are persecuted and tortured for this reason alone. muslims and christians have come together - a first in this country - to denounce this abomination. seventy-year-old anglican bishop christopher senyonjo was denied his bishopric by his hierarchy for being one of the few who took a stand in favor of homosexuals. the bill already mentioned may indeed reappear at any time. it even punishes with death homosexuals suspected of being hiv positive or suspected of having sex with minors. he's calling for a report. the local tabloid rolling stone, which has nothing to do with the magazine of the same name, did publish lists with the names and addresses of gay leaders under a foul headline: "hang 'em!" the publication of this leaflet was temporarily banned, but the damage was done, as has already been pointed out. homosexuality in africa is very often experienced as a western evil, which causes africa to lose its ancestral values. in this country, ngos say there are 500,000 gays out of a population of 32 million. many people are applying for asylum in european countries. could we at least do everything possible to ensure that these requests are dealt with with special consideration, as should be the case for all those who are victims of oppression and torture?
